### 

Email Campaign Statistics in HighLevel helps you track email performance, measure recipient engagement, and understand how your campaigns contribute to conversions and revenue. Review important metrics such as email deliveries, opens, clicks, and orders to identify what resonates with your audience. With performance trends and detailed reporting, you can make informed decisions to improve your email marketing strategy.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Email Campaign Statistics?](#What-is-Email-Campaign-Statistics?)
- [Key Benefits of Email Campaign Statistics](#Key-Benefits-of-Email-Campaign-Statistics)
- [Conversion Summary](#Conversion-Summary)
- [Engagement Summary](#Engagement-Summary)
- [Performance Analysis](#Performance-Analysis)
- [How to Analyze Performance Trends](#How-to-Analyze-Performance-Trends)
- [Top Performing Emails](#Top-Performing-Emails)
- [Recent Email Analysis](#Recent-Email-Analysis)
- [How to Access and Use Email Campaign Statistics](#How-to-Access-and-Use-Email-Campaign-Statistics)
- [Access the Email Statistics Dashboard](#Access-the-Email-Statistics-Dashboard)
- [View Statistics for an Individual Email Campaign](#View-Statistics-for-an-Individual-Email-Campaign)
- [Export Email Campaign Statistics](#Export-Email-Campaign-Statistics)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Email Campaign Statistics?**

Email Campaign Statistics is a reporting feature in HighLevel that helps you measure the effectiveness of your email marketing efforts. It provides visibility into email activity, recipient engagement, and applicable conversion metrics so you can evaluate campaign results and identify opportunities for improvement.

The Email Statistics dashboard combines reporting from Email Campaigns, Workflow email actions, and Bulk Actions. You can view combined statistics or filter the dashboard to focus specifically on Email Campaigns. For a more detailed analysis of an individual campaign, you can also access its dedicated statistics page.

---

## **Key Benefits of Email Campaign Statistics**

Understanding how contacts interact with your emails helps you evaluate campaign effectiveness and make data-driven improvements. Email Campaign Statistics provides insights into audience engagement, delivery performance, and conversions so you can identify successful campaigns and optimize future emails.

- **Monitor Campaign Performance:** Track email delivery, opens, clicks, and other engagement metrics to understand how your campaigns perform.
- **Measure Recipient Engagement:** See how contacts interact with your emails and identify opportunities to improve content and calls to action.
- **Analyze Performance Trends:** Review reporting data over time to identify changes in engagement and evaluate campaign results.
- **Identify Top Performing Emails:** Discover emails generating stronger engagement and use those insights to improve future campaigns.
- **Track Conversions and Revenue:** Review eligible orders, attributed revenue, and conversion metrics to understand how email campaigns contribute to sales.
- **Compare Email Sources:** Filter statistics by Email Campaigns, Workflows, or Bulk Actions to evaluate different email activities.
- **Export Performance Data:** Download available reporting metrics in CSV format for additional analysis and sharing.

---

## **Conversion Summary**

Conversion Summary helps you understand how email interactions contribute to business outcomes, such as purchases and revenue. By reviewing attributed conversions alongside engagement metrics, you can evaluate which campaigns are generating measurable results beyond opens and clicks.

Depending on the reporting view and available conversion data, you may encounter the following metrics:

| Metric | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Orders / Conversions | The number of eligible purchases or conversions attributed to the email campaign. |
| Revenue | The total revenue attributed to the campaign. |
| Conversion / Order Rate | The percentage of recipients associated with attributed conversions, based on the applicable reporting calculation. |
| Average Order Value | The average value of attributed orders. |
| Revenue per Recipient (RPR) | The average attributed revenue generated per email recipient. |

HighLevel uses an email attribution window to determine which qualifying email interactions receive credit for eligible purchases. The default attribution window is five days, and it can be customized.

If a contact engages with multiple eligible campaigns, the most recent qualifying email interaction within the attribution window receives credit for the purchase.

```
Important: Attributed revenue is not the same as return on investment (ROI). ROI also requires cost or spend information. Conversion data may display as zero if no eligible purchases have been attributed to the campaign.
```

For detailed attribution settings, eligibility rules, and calculations, see [Understanding Email Conversion and Revenue Attribution](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001701-understanding-roi-conversion-metrics-for-tracking-email-campaigns).

---

## **Engagement Summary**

Engagement Summary provides a high-level view of how recipients interact with your emails. Comparing delivery, open, and click activity helps you understand whether campaigns are reaching recipients and generating meaningful engagement.

The available reporting views can include the following metrics:

| Metric | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Sent | The number of emails sent during the selected reporting period. |
| Delivered | The number or percentage of emails successfully delivered, according to available delivery events. |
| Opened | Email open activity recorded through supported tracking. |
| Clicked | Email link-click activity recorded through supported tracking. |
| Unsubscribed | Recipients who opted out of future email communications. |
| Bounced | Emails that could not be delivered, including temporary or permanent failures where reported. |

**Unique Opens and Clicks**

Unique engagement metrics help prevent repeated activity from the same recipient from being counted multiple times.

- **Unique Opens:** Counts a recipient once even if they open the same email multiple times.
- **Unique Clicks:** Counts a recipient once for applicable email click activity, regardless of repeated clicks.

Unique metrics are useful when evaluating the number of recipients who engaged, rather than the total number of interactions.

```
Note: Open and click tracking depend on the configured sending provider and tracking settings. Opens are tracking signals rather than guaranteed proof that an individual read an email.
```

---

## **Performance Analysis**

Performance Analysis helps you evaluate how email metrics change over time. Reviewing these trends makes it easier to recognize engagement patterns, compare reporting periods, and identify areas where campaign performance may need improvement.

Depending on the available reporting controls, you can analyze metrics such as:

- Sent and delivered email activity.
- Email opens.
- Email clicks.
- Unsubscribes.
- Other supported performance events.

### 

**How to Analyze Performance Trends**

1. Open the Email Statistics dashboard.
2. Select the reporting date range you want to review.
3. Use the source filter to select **Email Campaigns** if you want campaign-specific results.
4. Scroll to **Performance Analysis**.
5. Select the available metric you want to analyze.
6. Review the chart to identify increases, decreases, or recurring patterns.

For example, if email sends remain consistent while unique clicks decline, consider reviewing your email content, audience targeting, and calls to action.

---

## **Top Performing Emails**

Top Performing Emails helps you identify email content generating stronger recipient engagement. Comparing high-performing emails can reveal which subject lines, messaging approaches, and calls to action are more effective with your audience.

The current unified Email Statistics dashboard supports evaluating top-performing emails using engagement metrics such as open and click rates.

The reporting source determines how an email is represented:

| Email Source | Reporting Unit |
| --- | --- |
| Email Campaigns | Individual campaign email sends. |
| Workflow Campaigns | Individual email actions within a workflow. |
| Bulk Action Campaigns | Individual bulk email sends. |

When comparing campaigns, consider both engagement rates and the audience size. A campaign with a high open rate but relatively few recipients may require a different interpretation from a larger campaign with a slightly lower open rate.

```
Note: The earlier Email Campaign Statistics guide described a revenue-ranked top-five display. That legacy description should not be carried into the updated guide as the definition of the current unified Top Performing Emails report.
```

---

## **Recent Email Analysis**

Reviewing recently sent email campaigns helps you evaluate new activity without relying exclusively on historical trends. Comparing recent campaign results can reveal whether changes to email content, targeting, or sending strategies are producing the expected engagement.

The original Email Campaign Statistics experience included a Recent Email Analysis area that displayed the 10 most recently sent emails. In the current reporting experience, you can review individual sent campaigns through their campaign statistics pages.

To analyze a recent campaign, review its delivery and engagement metrics, conversion results where available, and recipient-level details.

For deeper reporting, see [Email Statistics – Summary Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006834).

---

## **How to Access and Use Email Campaign Statistics**

Accessing the correct reporting view ensures that you are evaluating the intended campaigns and reporting period. HighLevel provides a unified Email Statistics dashboard for comparing email activity and a separate campaign-level statistics view for reviewing an individual send.

**Access the Email Statistics Dashboard**

1. Navigate to **Marketing → Emails** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. Select the **Statistics** tab.
3. Open the email source dropdown near the top of the dashboard.
4. Select **Email Campaigns** to focus on marketing campaigns, or **All Campaigns** to review combined email activity.
5. Select the appropriate reporting date range.
6. Review **Engagement Summary** to understand overall email activity.
7. Scroll to **Performance Analysis** to examine performance trends.
8. Review **Top Performing Emails** to identify stronger-performing email sends.

```
Important: Separate Beta activation is no longer part of the documented setup process. Once Email Statistics is available in your sub-account, you can access it directly.
```

---

## **View Statistics for an Individual Email Campaign**

Individual campaign statistics provide a more detailed view of delivery results, recipient engagement, and conversions. This is particularly helpful when investigating a specific campaign rather than comparing multiple sends.

1. Navigate to **Marketing → Emails → Campaigns**.
2. Locate the sent campaign you want to review.
3. Click the **three-dot menu (⋮)** next to the campaign.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083197064/original/GrtHPzLbHfcSkyjBLu9-WpyqmSuMhuTYQg.png?1791894200)
4. Select **Statistics**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083197179/original/QEcny8lPQYOehuwuX0MeGIReH-VvJR4foA.png?1791894244)
5. In the statistics side panel, click **Load More Statistics**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083197272/original/m2EYgMD9dvPuOrqU2dLM1L6CjpZt5PVKPQ.png?1791894284)
6. Open the **Summary** tab to review the campaign's performance.
7. Use the **Details** section to review available recipient-level activity, such as delivered, opened, clicked, or unsubscribed.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083197353/original/TSxXHiern3PKY0l7zfI_gB-9_JQO2zOXAA.png?1791894326)

**Export Email Campaign Statistics**

Exporting email statistics lets you perform additional analysis or share campaign performance data outside HighLevel. Export files are provided in CSV format and can include email activity from the selected reporting source.

1. Navigate to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Select the reporting source and date range.
3. Click **Export**.
4. Enter the email address or addresses that should receive the export.
5. Click **Export** to submit the request.
6. Open the email containing the CSV download link.

Export download links are valid for 30 days after generation. For additional instructions, see [Exporting Email Campaign Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-campaign-data).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why are my email statistics not showing immediately after I send a campaign?**

Most email statistics update in near real time, but some engagement events may take a few minutes to appear. Confirm that your campaign was sent and that you have selected the correct reporting source and date range.

**Q: Why is my campaign showing opens but no clicks?**

Recipients may have opened the email without clicking any links. If you expect click activity, confirm that click tracking is enabled and that the links are supported by the tracking configuration.

**Q: Why are some delivery or bounce statistics missing?**

The available reporting events can vary depending on your configured email service provider. Some providers support open and click reporting without exposing the same delivery or bounce information as LC Email or Mailgun.

**Q: Why doesn't my attributed email revenue match all purchases made by my contacts?**

Revenue attribution only includes eligible purchases associated with qualifying email interactions within the configured attribution window. Purchases outside the attribution window or attribution scope may not be credited to the campaign.

**Q: Why does a workflow appear as multiple entries in Top Performing Emails?**

HighLevel evaluates individual Workflow email actions separately. This helps you identify which specific emails are performing well rather than combining an entire workflow into one result.

**Q: What does it mean if the dashboard displays sample data?**

Sample data consists of demonstration statistics that help you preview the reporting experience. If a sample-data notice appears, use **Clear Sample Data** before analyzing actual email performance.

**Q: Can I identify contacts who unsubscribed or reported my campaign as spam?**

Yes. Open the individual campaign's statistics and review the relevant recipient-level information in the Details area, where available.

**Q: Does exporting campaign statistics change any campaign or contact information?**

No. Exporting statistics is a reporting action. It does not modify email campaigns, workflows, contact records, or the recorded statistics.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005552-how-to-access-the-all-in-one-dashboard-for-email-marketing)
- [Email Statistics – Summary Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006834)
- [Understanding Email Conversion and Revenue Attribution](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001701-understanding-roi-conversion-metrics-for-tracking-email-campaigns)
- [Click Performance in Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006833-click-performance-in-email-statistics)
- [Exporting Email Campaign Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-campaign-data)
- [Troubleshooting Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208601)

title_en: Moving Phone Numbers across accounts (US and International)
source_md:
Phone Number Migration

Moving Phone Numbers Across Accounts (US and International)

Move phone numbers between LC Phone and Twilio, or between LC Phone sub-accounts in different agencies, using a Support-coordinated migration process.

Overview

Phone numbers can be moved between LC Phone and Twilio or between LC Phone sub-accounts that belong to different agencies. The exact information required depends on the migration direction and whether the number is US-based or international.

HighLevel Support coordinates these supported cross-account migrations end-to-end, so you do not need to open a separate Twilio Support ticket. Preparing the correct Account SID, Location ID, phone numbers, and any applicable regulatory information helps prevent delays.

This guide explains which migration path to use, what to prepare, how to submit the request, and what to verify after the numbers move.

Important

Do not manually delete, release, disable, or disconnect a phone number while a migration is in progress unless HighLevel Support specifically instructs you to do so. Wait until Support confirms the move is complete and you have tested the number in the destination environment.

# **What is Phone Number Migration Across Accounts?**

Phone number migration moves an existing phone number from one supported phone environment to another without requiring you to purchase a replacement number. HighLevel Support coordinates supported LC Phone → Twilio, Twilio → LC Phone, and LC Phone → LC Phone migrations when the LC Phone sub-accounts belong to different agencies.

This process is different from **porting**. Migration is used when moving supported LC Phone or Twilio-managed numbers across compatible accounts. If the number currently belongs to a non-Twilio external carrier, use the phone-number porting process instead.

## **Key Benefits of the Phone Number Migration Process**

A coordinated migration allows businesses to retain established phone numbers while changing the account or phone environment that manages them. Preparing the required information before submitting the request helps reduce delays and makes post-migration validation easier.

- **Keep Existing Numbers:** Move eligible phone numbers instead of replacing numbers customers already know.
- **Centralized Coordination:** HighLevel Support coordinates supported cross-account moves from request through cutover.
- **Clearer Migration Planning:** Required IDs and regulatory details can be prepared before the migration request is submitted.
- **Support for Multiple Numbers:** Multiple eligible numbers can be included in the same migration request.
- **Post-Migration Validation:** Calls, SMS, compliance, routing, and number assignments can be verified after cutover before normal traffic resumes.

## **Supported Migration Scenarios**

The correct migration path depends on the phone system currently holding the number and where the number needs to go. Use the table below to identify the correct process before collecting IDs or submitting a request.

| Migration | When to Use It | Process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **LC Phone → Twilio** | Move an LC Phone-managed number into the customer's own Twilio account. | HighLevel Support coordinates the migration. |
| **Twilio → LC Phone** | Move a number from the customer's Twilio account into an LC Phone sub-account. | HighLevel Support coordinates the migration. |
| **LC Phone → LC Phone, Different Agencies** | Move an LC Phone number between sub-accounts that belong to different HighLevel agencies. | HighLevel Support coordinates the inter-agency move. |
| **LC Phone → LC Phone, Same Agency** | Move a number between two LC Phone sub-accounts under the same agency. | Use the in-app **Move Numbers** tool instead of this cross-account process. |
| **External Carrier → HighLevel** | The number is held by a carrier outside the supported LC Phone/Twilio migration paths. | Use the phone-number porting process. |

**No separate Twilio ticket is required for the three cross-account scenarios covered by this article.** Submit the required migration information to HighLevel Support and the migration will be coordinated for you.

## **What You Need Before Migrating**

Gathering the correct identifiers before contacting Support prevents unnecessary back-and-forth. The information required changes depending on the migration direction, so confirm the source and destination before submitting your request.

| Scenario | Prepare |
| --- | --- |
| **LC Phone → Twilio** | Gaining Twilio Account SID, HighLevel Location ID for the affected LC Phone sub-account, phone number(s), and preferred cutover window. |
| **Twilio → LC Phone** | Losing Twilio Account SID, destination HighLevel Location ID, phone number(s), and preferred cutover window. |
| **LC Phone → LC Phone, Different Agencies** | Destination Location ID, phone number(s), preferred cutover window, and source Location ID when available. |
| **International Number** | Applicable Regulatory Bundle SID, Address SID, destination Location ID when applicable, phone number(s), country, number type, and preferred cutover window. |

Phone Number Format

Provide each phone number in **E.164 format** whenever possible. For example, a US number should be submitted as **+1XXXXXXXXXX**.

**Security:** Do not include your Twilio Auth Token, password, payment information, or other credentials in a standard migration ticket unless HighLevel Support specifically provides an approved method for submitting that information.

## **How to Set Up a Phone Number Migration Across Accounts**

The migration begins by identifying the source and destination, collecting the required account identifiers, and submitting one complete request to HighLevel Support. Providing all required details in the initial request gives the migration team the information needed to coordinate the cutover.

### **Step 1: Identify the Migration Direction**

Confirm whether the number is moving from LC Phone to Twilio, from Twilio to LC Phone, or between LC Phone sub-accounts in different agencies. This determines which Account SID or Location ID must be included.

### **Step 2: Find the Twilio Account SID When Required**

The Twilio Account SID identifies the Twilio account involved in a US LC Phone ↔ Twilio migration.

- **LC Phone → Twilio:** Provide the **gaining Twilio Account SID** for the destination Twilio account.
- **Twilio → LC Phone:** Provide the **losing Twilio Account SID** where the number currently resides.
- **LC Phone → LC Phone across different agencies:** A Twilio Account SID is generally not required for this LC-to-LC move.

In Twilio, open the **Account Dashboard** and locate **Account Info**. Copy the Account SID for the applicable account.

![Twilio Account Dashboard showing the Account SID under Account Info](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054160307/original/o5oSPy13Wa2SCDElTiah8rlKOI8s74LdwQ.jpeg?1758293602)

The Twilio Account SID is available from the Account Dashboard under Account Info. Only the Account SID is required for the standard migration request.

### **Step 3: Find the HighLevel Location ID**

The Location ID, also called the Sub-account ID, identifies the HighLevel sub-account involved in the migration. For Twilio → LC Phone and inter-agency LC Phone moves, the destination Location ID is especially important. For LC Phone → Twilio, include the Location ID of the affected LC Phone sub-account so Support can identify the source location.

1. Open the applicable HighLevel sub-account.
2. Go to **Settings → Business Profile**.
3. Locate and copy the **Location ID**.

![HighLevel Business Profile Settings showing the Location ID](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054160913/original/MuHzpQF5_gS-jMkoIU47bJNg2hvRs4tLqA.png?1758293832)

The Location ID is available in Settings → Business Profile for the applicable HighLevel sub-account.

### **Step 4: Submit the Migration Request to HighLevel Support**

Submit one HighLevel Support request containing all migration details. Support will coordinate the supported cross-account migration and notify you when the number is ready for validation.

Include in the Request

- Migration direction: LC Phone → Twilio, Twilio → LC Phone, or LC Phone → LC Phone across different agencies
- Phone number(s) in E.164 format
- Applicable Twilio Account SID for US LC Phone ↔ Twilio moves
- Applicable HighLevel Location ID(s)
- Regulatory Bundle SID and Address SID for applicable international numbers
- Country and number type for international numbers
- Your preferred cutover window

![HighLevel Support flow for submitting a migration request](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155045972735/original/ruMK9XOl0NIlCzM2UaF8MuauyxRqZpVpiw.gif?1746109415)

Contact HighLevel Support and provide the migration details in one request so the phone team can coordinate the move.

## **Moving International Phone Numbers**

International phone numbers can require country- and number-type-specific regulatory information before they can be moved. Preparing the correct Regulatory Bundle and Address information before submitting the migration request helps prevent the transfer from being blocked by compliance requirements.

Prepare the Following

- **Regulatory Bundle SID** applicable to the number's country and number type
- **Address SID**
- Destination Location ID when applicable
- Phone number(s), including country code
- Country and number type, such as local, mobile, or toll-free
- Preferred cutover window

### **Check Regulatory Approval Before the Move**

Regulatory requirements vary by country and number type. Confirm that any required Address or Regulatory Bundle is current and approved and that the submitted documentation matches the destination requirements.

[Learn how to create Regulatory Bundles and Addresses →](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001213216-regulatory-bundle-and-address-creation-for-sub-accounts)

## **What to Check After the Migration**

A successful number move does not guarantee that every routing, messaging, compliance, or user setting in the destination environment is already configured. Validate the number immediately after Support confirms the migration so issues can be identified before normal call or SMS traffic resumes.

1. **Confirm the number appears in the destination environment.**
2. **Place an inbound test call** from another phone.
3. **Place an outbound test call** from the migrated number.
4. **Test inbound and outbound SMS** when messaging is enabled.
5. **Review call routing, forwarding, voicemail, user assignments, and workflow references.**
6. **Review A2P 10DLC status.** A2P registration is associated with the account/sub-account environment and should not be assumed to transfer with the number. Complete or verify registration in the destination and attach applicable numbers to the approved campaign.
7. **Review Toll-Free Verification and country-specific compliance.** Confirm the migrated number meets the destination environment's current compliance requirements before relying on SMS.
8. **Keep the migration ticket open until validation is complete.**

**Historical recordings and voicemails:** Moving the phone number does not migrate historical recordings or voicemail assets into a new phone environment. Download any historical assets you need to retain before losing access to the source environment.

## **Troubleshooting Phone Number Migrations**

Migration delays are commonly caused by missing identifiers, regulatory requirements, incorrect destination information, or post-migration configuration. Start with the migration ticket and confirm that the source, destination, and phone numbers match the original request.

Support is asking for additional information

Confirm that the ticket includes the phone numbers, migration direction, applicable Twilio Account SID, HighLevel Location ID, and regulatory information for international numbers.

An international number is not moving

Verify that the applicable Regulatory Bundle and Address are approved for the correct country and number type. Country-specific requirements can delay the move until compliance information is complete.

The number moved, but SMS is not working

Review the destination's A2P 10DLC, Toll-Free Verification, SMS permissions, and other applicable compliance requirements. A phone-number move does not automatically guarantee messaging compliance in the destination account.

The number moved, but calls are routing incorrectly

Review the destination number's forwarding settings, voicemail, user assignments, call routing, and any workflows or automations that reference the number.

You are moving numbers inside the same agency

Do not use the cross-account process when both eligible LC Phone sub-accounts belong to the same agency. Use the in-app **Move Numbers** tool under Agency Settings → Phone Integration.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Do I need to open a separate Twilio Support ticket?

No. For the supported LC Phone → Twilio, Twilio → LC Phone, and LC Phone → LC Phone across different agencies scenarios covered here, submit the required information to HighLevel Support. HighLevel coordinates the migration end-to-end.

Q: How long does a cross-account migration take?

A typical migration can take approximately 1–2 business days after Support has all required information. International numbers or migrations requiring additional regulatory review can take longer. Support will confirm the applicable cutover window.

Q: Can I migrate multiple phone numbers in one request?

Yes. Include all applicable phone numbers in a single list and clearly identify the source and destination. For larger lists, organize the numbers so Support can validate each number during the migration.

Q: Does A2P 10DLC registration move with the phone number?

Do not assume it does. A2P status is associated with the account or sub-account environment rather than only the phone number. After migration, verify or complete A2P registration in the destination and confirm that applicable numbers are attached to an approved campaign before relying on A2P messaging.

Q: Do historical call recordings and voicemails migrate?

No. Historical recordings and voicemail assets do not move automatically with the phone number. Download any historical assets you need to retain before you lose access to the source phone environment.

Q: Should I disable or delete LC Phone before moving the number to Twilio?

Do not manually delete, release, or disable the number during the migration unless HighLevel Support instructs you to do so. Wait until the migration is confirmed and you have tested the number in the destination environment.

Q: What if both sub-accounts are in the same HighLevel agency?

Eligible same-agency LC Phone → LC Phone moves should use the built-in **Move Numbers** tool under Agency Settings → Phone Integration instead of the cross-account Support process described here.

Q: Is moving an LC Phone or Twilio number the same as porting?

No. The migration process covered here moves eligible LC Phone or Twilio numbers between supported account environments. If the number belongs to a different external carrier, use the phone-number porting process.

### **Related Articles**

[Moving Phone Numbers: Migration Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006369-moving-phone-numbers-migration-guide) [Moving Numbers Between Sub-Accounts (Same Agency)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001203968-moving-numbers-tool-across-sub-accounts) [Regulatory Bundle and Address Creation for Sub-Accounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001213216-regulatory-bundle-and-address-creation-for-sub-accounts) [Porting Options: US In-App vs International Manual Process](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001211919) [How to Migrate an Agency and Sub-Account to LC Phone](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001204027)

title_en: WhatsApp - Organize Templates Using Folders
source_md:
Group, filter, sort, and organize WhatsApp templates with nested folders, direct navigation, and the redesigned Highrise interface.Managing WhatsApp templates is easier with the redesigned Templates and Folders experience in HighLevel. The Highrise interface adds filtering, sorting, folder visibility, and direct navigation into nested directories. You can organize templates by campaign, department, or use case while moving folders and templates between levels. This guide covers the updated management features alongside existing folder and reporting tools.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are WhatsApp Template Folders?](#what-is)
- [Key Benefits of WhatsApp Template Management](#key-benefits)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#prerequisites)
- [How to Organize WhatsApp Templates Using Folders](#how-to-organize)
- [Navigate Templates and Folders Within a Directory](#folder-scoped)
- [Filter WhatsApp Templates](#filter-templates)
- [Sort WhatsApp Templates](#sort-templates)
- [Find a Template's Folder](#folder-location)
- [Delivered Message Count](#delivered-count)
- [Weekly Delivery Trends](#weekly-trends)
- [Flexible Folder Creation](#flexible-creation)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

## **What Are WhatsApp Template Folders?**

WhatsApp Template Folders let you create custom folders and subfolders for organizing WhatsApp message templates in your Sub-Account. You can group templates by use case, campaign, department, or another structure that fits your workflow.

The updated Highrise (Design System V2) interface improves the Templates and Folders screens. You can open folders directly, view their templates or subfolders, filter and sort template lists, and see where templates are stored. Templates and folders can also be moved between different directory levels.

---

## **Key Benefits of WhatsApp Template Management**

Folder management and the redesigned template list help teams organize, locate, and review WhatsApp templates more efficiently.

- **Improved Organization:** Group templates by campaign, department, or use case for quick access.
- **Custom Hierarchies:** Nest folders inside folders to organize templates across multiple levels.
- **Faster Template Management:** Add, move, or locate templates without scrolling through long lists.
- **On-the-Fly Folder Creation:** Create folders while organizing templates or moving items between folders.
- **Breadcrumb Navigation:** See your current folder path and return to parent folders.
- **Template Reporting:** Open individual template reports to review delivery and engagement information.
- **New Filters:** Narrow the template list by category, language, status, and date.
- **New Sorting Options:** Sort templates by name, language, category, status, or last edited.
- **Clear Folder Visibility:** Identify a template's directory using the Folder column.
- **Folder-Scoped Views:** Browse templates and subfolders within the selected directory.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Access WhatsApp template management from the Sub-Account containing your WhatsApp templates. Your available actions depend on the WhatsApp features and permissions assigned to your user.

- The Sub-Account must have access to its WhatsApp Templates area.
- Your user must have the applicable WhatsApp management permissions.
- Folder organization does not change a template's message content or Meta approval status.
- Filters and sorting change how templates are displayed, not their content or status.
- Inside a selected folder, the Templates and Folders tabs show items belonging to that directory.

---

## **How to Organize WhatsApp Templates Using Folders**

Start from the WhatsApp Templates area in your HighLevel Sub-Account. You can create folders, navigate directory levels, filter or sort templates, and move items as your template library grows.

### **1. Navigate to WhatsApp Template Settings**

Open the applicable HighLevel Sub-Account and go to **Settings**.

Click **WhatsApp**, then open the top-level **Templates** tab.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084671557/original/XxMlY-oWGcG5VuVwd3-4WZ4GTiyVo95eCA.png?1793508195)

Use the inner **Templates** and **Folders** tabs to switch between the template list and folder directory.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084671569/original/w76kETdognENl-ywF1IQ4TwBldbSfb5lTw.png?1793508226)

### **2. Create a New Folder**

From **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**, select the inner **Folders** tab. Click **Create folder**, enter a folder name, and click **Create** to save.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673478/original/cnMfUk5JdhMgmr4dcxgKvcjUVOa5sT-JCQ.png?1793514772)

### **3. Create Subfolders**

Go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates → Folders**. Click the name of an existing folder to open it. Click **Create folder**, enter a subfolder name, and select **Create**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673598/original/RE9FJrxa7mS3SwjbJTCm6pTGVnFN_3sOGQ.png?1793515459)

**Note:** You can create multiple levels of folders and subfolders to organize your templates.

### **4. Use Breadcrumb Navigation**

From **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates → Folders**, open the folder you want to browse. Use the breadcrumb trail above the folder contents to return to a parent directory or the home level.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673134/original/oqnmfAryLXBLBLqVc4o9eFjxe5PEawLYyQ.png?1793513317)

### 

### **Navigate Templates and Folders Within a Directory**

The Highrise update introduces folder-scoped navigation. When you open a directory, the Templates and Folders tabs display the content belonging to that selected folder.

1. From the Sub-Account, go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
2. Select the inner **Folders** tab.
3. Click the folder name to enter that directory.
4. Choose **Folders** to view the subfolders inside it.
5. Choose **Templates** to view templates inside the selected folder.
6. Use the breadcrumbs to return to a parent folder or the home directory.

**Folders tab:** Shows the subfolders belonging to the selected directory.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084671871/original/XApLN_XvRHAwfYeyn6ZzAddUTXh3moapQw.png?1793509695)

**Tip:** If the selected folder has no templates or subfolders, the corresponding tab displays an empty state. Return to a parent folder to continue browsing.

### **Filter WhatsApp Templates**

Filtering helps you narrow the template list using selected attributes. This is useful when managing templates in different languages, categories, or approval states.

1. Open the relevant HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
3. Select the inner **Templates** tab.
4. Click **+ Add filter**.
5. Select the filter field you want to use.
6. Choose the available criteria for that field to narrow the displayed list.

The filter menu contains:

- **Category:** Find templates by message category.
- **Language:** Find templates using a selected language.
- **Status:** Narrow the list by template status.
- **Date:** Access date-based filtering options.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673292/original/cyFGfxOsGfdhk-GOPEwyVaM0D8ICo1ks1g.png?1793513911)

**Note:** The current menu labels its date filter **Date**. The template table also provides a separate **Last edited** column.

### 

### **Sort WhatsApp Templates**

Sorting changes the order in which templates appear in the list. You can organize the view by template name, language, category, status, or last edited date.

1. Open the relevant HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
3. Open the inner **Templates** tab.
4. Click **Sort** above the template list.
5. Select the field you want to sort by.
6. Review the selected sort direction shown in the menu.

The available sorting fields include:

- Template name
- Language
- Category
- Status
- Last edited

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084672714/original/0vaUlR4RcYUoLEtoK-ojEiYlebGu19cwsg.png?1793512326)

**Folder sorting:** The inner **Folders** tab provides its own folder-name sort control. The current interface displays **Sort: Folder name (A → Z)**.

### **Find a Template's Folder**

The redesigned Templates list includes a **Folder** column. This helps you identify which directory contains a template without opening each folder individually.

1. Open the applicable HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
3. Open the inner **Templates** tab at the main level.
4. Locate the template in the list.
5. Check the **Folder** column to see its directory placement.

When a template is associated with a folder, its folder name appears in the column. A dash is shown when no folder placement is displayed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084672816/original/EIN3b28iPPRs-vccBSEMhhqLPPCh2uDXOA.png?1793512520)

### **5. Move a Template into a Folder**

Move templates between directories as your campaigns and organizational needs change.

1. From the Sub-Account, go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
2. Open the inner **Templates** tab.
3. Locate the template in the main list or inside its current folder.
4. Click the template's three-dot menu under **Actions**.
5. Select **Move to Folder**.
6. Choose the destination folder or subfolder.
7. Click **Move** to complete the action.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084672814/original/XU_TQR6g73NnKUkl5k90J1hH5PWtndAWzA.png?1793512486)

### **6. Move Folders into Other Folders or Parent Levels**

The redesigned folder-management experience supports moving folders into other folders and back toward parent levels.

1. From the Sub-Account, go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**.
2. Open the inner **Folders** tab.
3. Locate the folder you want to move.
4. Click the three-dot menu under **Actions**.
5. Choose **Move Folder**.
6. In the **Move to Folder** dialog, select the intended destination.
7. Click **Move** to confirm the change.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673037/original/VQhvLlkFOVl22M364cJn4alxtyJRLF4NRg.png?1793513111)

Select an available destination in the folder picker. You can also use its **New folder** option when you need to create another directory.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673027/original/_66k0cx2nlC-l6UVsJziMaIoygJohOB4og.png?1793513051)

**7. View Template Performance Metrics**

From the Sub-Account, go to **Settings → WhatsApp → Templates**. Locate the template you want to review, then click **View reports** under **Actions**.

The redesigned Templates table provides direct access to reports. The earlier table layout shown in the existing reporting image may look different from the current Highrise interface.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673277/original/qcloCqqQb47lrYQcltf3J_03f3HO-PI7oQ.png?1793513869)

The available template reports can include:

- Messages Sent
- Messages Delivered
- Messages Read
- Button Clicks

Use the available report date controls to review activity over a selected period.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084672181/original/0qOdHn_1i6dZ-3VwAiL8gjU3NHKGDC9Nrg.png?1793511027)

**Note:** Template analytics have availability and regional limitations. Review the dedicated WhatsApp Template-Level Analytics guide for current reporting requirements.

---

## **Delivered Message Count**

Delivered-message information helps you understand how frequently an individual WhatsApp template reaches its recipients. In the redesigned management interface, open the template's report using **View reports**.

- Review the number of messages delivered for a selected template.
- Compare delivery information with sent and read counts where available.
- Use supported reporting date controls to review a specific period.

---

## **Weekly Delivery Trends**

Reviewing delivery activity across different periods helps you identify changes in template usage. Open the template report and use the available date controls to examine delivery trends.

- Review message activity for the selected reporting period.
- Compare delivery and engagement metrics over time.
- Use available information to assess template performance.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084673429/original/G-a2PBYj0HStCyxLwF84iI16Ztj6s7sj5A.png?1793514570)

Reporting layouts may differ from the earlier template-table example. Use View reports in the current Templates screen to access the applicable metrics.

---

## **Flexible Folder Creation**

Folders can be created as your needs change, including during template or folder reorganization. The updated destination picker includes a **New folder** option, helping you organize templates without returning to the main folder list.

- Create new directories as your template collection grows.
- Move templates into different folders or subfolders.
- Move folders into other directories or back toward parent levels.
- Use the destination picker to select an appropriate folder when reorganizing items.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I nest folders inside other folders?**

Yes. You can create multiple levels of folders and subfolders to match your organizational needs.

**Q: Will moving a template to another folder affect its approval or status?**

No. Moving templates between folders changes their organization, not their approval or delivery status.

**Q: Can I search for a template by name?**

Yes. The Templates list provides a Search by name field. When you enter a directory, the Templates tab displays templates belonging to that folder.

**Q: What happens when I switch between Templates and Folders inside a directory?**

The Templates tab shows templates in the selected folder. The Folders tab shows subfolders inside that same directory.

**Q: Can I rename or delete folders after creating them?**

Yes. Open the three-dot menu under Actions for the folder and choose the applicable management option.

**Q: Can I move a folder back to a parent level?**

Yes. The updated folder-management experience supports moving folders into another folder or back toward parent levels.

**Q: What happens if I delete a folder that contains templates?**

Templates inside the deleted folder are moved to its parent folder. The templates themselves are not deleted with the folder.

**Q: Can I export templates from a folder?**

Template export functionality remains unchanged. You can export individual templates using the available template actions.

**Q: Where can I view template delivery and engagement information?**

Locate the relevant template in the Templates list and select View reports. The report displays the available delivery and engagement information for that template.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [WhatsApp Settings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006911)
- [How to Create a WhatsApp Template](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000861)

- [How to Use the WhatsApp Template Library](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009127)
- [How to Manage WhatsApp User Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008814)
- [WhatsApp Template-Level Analytics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003714)

## **Eliza Agent Platform Settings**

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/06f62e3a01314816b040ced910783e31)

### **Setting up a new location in the Eliza Agent Platform**

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/20ae93197e0a4faaaa04615dcc9881b3)

Using Eliza's account starts with adding a location to the account.

Start by clicking the **"Add Location"** button on**Settings > Locations**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277242/original/WlVQGxXIL5J52wKCL4014tC2fbeOq349yQ.png?1680196895)

Select the Location from the dropdown, and the Location from HL will be added to Eliza.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277257/original/847OCAC4AzsmfBubPCCfCjB2kqEYjBaHYw.jpeg?1680196898)

Once the Location is selected from the dropdown, it will show the screen where you need to choose an optional default calendar and set a priority.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277233/original/dgCCMV_5k9LnB5qh6T0CVdig_X041oe06w.png?1680196890)

A priority is a generic feature provided by EAP for managing how to prioritize locations within your Eliza account. Locations can be prioritized based on time zones, service level agreements for specific locations, etc.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277232/original/FPpnyueICKgukEvZeocXh-XIlZ12CPBZ4g.png?1680196890)

Choose the agents who can handle the conversations in this Location from the previously created list of agents.  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277246/original/wwH_FLvvYGUI8iPtoxFLJ11lMrK_ZACSCw.png?1680196898)

A note can be added that will be available in the Settings > Announcements section for agents to see.

The selected Location can also be removed from Eliza on this screen. Once all of the above is configured, click on **Add Location** to add the account to Eliza.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277249/original/9CiiPdapVD-qMimTbFU47MR-RJorYUmD6g.png?1680196898)

### **Eliza Account setup**

Any incoming conversations will be automatically assigned to agents configured to work on that Location in a round-robin fashion. This happens only among the agents who are online.

."

Any incoming message part of a conversation assigned to a particular agent will still go to the same agent, even if they are offline.

### **Configuring Webhooks.**

Go to **Settings > Company.![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290277252/original/_upzFOaiLkVU22YyAH8su4EcS64UmnnrVg.png?1680196899)**

| **Type of message** | **Description** | **Keys Configured** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manual assignment | when a conversation is assigned to an agent thru the dashboard by an agent or admin | Type, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Conversation Count, contactId, contactName |
| Auto Assignment | When the system automatically assigns a conversation to an agent | Type, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Conversation Count, contactId, contactName |
| Unassignment | When a conversation is removed from an agent | Type, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Conversation Count, contactId, contactName |
| New Message | When a new message arrives for an existing conversation | Type, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Conversation Count, contactId, contactName |
| Disposition Assigned | Whenever the disposition is assigned | Type, dispositionName, dispositionTag, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Contact Id, Contact Name |
| Appointment Booked | Whenever the appointment is booked | Type, dispositionName, appointmentId, LocationName, Priority, Agent Email, Contact Id, Contact Name |

---

### **Dispositions setup**

Dispositions are a great way to manage and track different stages of a conversation.

Enter following details

1. Disposition name.
2. Short name.
3. Tag that needs to be assigned when this disposition is assigned.
4. Whether comments are allowed while assigning the disposition.
5. Whether the comments are mandatory.
6. An option to delete the disposition that is already created.

An agent can choose the disposition while ending the conversation, and the comments entered while assigning the disposition can be retrieved from Settings > Disposition Comments. The disposition can also be re-ordered so that the ordering reflects on the 'Conversation' screen when you click 'End chat.'

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290288548/original/TRSvVX_P-WP0v--i2sGsXzELUYm4XiDNKQ.jpeg?1680201553)

#### Waiting for the customer's response

Assigned by the system automatically when the agent chooses to close the conversation while waiting for the customer's response.

#### Appointment Booked

It is assigned automatically whenever the agent books an appointment.

#### Autoclosed

Assigned in the following situations

- Pause Conversations
- Eliza Bypass tag
- Send to Eliza tag

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290288533/original/vUBOaJp1sGBq71T9j36WdQM-xwgPOFe1FQ.png?1680201545)

This screen can review the comments and see if the business process can be made more efficient or create an FAQ.

## Downloading the comments

All the dispositions entered can be downloaded as an excel file using the download button at the top right corner for the chosen criteria, such as Location, Disposition name, and agent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290289460/original/BMCF86Icz5aM2A7iL7bU2XcOHShIlO8U_g.png?1680201944)

### **FAQ management - Templates and Location FAQs**

FAQs are an efficient way to increase agent productivity.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290290006/original/xKR0dE1JFdPpSgJDC2c5dWt2uPZh2-qeyQ.png?1680202145)

When you create an FAQ, the system will give a default set of questions you can use. If you need a different set of questions, you can create your own via the "Add FAQ" button.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48290290123/original/vVpURDuGd6rEqSzcBOg9dDFpjlnBr3saDw.png?1680202190)

If you want to define the questions and want your clients to enter answers, you can enter the questions in the Location and ask your clients to login into [https://app.gohighlevel.com/v2/location/<<locationid>>/settings/eliza\_faq](https://app.gohighlevel.com/v2/location/X5392tCsXVshYg8R5fll/settings/eliza_faq) and enter the answers. These answers will be available on the Eliza Agent Platform. Please note that the subaccount should have access to the Sub-Account **settings > Eliza Service tab**. Enable this tab via User permissions for that user.

You can also use custom values in the answers by clicking the icon near the answer box.

A template can be assigned to one or more locations by clicking the "Assign" button. The assignment operation works like a mathematical set union operation.

1. If the question is available only on the template and not on Location, then this new question will be added to the Location.
2. If the question is available on the template and the answer is blank, it will NOT be overridden when assigned to the Location with the same question, but with a valid answer, it will NOT be overridden.
3. If the question is available on the template with a valid answer, and the Location also has an answer, it will override the one already available.
4. If the question is available on the template and not on the Location, then this will be added as a new question.

- Parameters available on FAQs of the Location, and not on the FAQ template

---

On the conversations screen, use the following hotkeys for the below-identified actions.

### **Announcements**

Any announcement configured in the "Edit location" option will be available for the agent in this section.

The agent will only see those announcements that belong to the Location that they are added to work on.
