## **Action Details**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Field** | **Description** |
| **Action Name** | A custom name for the action, used to identify it on the workflow canvas and in execution logs. |
| **Model** | The AI vision model used for analysis. Two models are available: GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-5.6 Tera. |
| **Image URL** | The URL of the image to analyze. Supply it from a previous step or from a custom value. The URL must be publicly accessible – see Image URL Requirements below. |
| **Analysis Prompt** | Instructions telling the AI what to look for in the image and how to respond. Supports custom values for dynamic prompts. |
| **Detail Level** | How thoroughly the image is analyzed. Defaults to Auto; can be set to High or Low. |

---

## **How to Use the AI****Analyze****Image Action**

### **Step 1:** Add the Action

1. Go to **Automation** > **Workflows**.
2. **Create** a new **workflow** or **edit** an **existing** one.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/sdAZAU36nE7nJWCjV65F+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-26+at+16.44.40.png)
3. In your workflow, click the **+** icon to **add** a **new****action**, then find **AI Analyze Image****under AI Actions** and select it. Give the action a clear, descriptive name so it’s easy to identify on the canvas.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/kQLCL5FaVCUr4s1hKvvY+/GIF+Recording+2026-08-28+at+17.26.42.gif)

### **Step 2:** Select the Model

Choose the AI vision model to use for analysis. Two models are available:

- GPT-5.6 Luna
- GPT-5.6 Tera

If you’re unsure which to use, run the same image and prompt through both and compare the responses before publishing the workflow.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/U2OY2Fou3rn6EuItyWye+/Screenshot+2026-08-28+at+17.34.07.png)

### **Step 3:** Provide the Image URL

**Enter** the **URL** of the **image** you want **to** **analyze**. 

You can pull this from a previous step in the workflow – for example, the Image URL output of an [AI Image Generation action](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008497) – or from any custom value that holds an image URL. The **URL must be publicly accessible.**

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Z8S6ZdH2R7fdMm7vr2Ht+/GIF+Recording+2026-08-28+at+17.48.19.gif)

### **Step 4:** Enter the Analysis Prompt

Write a prompt telling the AI what to look for in the image and how to respond. The more specific your prompt, the more useful the output. 

**Examples:**

- Describe this product image in detail.
- Extract all text visible in this image.
- List the items visible in this photo.
- Read the total amount from this receipt and return only the number.

The prompt field supports custom values, so you can build the prompt dynamically from contact fields, web-hook data, or earlier action output.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/BrqlEWMFrFuZdOoyfJrw+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-28+at+17.54.02.png)

### **Step 5:** Set the Detail Level

**Choose** **how** **thoroughly** the **image** **should** **be** **analyzed**. 

The **default** is **Auto**, which lets the system pick an appropriate level. You can also select **High** for more careful analysis of fine detail, or **Low** for a faster, lighter pass when you only need a broad read of the image.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/NZGbmcfO6bnZOzWBZtoU+/Screenshot+2026-08-28+at+18.01.36.png)

### **Step 6:** Save the Action

**Save** the **action**. The analysis output will be available as a variable in all downstream actions once the workflow executes.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/b5dO4SBiQDmZxj1Kcu7t+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-28+at+18.05.31.png)

---

## **Image URL Requirements**

The image URL you provide must be publicly accessible. The AI model fetches the image directly from the URL, so anything that blocks anonymous access will cause the action to fail.

```
Tip: A quick way to check is to open the URL in a private or incognito browser window. If the image loads without signing in, the action can reach it. Images stored in Media Storage – including those created by the AI Image Generation action – are already hosted at publicly accessible URLs and work without any extra setup.
```

**This means the URL must not:**

- Require a login, password, or authentication token to view.
- Sit behind a private share link, permission-restricted drive, or internal network.
- Point to a page containing the image rather than the image file itself.

---

## **Using the Output in Downstream Actions**

Once the action executes, its response is available in any subsequent action through the custom value picker under AI Analyze Image. The **output is a text value containing the AI’s answer to your prompt** – a description, extracted text, a list, or whatever else your prompt asked for.

Because the output is plain text, you can use it anywhere a text value is accepted: save it to a contact custom field, include it in an email or SMS, pass it to an outbound webhook, or feed it into another AI action for further processing.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/iUgQiDneO23xj0y0qbfR+/GIF+Recording+2026-08-28+at+18.16.48.gif)

---

## **Use Cases**

### **1. Extracting Text from Customer-Submitted Images**

**Scenario:** Customers send photos of receipts, invoices, or documents over MMS. You want to read the text out of those images and store it against the contact record instead of reviewing each one manually.

**Setup:**

- **Trigger:** Customer Replied (with image attachment)
- **Action 1:** AI Analyze Image – Image URL from the attachment. Prompt: “Extract all text visible in this image.” Detail Level: High.
- **Action 2:** Update Contact – Save the extracted text to a custom field for review or follow-up.

## **2. Verifying a Generated Image**

**Scenario:** Your workflow generates an image with the AI Image Generation action, and you want a second check on what was actually produced before it goes out to a customer.

**Setup:**

- **Action 1:** AI Image Generation – Generate the image from your prompt.
- **Action 2:** AI Analyze Image – Use the Image URL output from the previous action. Prompt: “Describe this image in detail.”
- **Action 3:** If/Else or Internal Notification – Route the workflow based on the description, or send it to your team for a quick sanity check before delivery.

### **3. Describing Product Images from a Web-hook**

**Scenario:** Product images arrive from an external system with no accompanying copy. You want a written description generated automatically for each one.

**Setup:**

- **Trigger:** Inbound Web-hook (carrying the image URL)
- **Action 1:** AI Analyze Image – Prompt: “Describe this product image in detail, including colour, material, and style.”
- **Action 2:** Outbound Web-hook – Send the description back to your catalogue or content system.

**More Ideas**

- **Screenshot triage:** Read error messages out of support screenshots so tickets can be routed by content rather than by hand.
- **Alt text generation:** Produce accessibility descriptions for images used across your sites and campaigns.
- **Image tagging:** Ask the model to return a short list of categories or keywords, then use that output to tag contacts or route the workflow.
- **Submission checks:** Confirm an uploaded image contains what was asked for before it moves further through the process.

---

## **Tips for Better Results**

- Be specific about the output you want. “Return only the invoice number” gives you a usable value; “Tell me about this image” gives you a paragraph you’ll have to parse.
- Use High detail for small text, fine print, and dense documents. Auto is fine for general descriptions.
- Verify the image URL is publicly reachable before publishing – this is the most common cause of the action failing.
- If you plan to store the output in a custom field, ask the prompt to return the value in a consistent format so downstream steps can rely on it.
- Test with a few real images before running the workflow at volume – image quality varies more than text input does.

---

## **Pricing**

Image analysis is billed per execution. The figures below give you an idea of what analyzing an image normally costs. Most analyses fall within this range.

```
Note: Treat these figures as a planning estimate rather than a fixed rate.
```

| Metric | Cost per analysis | In cents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median | $0.0004 | 0.04¢ |
| Average | $0.0013 | 0.13¢ |

## 

Your actual cost per analysis will vary depending on how you configure the action. The main factors are:

- **Model** – the vision model you select.
- **Detail Level** – the level you set (Auto, High, or Low). High analyzes the image more thoroughly and costs more than Low.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How much does it cost to analyze an image?**

Analyzing an image normally costs between $0.0004 (0.04¢) and $0.0013 (0.13¢). Your actual cost depends on the model and the Detail Level you select. See the Pricing section above for more detail.

**Q: What happens if the image URL is behind authentication?**

The action will not work. The AI model fetches the image directly from the URL, so it must be publicly accessible without a login, token, or permission check. Open the URL in a private browser window to confirm it loads for anyone.

**Q: Where do I get the image URL from?**

From any previous step in the workflow that produces one – such as the Image URL output of an AI Image Generation action, an inbound webhook payload, or a message attachment – or from a custom value where you’ve stored an image URL.

**Q: Which model should I choose?**

Two vision models are available: GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-5.6 Tera. If you’re unsure, run the same image and prompt through both and compare the responses before publishing the workflow.

**Q: What does the Detail Level setting affect?**

It controls how thoroughly the image is analyzed. Auto (the default) lets the system decide. High examines the image more carefully, which helps with small text and fine detail. Low is a faster, lighter pass suited to broad descriptions.

**Q: Can I use this to extract text from images (OCR)?**

Yes. Set your prompt to something like “Extract all text visible in this image” and the action returns the text as its output. For receipts, invoices, and other small or dense text, set the Detail Level to High.

**Q: What format is the output in?**

The output is a text value containing the AI’s response to your prompt. It’s available in downstream actions through the custom value picker under AI Analyze Image, and can be used anywhere a text value is accepted.

**Q: Can I use this together with the AI Image Generation action?**

Yes. Add AI Analyze Image after an AI Image Generation step and pass in the generated Image URL. This lets you describe or verify what was produced before the image is sent onward. Images created by AI Image Generation are stored at publicly accessible URLs, so no extra setup is needed.

**Q: Can I analyze more than one image in a single action?**

Each AI Analyze Image action processes one image URL. To analyze several images in a workflow, add a separate action for each, and reference each action’s output individually in your downstream steps.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Workflow Action – AI Image Generation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008497)
- [Workflow Action - AI Extract Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007992)
- [Workflow Action - AI Translate](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005892)
- [Workflow Action - AI Agent](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007600)

title_en: How to Create Services?
source_md:
Services helps you create bookable services so customers can self-schedule online with confidence. Use variations to present multiple options under a single service, add-ons to increase order value, and resources to prevent conflicts. This article walks through accessing the Services panel, organizing services with categories and creating a new service.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Services?](#What-are-Services?)
  - [Key Benefits of Creating Services](#Key-Benefits-of-Creating-Services)
  - [How to Access the Services Panel](#How-to-Access-the-Services-Panel)
  - [Creating and Managing Categories](#Creating-and-Managing-Categories)
  - [Service Management Features](#Service-Management-Features)
  - [What are Add-ons?](#What-are-Add-ons?)
  - [What are Resources?](#What-are-Resources?)
- [How to Create a New Service](#How-to-Create-a-New-Service)
  - [Best Practices](#Best-Practices)
  - [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are Services?**

Services is where you define what your business offers to clients, like coaching sessions, spa treatments, or fitness programs. It helps you create service listings that customers can book online while keeping things organized behind the scenes.

You can manage how and when services are offered, who provides them, and enhance them with optional **add-ons**, **resource management**, and **categories**. Services support both simple bookings and advanced business flows such as:

- Multi-location scheduling
- Service variations (e.g., different durations or price tiers)
- Upsells with add-ons
- Deposit payments

---

## **Key Benefits of Creating Services**

Knowing what each feature does makes setup faster and keeps your booking page accurate. The benefits below reflect options you configure directly when creating or editing a service:

- **Variations:** Offer multiple options (such as different lengths or tiers) within a single service, each with its own duration and price
- **Add-ons:** Present optional extras during checkout that can increase the price of the booking
- **Resources:** Reserve limited items (like rooms or stations) so they aren’t double-booked
- **Processing Time & Buffers:** Build realistic gaps and in-service timing to support smooth scheduling
- **Staff & Availability:** Assign team members to the service and manage their working hours
- **Categories:** Group services and control the order shown on the booking page
- **Private Service:** Hide specific services from the public list when you only want to share them directly
- **Custom URL & Preview:** Share a clean link and verify the booking experience before promoting it
- **Deposits & Pricing:** Collect a deposit at booking and manage your pricing settings

---

## **How to Access the Services Panel**

The Services Panel is the starting point for building, organizing, and previewing your booking experience. Within the Services Panel, you’ll find:

- A searchable and sortable list of all services
- An option to create new services
- Each service’s name, duration, price, and assigned staff
- Categories displayed on the left for easy organization
- A three-dot menu with actions: Edit, Duplicate, Delete, or Share
- A View Booking Page link for customer-facing access

To access your list of services in the Services Panel, follow these steps:

1. Click the **Calendars**tab on the left navigation bar
2. Select **Calendar Settings** from the top navigation ribbon
3. Choose the **Services**tabfrom the top navigation ribbon on the Calendar Settings page

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053194082/original/3bRHQg9UvjpCEI-cmOCAs2J_HfXmhyqITw.png?1757089766)

---

## **Creating and Managing Categories**

Service categories serve as a way to group similar or relevant services, making it easier for customers to navigate your offerings. These categories are displayed on the booking page, under which specific services are listed.

- Click the **+ New Category**button to create a new category
- Use the **three-dot (⋮) icon** to edit a category
- Drag categories to rearrange them; the order is reflected in the booking page layout

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053193881/original/6Dly2UQCoo1DUa-WUMzCBkaJ-2L1Nfx7mQ.png?1757089527)

---

## **Service Management Features**

Use the service editor to edit and update existing features. To open the editor, click the **three-dot (⋮) icon** next to the service within the Services Panel and choose **Edit**. The Service Editor includes:

- **Service Details:** Staff, duration, buffer times, processing, variations, pricing, payments, deposits
- **Add-Ons:** Upsell or enhance services with extras
- **Resources:** Assign rooms, chairs, or other assets required for the service

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053195733/original/IXCx7zTww4I0Vpf_veiiL1h7A98S2-wMvQ.png?1757092032)

---

## **What are Add-ons?**

Add-ons let you enhance services by offering optional extras that customers can book alongside their main service. They’re perfect for upselling additional features (like massage oils, treatments, or accessories) and for giving customers the ability to personalize their appointments. Add-ons can be customer-facing on the booking page or used internally by staff when creating appointments.

### **How Add-ons Appear on the Booking Page**

- Customer-facing add-ons display as optional checkboxes when booking a service
- The add-on price and/or duration is added to the total booking cost
- Hidden add-ons will not appear for customers but can be selected by staff inside the appointment modal

### **Accessing Add-ons**

1. Navigate to the Services Panel (**Calendar** > **Calendar****Settings** > **Services**)
2. Open the Service Editor for the selected service (**Three-dot (⋮)** > **Edit**) and click the **Add-ons** tab
3. Here you’ll see a list of add-ons linked to the selected service, along with their Price, Duration, and Maximum Quantity
4. From this tab, you can create new Add-ons or edit existing ones

[Click here for more information about Add-ons, including how to create and edit them](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003506)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053196384/original/tVczpEVTqXC1V5I3_eqojPVhMuk3ZFEMpw.png?1757092752)

---

## **What are Resources?**

Resources are shared assets like rooms, chairs, stations, or tools that must be available for a service to take place. Assigning resources to services helps prevent double bookings and ensures accurate capacity management.

Each resource can be linked to one or more services and configured by:

- Location: Assign where each resource is available
- Capacity: Set how many appointments or people the resource can accommodate

For example, a "Room 1" resource might be used by several services but can only support 4 people at a time. You can specify this capacity per location for granular control.

### **Accessing Resources**

1. Navigate to the Services Panel (**Calendar** > **Calendar****Settings** > **Services**)
2. Open the Service Editor for the selected service (**Three-dot (⋮)** > **Edit**) and click the **Resources** tab
3. Here you’ll see a list of Resources, along with their Total Capacity, Services Associated, Locations Associated and Status
4. From this tab, you can create new Resources or edit existing ones

[Click here for more information about resources, including how to create and edit them](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003505)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200308/original/F4xstc-mtexKkqen5QZmnVEQh6GnevLSxA.png?1757099398)

---

## **How to Create a New Service**

Use the steps below to set up your service—details, timing, pricing, staff, and preview—so your booking page is accurate and ready to share.

#### **Step 1:**Click + New Service

- Navigate to the Services Panel (**Calendar** > **Calendar****Settings** > **Services**)
- Click the **+ New Service**button in the upper right corner

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200512/original/JllFIQ5or4T6MV8J87DSZJtJpDmKe_tX2Q.png?1757099763)

#### **Step 2:** Add Basic Details

- Fill in the basic details for the service. These details include:  
    
  - **Service Image:** Upload an image that visually represents your service. You can upload from your device or a Media Library.
  - **Service Name:** The title of the service shown to customers
  - **Service Color:** Assign a color to help identify this service in the calendar
  - **Category:** Place the service under a relevant category (a new service will automatically be added to the default category if none selected)
  - **Custom URL:** Set a unique booking link for the service
  - **Description:** Add a brief summary of what the service offers. You can format this content using the rich text editor (bold/italic/underline/strikethrough, bulleted or numbered lists, hyperlinks, text/background colors, headings, and text alignment).
  - **Private Service:**Hide this service from public booking pages. New bookings may only be scheduled internally via the platform
  - **Staff Members:** Assign staff who can provide this service. At least one staff member must be assigned for the service to be bookable
  - **Duration:** Add how long the service will last
- Once all basic details have been added, click **Advanced Settings**to configure additional service details

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064240832/original/mtgpoUtmjJTfbLEIars6IidCO77vcShExQ.png?1770282550)

#### **Step 3:**Configure Service Details

- **Duration:** Set how long the service lasts
- **Processing Time:** Break down duration into three phases (Initial, Processing, Final). Staff are only booked during Initial/Final phases, and remain available for other appointments during the Processing phase
- **Buffer Time:** Add time before or after the appointment for prep or cleanup

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200659/original/3SudWPP0pe6TcJ3z9FBQS9RJcEcPyyolmQ.png?1757100317)

#### **Step 4:** Set Up Payments

- **Price:** Enter the price customers will pay
- **Partial Payments:**Allow customers to pay a deposit instead of full payment. Choose between fixed amount or percentage

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200704/original/Q1UOse8gPASRMJNB-W_Hn8cvzePFg1KUqw.png?1757100437)

#### **Step 5:**Configure Variations (Optional)

Enable **Variations** to offer multiple options under one service (e.g., different durations, or pricing).

- Add each variation’s **Name**, **Duration**, **Price**, and **Processing Time**(if any)
- Example:  
    
  - 30 mins – $120
  - 45 mins – $100
  - 60 mins – $350

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200766/original/28G7T1XuQ7SmiRxpjXjH8u0sSH1-UBj-Jw.png?1757100623)

#### **Step 6:**Save & Preview

- Click **Save Changes** to apply updates
- Use **View Booking Page** to preview how customers will see the service

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200841/original/sKKRX3ykjoipospSSPJNtwBNv7P_7zxc9w.png?1757100758)

---

## **Best Practices**

- Assign Staff and configure their availability to every service for them to be bookable
- Organize services meaningfully into categories
- Leverage Add Ons for upsells and custom options
- Use Resources to prevent over-utilization and optimize availability of linked resources

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I hide a service from the public booking page?**  
Yes. Enable "This is a private service" for the service and share the direct link instead. When this is turned on, the service will not be shown on the public booking page.

**Q: How do categories impact the booking page?**  
Category assignment and order determine how services are grouped and displayed in the public booking page. Please be aware that changing the order of the categories in the editor will change the order on the booking page.

**Q: What’s the difference between processing time and buffers?**  
Processing time is part of the appointment when the service is still in progress. Buffers are extra time added before or after the appointment to space out bookings (useful for setting up before or cleaning after an appointment).

****Q:** Does inventory tracking for products linked to services stay in sync with service appointments?**No. Inventory tracking for products linked to services is not managed or synced with the service booking lifecycle.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053200945/original/oiMHTczBsWHOaPw52X4JoZvCFrd-Webu6A.png?1757101127)

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Services - Overview & How to Get Started](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006240)
- [Global Settings in Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003546)
- [How to Enable Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006240)
- [Configuring Staff in Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005331)
- [Categories in Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003547)
- [Resources in Services](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003505)
- [Workflow Trigger – Service Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006140)

title_en: Slack Workflow Triggers: Setup, Filters, and Examples
source_md:
Slack triggers start HighLevel workflows when activity happens in your connected Slack workspace. Use them to route requests, welcome new channel members, and notify teams when messages, mentions, or emoji reactions arrive.

This article covers all five Instant Slack triggers: New Reaction Added, New Direct Message, User Invited to Channel, New Mention, and New Message Posted to Channel. Each is marked Premium in the workflow builder.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Slack Workflow Triggers?](#What-Are-Slack-Workflow-Triggers?)
- [Key Benefits of Slack Workflow Triggers](#Key-Benefits-of-Slack-Workflow-Triggers)
- [Available Slack Triggers](#Available-Slack-Triggers)
- [How to configure a Slack Trigger](#How-to-configure-a-Slack-Trigger)
- [Map event data and test the workflow](#Map-event-data-and-test-the-workflow)
- [New Reaction Added](#New-Reaction-Added)
- [New Direct Message](#New-Direct-Message)
- [User Invited to Channel](#User-Invited-to-Channel)
- [New Mention](#New-Mention)
- [New Message Posted to Channel](#New-Message-Posted-to-Channel)
- [Frequently asked questions](#Frequently-asked-questions)

---

## **What Are Slack Workflow Triggers?**

Slack workflow triggers allow you to start HighLevel workflows automatically when specific activities occur in your connected Slack workspace. Instead of manually monitoring Slack conversations, you can use these triggers to respond to incoming requests, welcome new team members, track message reactions, and notify other teams.

HighLevel provides five Instant Slack triggers for direct messages, channel invitations, app mentions, channel messages, and emoji reactions. Each trigger is a Premium feature and can be configured directly from the Workflow Builder.

A Slack **trigger** starts a workflow when a matching event occurs in Slack, while a Slack **action** performs a task, such as posting a notification to a channel or sending a direct message. You can combine these capabilities to automate communication between Slack channels and teams.

---

## **Key Benefits of Slack Workflow Triggers**

Slack workflow triggers help teams respond to conversations and requests without continuously monitoring their channels. By connecting Slack events to HighLevel workflows, you can streamline internal communication and automate routine follow-up tasks.

- **Automated Request Routing:** Start workflows when someone sends a direct message or @-mentions your Slack app, making it easier to notify the appropriate team.
- **Faster Team Onboarding:** Automatically send welcome messages or onboarding resources when users join selected Slack channels.
- **Improved Feedback Tracking:** Monitor emoji reactions on messages to initiate review notifications or follow-up processes.
- **Cross-Team Communication:** Notify other teams when new messages are posted in shared request channels.
- **Reduced Manual Monitoring:** Respond to supported Slack events automatically without having to continuously check conversations.
- **Flexible Workflow Automation:** Combine Slack triggers with HighLevel workflow actions to create automated processes that match your team's needs.

---

## **Available Slack Triggers**

HighLevel provides five Instant Slack triggers that respond to different types of workspace activity. Selecting the appropriate trigger helps ensure your workflow starts only when the intended Slack event occurs.

| Trigger | Starts when | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [New Reaction Added](#new-reaction-added) | An emoji reaction is added to a message in the selected channel. | Selected Slack channel |
| [New Direct Message](#new-direct-message) | Someone sends a direct message to the connected Slack app (bot). | Connected Slack app (bot) |
| [User Invited to Channel](#user-invited-to-channel) | A user joins or is invited to the selected channel. | Selected channel |
| [New Mention](#new-mention) | The Slack app (bot) is @-mentioned in a channel it has been added to. | Selected channel containing the app |
| [New Message Posted to Channel](#new-message-posted-to-channel) | A new message is posted to the selected public or private channel. | Selected public or private channel |

```
Important: Slack triggers are Premium workflow features. Premium executions may incur usage charges depending on your account configuration and available allowances. For additional information, see How to Enable and Rebill Workflow Premium Features.
```

---

## **How to configure a Slack Trigger**

1. Go to **Automation > Workflows** and open the workflow you want to configure.
2. Click **Add trigger**, search for **Slack**, and choose the event you want to monitor.
3. Select the correct **Connected account** for the Slack workspace. If no account is connected, complete the Slack connection flow first.
4. Keep the default **Workflow trigger name** or give it a descriptive name.
5. Configure the trigger’s channel or filters. The four channel-based triggers require a selected channel; New Direct Message has optional text and sender filters. See the trigger-specific sections below.
6. If later actions need Slack event details, use **Map your trigger** as described below.
7. Click **Save trigger**, then add the workflow actions for your use case.

Search for Slack in Add trigger to see the five available instant triggers.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084416075/original/hQk838CqaRanVH8eL5kha74FixYaxFY7yg.png?1793194291)

---

## **Map Event Data and Test the Workflow**

Mapping makes the Slack event’s metadata available in the custom values of following actions. Use the fields returned by your sample record when configuring those actions.

1. Create a new Slack event that matches the selected trigger and its configured filters. Each trigger section below includes an example test event.
2. Under **Map your trigger**, click **Find new records**.
3. Select a returned record as the mapping reference, then use the available trigger values in your later workflow actions.
4. Review the trigger and actions before enabling the workflow. When you are ready for live events, publish the workflow, create a new matching event in Slack, and check **Execution logs** to confirm the expected steps run.

If no records are returned, confirm the connected account, channel, and filters, create another matching event, and click **Find new records** again.

The channel names in the examples below are illustrative. Select channels available in your own connected Slack workspace.

---

## New Reaction Added

The **New Reaction Added** trigger starts a workflow when an emoji reaction is added to a message in the Slack channel you select.

**Setup:** Select the channel whose message reactions you want to monitor.

**Configuration:**

- **Connected account:** Select the Slack account associated with the workspace.
- **Channel:** Choose the Slack channel whose message reactions you want to monitor.
- **Map your trigger:** Capture a matching reaction event to make its available information accessible to subsequent workflow actions.

![New Reaction Added: workflow trigger name, filters, and Map your trigger settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084326121/original/wBeV1blwPVfsqbuw8gtsRbB4_xsLq2jT4A.jpeg?1793113160)

*New Reaction Added setup fields in the workflow builder.*

**Test event:** Add an emoji reaction to a message in that channel.

### Example

Your team reviews requests in #content-review. When a message receives an emoji reaction, send a notification to #review-updates so the team can follow up.

**Workflow Configuration Example:**

1. **Trigger:** New Reaction Added  
   **Channel:** #content-review
2. **Action:** Use the Slack Message action to send a notification to #review-updates. Add the details you need from the mapped trigger record.

---

## New Direct Message

The **New Direct Message** trigger starts a workflow when a direct message is sent to your connected Slack app (bot).

**Setup:** Listen for DMs sent to the Slack app (bot). Use Add filters if you want to limit the trigger by message text or sender.

**Optional filters**

- **Filter by text contains:** Limit the trigger to DMs containing a phrase. Matching is case-insensitive. Press Enter / Return to add a phrase. Text is required once this filter is added; remove it to match every message.
- **Sender:** An optional sender filter is available under **Add filters**.

![New Direct Message: workflow trigger name, filters, and Map your trigger settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084326776/original/kyqmYwK4WbFAQzyYe-weqPlf7XJzZGSMUA.jpeg?1793113387)

*New Direct Message setup fields in the workflow builder.*

**Test event:** Send a new direct message to the connected Slack app (bot).

### Example

Team members send requests directly to your Slack app. When a new DM arrives, notify #internal-help so the team can review it.

**Workflow Configuration Example:**

1. **Trigger:** New Direct Message
2. **Action:** Use the Slack Message action to post a notification in #internal-help. Include relevant details from the mapped trigger record.

---

## User Invited to Channel

The **User Invited to Channel** trigger starts a workflow when a user joins or is invited to the Slack channel you select.

**Setup:** Select the channel you want to watch for new members. Both joining and being invited are covered.

![User Invited to Channel: workflow trigger name, filters, and Map your trigger settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084321262/original/Db8V2z40Gd475YJP6mWHs6Xf2scJf2HuAw.jpeg?1793110784)

*User Invited to Channel setup fields in the workflow builder.*

**Test event:** Have a user join or be invited to that channel.

### Example

When a teammate joins or is invited to #new-starters, post a welcome message in that channel with a link to your onboarding resources.

**Workflow Configuration Example:**

1. **Trigger:** User Invited to Channel  
   **Channel:** #new-starters
2. **Action:** Use the Slack Message action to post the welcome message in #new-starters.

---

## New Mention

The **New Mention** trigger starts a workflow when your Slack app (bot) is @-mentioned in a channel it has been added to.

**Setup:** Add the Slack app (bot) to the channel, then select that channel in the trigger. The message must @-mention the app itself.

![New Mention: workflow trigger name, filters, and Map your trigger settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084321356/original/hGRX00RQFliC1iEa2NBXxk3NiuiZGOaNSg.jpeg?1793110835)

*New Mention setup fields in the workflow builder.*

**Test event:** Post a new message that @-mentions the Slack app in that channel.

### Example

Your team @-mentions the Slack app in #ops-requests when they need help. Use the trigger to notify #ops-triage of each new request.

**Workflow Configuration Example:**

1. **Trigger:** New Mention  
   **Channel:** #ops-requests
2. **Action:** Use the Slack Message action to post a notification in #ops-triage. Include relevant details from the mapped trigger record.

---

## New Message Posted to Channel

The **New Message Posted to Channel** trigger starts a workflow when a new message is posted to the public or private Slack channel you select.

**Setup:** Select the public or private channel whose new messages you want to monitor.

![New Message Posted to Channel: workflow trigger name, filters, and Map your trigger settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084326811/original/zVIZIiwvlAsWkNw9NHfj3H3oQmBR1YDrNQ.jpeg?1793113409)

*New Message Posted to Channel setup fields in the workflow builder.*

**Test event:** Post a new message in that channel.

### Example

Team members post requests in #service-requests. When a new message is posted, notify #service-triage so the team can review it.

**Workflow Configuration Example:**

1. **Trigger:** New Message Posted to Channel  
   **Channel:** #service-requests
2. **Action:** Use the Slack Message action to send a notification to #service-triage. Include relevant details from the mapped trigger record.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**Q. Why is my channel missing?**

Channel lists include public and private channels visible to the connected Slack user. Check that you selected the correct Slack account and that this user can access the channel.

**Q. Why doesn’t a direct message between teammates start the workflow?**

New Direct Message listens for messages sent to the Slack app (bot). A conversation between two people is outside the event described by this trigger.

**Q. Why doesn’t a mention start the workflow?**

Confirm that the app has been added to the selected channel and that the new message @-mentions the app itself. Also check that the workflow is enabled for live events.

**Q. Why are no sample records available?**

Create a new event that matches the selected trigger and filters, then click Find new records again. Use the test event shown in that trigger’s section.

**Q. Can I use Slack event details in later actions?**

Yes. Select a record in Map your trigger, then choose the available trigger values in following actions. Use the fields actually returned by your sample record.

**Q. How do I avoid a notification loop?**

For New Message Posted to Channel, send workflow-generated Slack notifications to a different channel from the channel being monitored. This helps avoid a notification starting the same workflow again.

**Q. Are these Premium triggers?**

Yes. All five are marked Premium in the workflow builder.

title_en: Appointment Booking in Conversation AI
source_md:
Make it easier for leads and customers to schedule time with your business by letting Conversation AI handle appointment booking automatically. HighLevel can book appointments through Conversation AI across supported channels, collect the contact details you need, and guide the conversation toward the right calendar based on your setup. You can also extend the experience with multiple calendar selection, fallback routing, cancellations, reschedules, and post-booking automation for a smoother customer journey.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Appointment Booking in Conversation AI?](#What-is-Appointment-Booking-in-Conversation-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Appointment Booking in Conversation AI](#Key-Benefits-of-Appointment-Booking-in-Conversation-AI)
- [Before You Begin](#Before-You-Begin)
- [How Appointment Booking Works in Conversation AI](#How-Appointment-Booking-Works-in-Conversation-AI)
- [Single Calendar Booking](#Single-Calendar-Booking)
- [Multiple Calendar Booking](#Multiple-Calendar-Booking)
- [Prompt and Calendar Setup Best Practices](#Prompt-and-Calendar-Setup-Best-Practices)
- [How To Setup Appointment Booking in Conversation AI](#How-To-Setup-Appointment-Booking-in-Conversation-AI)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Appointment Booking in Conversation AI?**

Appointment booking in Conversation AI allows a HighLevel bot to talk with contacts, gather the required information, offer available time slots, and book appointments on a selected booking calendar. Depending on how your bot is configured, it can support a single calendar or route requests across multiple calendars using intent-based matching. It can also work alongside broader bot settings, training, and automation so your team can reduce manual scheduling work while keeping the conversation natural and on-brand.

---

## **Key Benefits of Appointment Booking in Conversation AI**

- **Automated scheduling:**lets the bot collect contact details, present available times, and complete the booking without manual back-and-forth.
- **Smarter routing:**helps the bot choose the right calendar when you configure multiple calendars with descriptions, keywords, and optional fallback behavior.
- **Better customer experience:**supports fast replies across supported channels and reduces delays when contacts want to book, cancel, or reschedule.
- **Operational efficiency:**allows your team to trigger workflows, pause the bot after booking, or hand off to the right process after an appointment is scheduled.
- **More accurate follow-up conversations:** recent appointment context can help the bot avoid repeated booking prompts and answer follow-up questions more naturally.

---

## **Before You Begin**

A successful booking setup depends on having the right calendar and bot foundation in place before you turn on appointment booking. This helps prevent missing slots, poor routing, and incomplete responses when contacts ask follow-up questions.

Before setting up appointment booking in Conversation AI, make sure you have:

- HighLevel booking calendar already configured
- Conversation AI bot created in the sub-account
- Brand voice or Bot training setup that reflects your business accurately
- The channels selected where you want the bot to respond
- A clear plan for whether the bot should book on one calendar or route across multiple calendars

---

## **How Appointment Booking Works in Conversation AI**

Appointment booking works by combining your bot goals, calendar selection, bot training, and response behavior into one scheduling experience. When a contact asks to book an appointment, the bot can collect required details, check availability from the connected calendar, suggest time slots, and confirm the booking inside the conversation. In more advanced setups, the bot can also support cancellation and rescheduling, depending on the options you enable.

### **Accurate Date and Time Handling**

Conversation AI uses the original message timestamp to interpret dates and times throughout a conversation. This helps the bot schedule appointments accurately, even when a contact replies hours or days later.

**Relative Dates:**The bot interprets expressions such as "today," "tomorrow," and specific weekdays based on when the contact originally sent the message.

**Multilingual Date References:** The bot interprets relative dates in other languages, including "kal" and "demain," using the original message context.

**Past Time Slots:** If a previously offered appointment slot has already passed, the bot informs the contact and offers the next available time.

**Appointment Conflicts:**The bot prevents new bookings at times when the contact already has an appointment.

**Date Calculations:**The bot handles invalid dates, past dates, month and year transitions, and daylight-saving time changes.

For example, if a contact asks for an appointment "tomorrow" late at night but confirms the following morning, Conversation AI uses the date of the original request rather than interpreting "tomorrow" again.

These improvements help prevent incorrect bookings during conversations that continue across multiple days.

---

## **Single Calendar Booking**

Single calendar booking is the best option when all appointment requests should go to one booking calendar. This setup is simpler to manage and works well for businesses with one service type, one scheduling path, or one main appointment destination.

With a single calendar setup, the bot uses the calendar you assign for appointment booking and guides contacts through available time slots for that calendar. This is often the fastest path to launch if you do not need service-based routing.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068782892/original/7wDlhcmmtlBOX60j6wWVqvt9FE7m9v4Nvw.png?1775732945)

---

## **Multiple Calendar Booking**

Multiple calendar booking is ideal when your business offers different appointment types, departments, services, or routing needs. HighLevel supports multiple calendar selection for Conversation AI so the bot can identify the best calendar for the request instead of sending every inquiry to a single destination.

To improve routing accuracy, you can configure each calendar with:

- a clear description of what the calendar is for

- additional trigger keywords related to the service or use case

- an optional fallback calendar if the bot cannot confidently match the request to one calendar

This setup helps the bot distinguish between services such as consultations, demos, support calls, or location-specific bookings.

**Note:** Multiple calendar booking is currently available only for **prompt-based Conversation AI bots**.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068783071/original/5VnAh9823NG08ukvpGXYyToT5rtScHRtMQ.gif?1775733041)

---

## **Prompt and Calendar Setup Best Practices**

Good booking performance depends on more than selecting a calendar. The bot also needs the right prompt, training, and business context so it can guide the conversation clearly and answer user questions accurately. Calendar details are used for calendar selection, while information you want the bot to discuss with end users should also be included in the main prompt.

Use these best practices when preparing your bot:

- Write clear calendar descriptions so the bot can tell when each calendar should be used.

- Add relevant keywords for common services, appointment types, or request phrases.

- Put customer-facing business details in the bot’s prompt or training, not only in calendar descriptions.

- Keep your initial message and tone aligned with your brand voice.

- Choose the contact fields you really need so the booking process stays efficient.

---

## **How To Setup Appointment Booking in Conversation AI**

A proper setup ensures the bot can understand booking intent, use the right calendar, and respond in a way that feels helpful instead of repetitive. Following these steps also makes it easier to expand later into multi-calendar routing, cancellations, reschedules, or workflow automation.

1. Go to your HighLevel sub-account and open **AI Agents > Conversation AI**. Create a new bot or open an existing bot you want to use for appointment booking.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068766776/original/rR9-acklfGCzfp-6BQemzHGazUNmx_2ihQ.png?1775724633)
2. Configure the bot basics, including the bot name, wait time before responding, and initial message. These settings shape how the appointment conversation begins.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068784776/original/s7iGMy4c9j_G7DwVcM5JffVzvpXzefUDMg.gif?1775733992)
3. Open Bot Goals and choose the contact information you want the bot to collect, such as name, email, or phone number.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068783510/original/X2PeH5UhGfSAhzdpfu_RD_nrkBEpLNsNVQ.png?1775733257)
4. Enable Appointment Booking and select the booking calendar you want the bot to use. If you only need one scheduling path, choose a **Single C****alendar.** For Guided and Flow Builder bots, Single Calendar is currently the only available option.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068766915/original/Z2v6lT98uylxj42SnvgHn1jebUn14fcDMg.png?1775724726)
5. If your business needs service-based routing, select **Multiple C****alendars** and configure each one with a description and any supporting keywords. Add a fallback calendar if you want the bot to route unmatched requests to a default option  
     
   **Note:** Multiple Calendar booking is currently available only for **prompt-based Conversation AI bots**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068783913/original/JHkCln7HPBDLfdNbyI0b-6v0pwNdW0M18A.gif?1775733516)
6. If you want to use a Services Calendar (v2), select **Services** option. You can choose the public-facing services the AI should handle, and the bot can book using service details such as staff selection, add-ons, and variations. Keep in mind that private services are not supported, and online payment is not collected by the bot during the booking flow.  
     
   **Note:** Services booking is currently available only for **prompt-based Conversation AI bots**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068781330/original/s1uU_oC39st0VGv10umS2dat1EGKXyjYWQ.gif?1775732167)
7. Add prompt instructions and training content that explain what the bot should say to contacts about your services, availability expectations, and booking flow. Do not rely only on calendar descriptions for customer-facing information.
8. Decide whether the bot should also support cancellation and rescheduling. Configure any post-booking behavior you need. This can include sending only the booking link, pausing the bot after an appointment is booked, or triggering one or more workflows after booking.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068781664/original/rtSNJDtGawJK3ZtKRx00qppYDdQmn9O3mA.png?1775732379)
9. Save the bot and test the experience carefully. Live testing is especially important for confirming cancellation or reschedule behavior.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Should I use one calendar or multiple calendars?**  
Use one calendar if every appointment request should go to the same booking path. Use multiple calendars when you need the bot to route requests based on service type, department, or intent.

**Q: Can the bot cancel or reschedule appointments?**  
Yes, HighLevel supports cancellation and rescheduling options in Conversation AI-related appointment flows when those settings are enabled.

**Q: Do calendar descriptions replace prompt instructions?**  
No. Calendar descriptions help the bot choose the right calendar, but customer-facing details should also be included in the main prompt or bot training.

**Q: Can appointment booking work inside a flow-based bot?**  
Yes. HighLevel’s Conversation AI Flow Builder includes a Book Appointment AI action and appointment options such as cancel and reschedule.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Setting Up Conversation AI: Streamline Client Engagement](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401-setting-up-conversation-ai?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI: Multiple Calendars Support for Appointment Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006559-conversation-ai-multiple-calendars-support-for-appointment-booking?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI Flow Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006515-conversation-ai-flow-builder?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Set Up a Booking Calendar in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005061-getting-started-setup-a-booking-calendar?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Cancellation and Rescheduling of Appointments in Form Based Bots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005503-cancellation-and-rescheduling-of-appointments-in-form-based-bots?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Appointment Booking for Voice AI Agents in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005293-appointment-booking-for-voice-ai-agents-in-highlevel)

title_en: User Access
source_md:
Managing who has access to your HighLevel account is important for security, efficiency, and accountability. This article explains how to manage users at both the agency and sub-account levels, configure user details and account assignments, control roles and permissions, manage Login As access, and verify sensitive login-email changes. You'll also learn how email-change security alerts work and how to restore a previous login email address if an unexpected change occurs.

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Agency User Management](#agency-user-management)
- [User Management (Sub-Account Level)](#sub-account-user-management)
- [Permissions & Roles Overview](#permissions-roles)
- [Email Change Verification](#email-verification)
- [Email-Change Security Alerts and Reversal](#email-change-security-alerts-and-reversal)
- [Best Practices](#best-practices)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

## **Agency User Management**

### **Who This Is For**

This section applies to agency owners and admins who need to grant access to employees or client personnel across multiple sub-accounts.

### **How to Access**

1. From **Agency View**, go to **Settings**.
2. Select **Users**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892627/original/4rksi5CiFQLIU1TZgVjxi5mqcDZ8GwbX0w.png?1793760886)

### **What You Can Do**

From **Users**, you can search the user list, add new users, edit existing users, manage roles and permissions, transfer ownership when applicable, manage sub-account access, or remove users.

When adding or editing a user, you can configure supported user details, roles, permissions, and account assignments.

- **Personal logo** for the user profile
- **First name**
- **Last name**
- **Email address** used as the login email
- **Phone number**
- **Password**
- **Permissions**
- **User Type**  
  - **Agency:** The user can access all client accounts under the agency.
  - **Account:** The user can access only selected client accounts.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892665/original/qLJ4wK_PYrvt4YfLprnzkltoFCSAqItSFg.png?1793760946)

### **Account Assignment**

- For an **Agency** user type, specify which client accounts the user should receive notifications for.
- For an **Account** user type, select the specific client accounts the user can access.

The redesigned **Users** experience also provides user search, clearer owner-role guidance, ownership transfer controls, improved duplicate-email guidance, and call-forwarding and voicemail options during user creation.

If an email address already exists in the agency, HighLevel provides guidance on the appropriate next step, such as contacting the agency admin or adding the existing user from **Users**.

### **Login As Permission**

The ability to **Login As** another user is permission-gated for each admin. When **Enable Login As** is turned off for a user, the Login As option is hidden.

Go to **Agency View → Settings → Users → Edit User → Roles & Permissions → User Management** to manage this permission.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892676/original/xijOIpReWYClm8pFCkp4ZdfuOn-98BT5YQ.png?1793760989)

---

## **User Management (Sub-Account Level)**

### **Who This Is For**

This section applies to admins and users who manage access within a specific HighLevel sub-account. Users added here are also visible in the Agency-level **Users** area.

### **How to Access**

1. Open the required **Sub-Account**.
2. Go to **Settings → Users**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892689/original/Pf6MO6sJ3-OpPXhZFxRB4SdaxEHV4RGeRA.png?1793761093)

### **What You Can Do**

From **Users**, you can search, add, edit, and remove users and manage their available roles, permissions, and access settings.

Supported user details include:

- **Personal logo**
- **First name**
- **Last name**
- **Email** used for login
- **Phone number**
- **Password**
- **Permissions**

When creating a user, the redesigned experience also includes available call-forwarding defaults and voicemail setup.

If the email address already exists in the agency, HighLevel provides guidance on the appropriate next step, such as contacting the agency admin or adding the existing user from **Users**.

Automatic personal booking calendar creation for newly added sub-account users depends on the agency-level **Preloaded Example Data** setting in **Settings → Company**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892695/original/5CEQ_LbCCLMVWvt-gnLVypDxvyxrqcwgYA.png?1793761137)

---

## **Permissions & Roles Overview**

You can control what each user can access and what actions they can perform by assigning the appropriate roles and permission scopes.

Permissions can determine which areas of HighLevel a user can access, which actions they can perform, and which accounts or assigned data they can work with.

---

## **Email Change Verification (Multi-Channel OTP)**

Changing a user's login email is a sensitive update. HighLevel supports multi-channel OTP verification so identity can still be confirmed when the existing email address is inaccessible.

**Available verification methods:**

- **Email OTP**
- **Phone (SMS) OTP**
- **TOTP (Authenticator app)**

The verification methods shown depend on the user's verified 2FA methods.

### **When You Change Your Own Email**

Users can manage their own login email from **My Profile → Security**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892699/original/EjJfKk-J4xzmUEVicD5nSUG8lfzHmscD0w.png?1793761169)

- The system prompts you to verify using another available 2FA method, such as **SMS** or an **Authenticator app**.
- If no other verified method is available, you are prompted to set up an authenticator app.

### **When an Admin Changes Another User's Email**

The system shows the available verification methods for that user, which can include Email, SMS, and/or an Authenticator app.

---

## **Email-Change Security Alerts and Reversal**

HighLevel sends security alerts whenever a user's login email address changes. These notifications help users identify unexpected account changes and restore their previous email address without contacting an administrator. The security alerts provide an additional layer of protection alongside the existing email-change verification process.

### **How Email-Change Security Alerts Work**

Security alerts keep users informed when their login email address changes, whether they make the update themselves or an administrator makes it on their behalf. Each alert provides details to help the account owner recognize and respond to an unexpected change.

When a user's login email address changes:

- **Email Notification:** A security alert is sent to the previous email address. This ensures the person who previously controlled the login email receives notification of the change.
- **In-App Notification:** The affected user also receives a security notification within HighLevel.
- **Change Details:** The alert identifies what changed and when the change occurred. The timestamp is displayed in the user's timezone.
- **Change Attribution:** The alert identifies the initiator as "by you" or "by your admin," helping users distinguish their own changes from administrator-initiated updates.
- **Admin-Initiated Changes:** Alerts also cover supported administrative and impersonation flows when an email address changes on a user's behalf.

If you recognize the email change and intended to make it, no further action is required.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892100/original/Lbv_d2AIt8U1afANz0Z8Lh0c_q0tCogl9w.png?1793759095)

*Example security alert email showing the date, change details, and available reversal action.*

### **How to Reverse an Unexpected Email Change**

If your login email address changes without your knowledge, you can restore your previous email using the reversal link included in the security email. This self-service recovery process does not require you to log in, making it possible to reverse the change even if your account access has been affected.

1. Open the inbox associated with your previous login email address.
2. Find and open the security alert notifying you that your email address has changed.
3. Review the change details, including when the change occurred and whether it was initiated by you or your administrator.
4. Click the reversal link provided in the security email. HighLevel restores your previous login email address without requiring you to sign in.
5. Review the confirmation page to verify that your previous email address has been restored.

**Important:** The reversal link is valid for **30 days** and can be used only once. If the email change was expected, you do not need to use the reversal link.

After the previous email address is restored, HighLevel displays a confirmation page indicating that the reversal is complete.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892051/original/K5xKFBJafkDVs72k9tDyMubpst2j0BlRsw.png?1793758839)*Example confirmation page displayed after restoring the previous login email address.*

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892098/original/emT_cSBNnacURr9KjwSBYSqnphmYsVTvTw.png?1793759062)

*Example of an email message indicating that a login email address was restored.*

A reversal link can only be used once. If the link has already been used, it cannot complete another reversal. Contact your agency if you need assistance.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084892070/original/jGbpHtq4_WNtkwBQc3KcEHYmBufO6a_-WQ.png?1793758899)

*Example screen for a reversal link that has already been used.*

### **Security, Branding, and Language Support**

Email-change security alerts protect account access while maintaining a consistent experience for users across different agencies and languages. Notifications and recovery pages support agency branding and localization, while completed reversals are recorded for accountability.

- **Agency Branding:** Security alerts use the agency's logo and domain to maintain the agency's branded experience.
- **Language Support:** Security alerts and reversal pages support 12 locales. If a translation is unavailable, the affected text appears in English.
- **Auditability:** Every completed email-address reversal is recorded.
- **Automatic Alerts:** Notifications are triggered by supported login-email changes, including updates made directly by a user or on the user's behalf.

Email-change security alerts complement the existing multi-channel OTP verification process. Verification helps secure the email update, while security alerts provide visibility and recovery after the change occurs.

---

## **Best Practices**

- **Use least privilege:** Give users only the permissions they need. Avoid granting full agency access unless necessary.
- **Use Account-type users for limited access:** Choose this user type when someone should have access only to selected client accounts.
- **Track changes:** Maintain clear records of who has access and when access changes are made.
- **Review access periodically:** Update permissions or remove users when their responsibilities change or access is no longer required.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What's the difference between an Agency user type and an Account user type?**

An **Agency** user type grants access across all client accounts under the agency. An **Account** user type restricts access to only the client accounts you explicitly select.

**Q: If I add a user under Users in a sub-account, will they appear in Agency User Management?**

Yes. Users added in a sub-account are also visible in the Agency-level **Users** list.

**Q: Can I set different permission levels for different users?**

Yes. Permission settings let you control which supported features and actions each user can access.

**Q: How do I change someone's access later if their role changes?**

Open the relevant user record in **Users** at either the Agency or Sub-Account level, then update the user's type, assigned accounts, roles, or permissions as needed.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Admin vs. User Roles and Permission Scopes](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001078296-admin-vs-user-roles-and-permission-scopes)
- [User Roles, Permissions and Assigned Data: Subaccount](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002544-user-roles-permissions-and-assigned-data-subaccount)
- [How to Create a User or Admin to Manage Multiple Locations Without Giving Them Agency Access](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001153972-how-to-create-a-user-or-admin-to-manage-multiple-hl-locations-without-giving-them-agency-access-)
- [Agency | Managing User Roles & Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002543-agency-managing-user-roles-permissions)
- [Login As User (Agency Admin Only)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/48001223053?portalId=48000045315)
- [Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008837-phone-number-change-security-alerts-and-reversal)

title_en: How to Use Breakout Rooms in Meeting Room
source_md:
Breakout Rooms let you divide a Meeting Room session into smaller groups for workshops, training, coaching, and team discussions. Hosts can create rooms, assign participants, manage individual discussions, and bring everyone back to the main meeting. This guide explains how to create breakout rooms, configure participant permissions, manage active sessions, and control recording and live transcription for individual rooms.

```
TLDR: In an active Meeting Room, click Breakout Rooms, choose the number of rooms and an assignment method, then click Create rooms. Review your assignments and Options, then click Open all rooms. Use Close all rooms when you are ready to bring everyone back.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Breakout Rooms?](#What-are-Breakout-Rooms?)
- [Key Benefits of Breakout Rooms](#Key-Benefits-of-Breakout-Rooms)
- [Participant Assignment Methods](#Participant-Assignment-Methods)
- [Breakout Room Settings](#Breakout-Room-Settings)
- [How To Create and Open Breakout Rooms](#How-To-Create-and-Open-Breakout-Rooms)
- [How To Manage Active Breakout Rooms](#How-To-Manage-Active-Breakout-Rooms)
  - [View and Join Rooms](#View-and-Join-Rooms)
  - [Broadcast a Message to All Rooms](#Broadcast-a-Message-to-All-Rooms)
  - [Manage Timers and Close Rooms](#Manage-Timers-and-Close-Rooms)
  - [Record and Transcribe Individual Rooms](#Record-and-Transcribe-Individual-Rooms)
- [How Participants Join and Switch Rooms](#How-Participants-Join-and-Switch-Rooms)
  - [Join an Assigned Room](#Join-an-Assigned-Room)
  - [Choose or Switch Rooms](#Choose-or-Switch-Rooms)
  - [Return to the Main Meeting](#Return-to-the-Main-Meeting)
- [Important Notes and Limits](#Important-Notes-and-Limits)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Breakout Rooms?**

Breakout Rooms are smaller discussion spaces within a Meeting Room session. Instead of keeping everyone in one conversation, the host can divide participants into groups that collaborate independently and then return to the main meeting.

For example, a trainer can divide attendees into practice groups, a team lead can organize separate brainstorming discussions, or a coach can create smaller groups for focused conversations.

Hosts manage the rooms from the meeting interface, including participant assignments, room access, broadcasts, timers, recording, and live transcription.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084152632/original/cPl1tL6GaYRnFfFcbEKCdb5Zj2fQ51TWhQ.png?1792975983)

---

## **Key Benefits of Breakout Rooms**

Breakout Rooms help hosts organize group activities while keeping participants within the same meeting experience.

- **Flexible grouping:** Assign participants automatically, select their rooms manually, or let them choose a room.
- **Centralized session management:** Join discussions, move participants between rooms, and broadcast messages to every room.
- **Controlled session timing:** Set a duration, extend sessions when needed, and use a countdown before participants return.
- **Independent recording and transcription:** Manage recording and live transcription separately for each breakout room.

---

## **Participant Assignment Methods**

When creating breakout rooms, choose how participants will be assigned. The available methods support different types of activities and levels of host control.

| Assignment method | How it works | Useful for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Automatically** | Assigns participants to rooms automatically. | Quickly dividing a meeting into smaller groups. |
| **Manually** | Lets the host choose participants’ room assignments. | Creating specific teams, coaching groups, or workshop groups. |
| **Let participants choose** | Lets participants select which room to join. | Topic-based discussions or activities where attendees choose their group. |

```
Automatic assignment and automatic movement are separate settings. 
Automatically determines participants’ room assignments. 
Auto-move people to rooms, available under Options, determines whether assigned participants move into their rooms automatically when the rooms open.
```

---

## **Breakout Room Settings**

Click **Options** in the Breakout Rooms panel to configure how participants move between rooms and how breakout sessions end.

| Setting | What it controls |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto-move people to rooms** | Moves assigned participants into their breakout rooms automatically when the rooms open. |
| **Let people switch rooms** | Allows participants to move between breakout rooms. |
| **Allow return to main room** | Allows participants to return to the main meeting while breakout rooms are active. |
| **Close after** | Sets the duration before breakout rooms close automatically. |
| **Countdown** | Sets a countdown before rooms finish closing and participants return to the main meeting. |

Configure these settings before opening the rooms so the participant experience matches your activity. For example, a structured training session may use assigned rooms and automatic movement, while an open discussion may allow participants to choose and switch rooms.

---

## **How To Create and Open Breakout Rooms**

These steps begin inside an active Meeting Room session where you are the host. For instructions on starting a Meeting Room through Communities, see **[Communities – Use Go Live to Host Meetings & Broadcasts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006673)**.

### 

**Step 1: Open Breakout Rooms**

Click **Breakout Rooms**, represented by the four-square icon in the meeting toolbar. The Breakout Rooms panel opens on the right side of the meeting.

**Step 2: Choose the Number of Rooms and Assignment Method**

Enter the number of rooms you want to create. You can create up to **100 breakout rooms per session**.

Under **Assign people**, choose **Automatically**, **Manually**, or **Let participants choose**. Then click **Create rooms**.

**Step 3: Review the Draft Room Plan**

After creating the rooms, review the room list and participant assignments. The panel displays a **Draft** label while you prepare the breakout session.

Expand a room to review its participants. Rename rooms and adjust assignments as needed, or click **Add room** to create another room. Review the **Not assigned** section for participants who do not currently have a room assignment.

```
Creating rooms does not start the breakout session. Participants are not moved into rooms while you are preparing the draft plan.
```

**Step 4: Configure Options**

Click **Options** and review the movement permissions, automatic closing duration, and countdown settings.

Return to the room list after configuring your settings.

**Step 5: Open the Rooms**

Click **Open all rooms** to start the breakout session.

Assigned participants receive an invitation to join their room or move automatically, depending on your settings. When participant choice is enabled, attendees can select a room to join.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084152661/original/Ac3hxXTA_uR1W5jRW4avmA2oy4DwJimYTA.png?1792976145)

---

## **How To Manage Active Breakout Rooms**

Once rooms are open, use the Breakout Rooms panel to monitor groups, support participants, and manage the session.

### **View and Join Rooms**

Use the **Rooms** tab to review the room list. Expand a room to see its participants, or use **Search people or rooms** to locate a specific person or room.

Click **Join** next to a room to enter that discussion. You can also move participants between rooms as needed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084152662/original/6dhx-4rL-epWPB4fZPgieFwzIgYFplSJ4A.png?1792976145)

### **Broadcast a Message to All Rooms**

Broadcasts let you share instructions or reminders with every breakout room without joining each discussion.

1. Click **Broadcast** at the bottom of the Breakout Rooms panel.
2. Enter your message in **Message to all rooms**.
3. Click **Send**.

For example, you might remind groups to select a spokesperson or prepare one idea to share when they return.

### **Manage Timers and Close Rooms**

Use **Close after** to configure automatic closure. During a timed session, the host panel displays the remaining time. Sessions can also be extended when groups need more time.

To end one breakout room, open its three-dot action menu and select **Close room**. To bring all groups back, click **Close all rooms**.

When a closing countdown is enabled, participants receive a countdown before returning to the main meeting.

### **Record and Transcribe Individual Rooms**

Recording and live transcription are managed independently for each breakout room. Use the room’s three-dot action menu to access its controls.

| Action | How to use it |
| --- | --- |
| **Start or stop recording** | Use the room’s recording control to manage recording for that room. While recording is active, the menu includes **Stop recording**. |
| **Start live transcription** | Select **Transcribe this room** from the room’s action menu. |
| **Stop live transcription** | Use that room’s transcription control to stop transcription independently of recording. |
| **Check capture status** | Review the room’s recording and transcription indicators. An active recording displays a **REC** indicator next to the room. |

```
Manage recording and transcription for each room individually. These are separate controls, so review the status of each room you intend to record or transcribe.
```

---

## **How Participants Join and Switch Rooms**

The participant experience depends on the host’s assignment method and movement settings.

### **Join an Assigned Room**

When invited to an assigned room, participants see a **Join breakout room** dialog that identifies the room.

Click **Join** to enter the room. Click **Not now** to dismiss the invitation without joining at that moment.

When **Auto-move people to rooms** is enabled, assigned participants can be moved automatically instead of accepting an invitation.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084152663/original/EIhMV4sIuQ3Fqeggq28t63AD5icQDCT-TA.png?1792976178)

### **Choose or Switch Rooms**

When the host allows participants to choose their room, open **Breakout Rooms** from the meeting toolbar to view the **Choose a room** dialog.

Review the available rooms, expand a room to see its participants, and click **Join** next to the room you want to enter.

Participants can switch rooms when the host permits room switching.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084152672/original/uaYN41kkazp_iQ7rm-c_fyzx3AVcII5xzw.png?1792976194)

### **Return to the Main Meeting**

When the host enables **Allow return to main room**, participants can return to the main meeting while breakout rooms are active.

When rooms are closing, participants see the closing countdown. They can click **Return now** to return before the countdown finishes, or return automatically when the rooms close.

---

## **Important Notes and Limits**

**Room limit:** You can create up to **100 breakout rooms per session**. This is the number of breakout rooms, not a statement of participant capacity.

**Draft versus open rooms:** **Create rooms** prepares the room plan. **Open all rooms** starts the breakout session.

**Participant permissions:** Choosing rooms, switching rooms, and returning to the main meeting depend on the host’s settings.

**Per-room capture:** Recording and live transcription are managed independently for individual rooms. Check the relevant room’s status indicators rather than assuming the same settings apply to every room.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How many breakout rooms can I create?**

You can create up to **100 breakout rooms per session**.

**Q: Does creating rooms immediately move participants out of the main meeting?**

No. Rooms remain in a draft state until you click **Open all rooms**. After rooms open, participants join through an invitation, move automatically, or choose a room, depending on the settings.

**Q: What is the difference between automatic assignment and automatic movement?**

Automatic assignment determines which room each participant is assigned to. Automatic movement determines whether assigned participants move into those rooms without clicking **Join**.

**Q: Why are some participants listed under Not assigned?**

These participants do not currently have a breakout-room assignment. Review this section and assign anyone who needs to join a specific group.

**Q: Can participants choose or switch rooms themselves?**

Yes. Select **Let participants choose** when creating rooms to allow room selection. Use **Let people switch rooms** in **Options** to allow movement between rooms.

**Q: Can I send the same instructions to every room?**
