Yes. Click **Broadcast**, enter your message, and click **Send** to share it with all breakout rooms.

**Q: Can I record one room without recording every room?**

Yes. Recording is managed independently for each breakout room. Live transcription is also controlled separately for each room.

**Q: Can participants return before the breakout session ends?**

Yes, when the host enables **Allow return to main room**. During the closing countdown, participants can also click **Return now**.

---

title_en: How to Clone and Share Managed Agents Using Snapshots
source_md:
Managed Agents (formerly Super Agents) can be packaged inside HighLevel Account Snapshots and deployed across multiple subaccounts. This helps agencies reuse proven AI configurations, streamline client onboarding, and maintain consistent agent behavior without rebuilding each agent manually. Managed Agents are available under the **Agent Studio** asset category during Snapshot creation, refresh, and loading workflows.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Managed Agents in Snapshots?](#What-Are-Super-Agents-in-Snapshots?)
- [Key Benefits of Managed Agents in Snapshots](#Key-Benefits-of-Super-Agents-in-Snapshots)
- [What Transfers with a Managed Agent?](#What-Transfers-with-a-Super-Agent?)
- [Managed Agents in the Snapshot Asset Selector](#Super-Agents-in-the-Snapshot-Asset-Selector)
- [Conflict Checking When Loading Managed Agents](#Conflict-Checking-When-Loading-Super-Agents)
- [Refreshing a Snapshot After Updating a Managed Agent](#Refreshing-a-Snapshot-After-Updating-a-Super-Agent)
- [How To Set Up Managed Agents in Snapshots](#How-To-Set-Up-Super-Agents-in-Snapshots)
- [Create a Snapshot That Includes a Managed Agent](#Create-a-Snapshot-That-Includes-a-Super-Agent)
- [Load the Managed Agent into Another Subaccount](#Load-the-Super-Agent-into-Another-Subaccount)
- [Verify the Managed Agent in the Destination Subaccount](#Verify-the-Super-Agent-in-the-Destination-Subaccount)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Managed Agents in Snapshots?**

Managed Agents in Snapshots are reusable Agent Studio assets that can be copied from a source subaccount into other HighLevel subaccounts. A Snapshot packages the selected agent configuration so agencies can deploy the same AI-powered experience across clients, locations, or standardized account templates.

When a Managed Agent is included in a Snapshot, HighLevel preserves its agent structure, configuration, connected Knowledge Bases, and version state. Supporting assets must also be selected when they are needed by the agent.

---

## **Key Benefits of Managed Agents in Snapshots**

Packaging Managed Agents in Snapshots reduces repetitive setup work while helping agencies deliver consistent AI experiences across multiple accounts.

- **Faster client onboarding:** Deploy prebuilt Managed Agents without recreating their configuration for every new client.
- **Consistent AI experiences:** Reuse tested prompts, instructions, triggers, capabilities, and agent behavior across subaccounts.
- **Scalable deployment:** Distribute one or more Managed Agents to multiple clients or business locations.
- **Flexible asset selection:** Include individual Managed Agents independently or package them with other Snapshot assets.
- **Simplified updates:** Refresh a Snapshot after changing an agent in the source subaccount, then distribute the updated asset to linked accounts.
- **Reusable agency solutions:** Share configured agents through Snapshot links or include them in broader account templates.

---

## **What Transfers with a Managed Agent?**

Understanding what a Snapshot preserves helps you prepare the source subaccount and identify any supporting assets that must be selected separately.

A Managed Agent Snapshot can preserve:

- Agent flow structure
- Node configurations
- Prompts and instructions
- Triggers
- Skills and capabilities
- Connected Knowledge Bases when the required Knowledge Base assets are selected
- Agent version state, such as Draft, Staging, or Production
- Selected supporting assets

Snapshots transfer selected configuration assets rather than live account activity or customer records. Integrations, third-party connections, credentials, and other account-specific resources may require additional setup in the destination subaccount.

```
Important: Review the agent’s dependencies before creating the Snapshot. If the Managed Agent relies on a Knowledge Base, workflow, Custom Value, or another selectable asset, include that supporting asset in the Snapshot.
```

---

## **Managed Agents in the Snapshot Asset Selector**

The Snapshot asset selector organizes supported assets by product category. Managed Agents appear beneath **Agent Studio**, allowing you to expand the category and select only the agents needed for a particular deployment.

You can use this asset selector when:

- Creating a new Snapshot
- Refreshing an existing Snapshot
- Loading a Snapshot into a subaccount
- Pushing selected Snapshot assets to linked subaccounts

HighLevel also supports selecting individual assets rather than loading every asset contained in the Snapshot.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076472939/original/W8W6GVxjQGXSa7Q9SG6CuMx2LnD-Bk6FLw.png?1784628209)**

---

## **Conflict Checking When Loading Managed Agents**

Conflict checking helps identify selected Snapshot assets that may overlap with assets already present in the destination subaccount. Reviewing conflicts before loading reduces the risk of unintentionally replacing an existing configuration.

The asset-selection screen provides two options:

- **Proceed to check conflicts:** Continue to the conflict-review step before loading the selected Managed Agents.
- **Proceed without conflict check:** Start the load without reviewing possible conflicts first.

Use conflict checking when loading a Snapshot into an active subaccount that may already contain a related agent or earlier version. General Snapshot loading supports reviewing conflicting assets and deciding which selected items should be applied.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076473369/original/BFlJGmzaZi2z-raffc0oC2RaiMcyILsSxw.png?1784628379)**

After choosing to check conflicts, expand the destination subaccount to review the identified items and select the assets you want to apply.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076473649/original/JyEnlZza1H6n80C1GxTQAozsV6cK_qkqOQ.png?1784628471)

---

## **Refreshing a Snapshot After Updating a Managed Agent**

Snapshots do not update automatically when an agent changes in the source subaccount. Refreshing the Snapshot captures the latest selected configuration and creates an updated Snapshot version for future loads or pushes.

**To refresh a Managed Agent:**

1. Make the required changes to the agent in the original source subaccount.
2. Return to **Agency View > Account Snapshots**.
3. Locate the Snapshot and click its **Refresh** icon.
4. Expand **Agent Studio**.
5. Select the updated Managed Agent.
6. Select any new or modified supporting assets.
7. Click **Refresh**.
8. Wait for HighLevel to finish fetching the selected assets.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076473857/original/gZ1q_wBrMO7jXd5VKpRDQLkUDg3-EQ98Kw.png?1784628576)**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076474098/original/XthFMSkWPAS-1Y6T_wbaPGkMxfZYRAp0LQ.png?1784628720)**

After refreshing, use the applicable Snapshot loading or push-update workflow to distribute the selected changes. Updates pushed from an agency Snapshot are available to linked subaccounts within that agency; external recipients generally need an updated shared Snapshot.

---

## **How To Set Up Managed Agents in Snapshots**

Preparing the source agent and selecting its required assets helps ensure that the destination subaccount receives a complete, usable configuration. Review the agent before creating the Snapshot, then verify its settings after loading.

### 

### **Create a Snapshot That Includes a Managed Agent**

1. Open the source subaccount and confirm that the Managed Agent contains the configuration you want to reuse.
2. Switch to **Agency View**.
3. Navigate to **Account Snapshots**.
4. Click **Create New Snapshot**.
5. Enter a descriptive Snapshot name.
6. Select the source subaccount containing the Managed Agent.
7. Continue to the asset-selection step.
8. Expand **Agent Studio**.
9. Select the Managed Agent or Managed Agents you want to include.
10. Select any supporting assets required by the agents, such as applicable Knowledge Bases, workflows, or Custom Values.
11. Review the selected assets.
12. Click **Create** to save the Snapshot.

HighLevel creates Snapshots from assets already configured in a source subaccount; the Snapshot itself is not built independently from scratch.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076474265/original/OE0JF1k_PgdFextNgRGehvtzC1_ik7UvCQ.png?1784628816)

---

### **Load the Managed Agent into Another Subaccount**

1. From **Agency View**, open **Sub-Accounts**.
2. Locate the destination subaccount.
3. Open its three-dot menu and select **Manage Client**.
4. Open **Actions** and select **Load Snapshot**.
5. Choose the Snapshot containing the Managed Agent.
6. Select the destination subaccount when prompted.
7. At the **Assets** step, expand **Agent Studio**.
8. Select the Managed Agents you want to load.
9. Choose one of the following:

   - Click **Proceed to check conflicts** to review possible conflicts.
   - Click **Proceed without conflict check** to continue directly.
10. When using conflict checking, expand the destination subaccount and review the available selections.
11. Click **Proceed** to start loading the selected assets.
12. Wait for the loading process to finish.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076474600/original/vIP43johIVbtdDc7cSES06LkXe3IninAQw.png?1784628984)**

---

### **Verify the Managed Agent in the Destination** **Subaccount**

1. Open the destination subaccount.
2. Navigate to **AI Agents > Agent Studio**.
3. Open the **Managed Agents** tab.
4. Confirm that the transferred agent appears in the list.
5. Open the agent and review its:

   - Name and description
   - Triggers
   - Skills
   - Capabilities
   - Knowledge Base configuration
   - Instructions
   - Required integrations or account-specific connections
6. Test the agent in the destination account.
7. Publish or activate it when it is ready for use.

Some copied assets may require integrations, permissions, approvals, credentials, or destination-specific configuration before they can operate correctly.

******![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076474707/original/QQeLExgm4XzMmYg1kF7hMNABhnihojWoMw.jpeg?1784629036)******

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076474806/original/0jRgSjcRDYwraOlj1fsNRBYp6wX-w1HH4Q.png?1784629102)**

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I include more than one Managed Agent in a Snapshot?**  
A: Yes. Expand the Agent Studio category and select the individual agents you want to package.

**Q: Do I need to include every Snapshot asset when copying a Managed Agent?**  
A: No. Snapshot asset selection is granular. Select the Managed Agent and any supporting assets it needs rather than loading unrelated assets.

**Q: Why is my transferred agent missing its Knowledge Base content?**  
A: Confirm that the required Knowledge Base was selected when the Snapshot was created or refreshed. Snapshots package the assets selected in the asset picker.

**Q: Should I use conflict checking when loading a Managed Agent?**  
A: Conflict checking is recommended when the destination account may already contain a related agent or earlier version. It gives you an opportunity to review possible overlaps before the selected assets are applied.

**Q: Does editing the source Managed Agent automatically update the Snapshot?**  
A: No. Refresh the Snapshot and select the modified agent to capture its latest configuration.

**Q: Will a transferred Managed Agent run immediately?**  
A: Review and test the agent after loading. Account-specific integrations, permissions, credentials, or other connections may need to be configured in the destination subaccount before the agent can operate as intended.

**Q: Can I push an updated Managed Agent to multiple subaccounts?**  
A: Yes. After refreshing the Snapshot, use the push-update workflow to select linked subaccounts and the assets that should receive the update.

**Q: Can Managed Agents be distributed through shared Snapshots?**  
A: Agent Studio agents can be packaged for distribution through Snapshot links, and the dedicated Agent Studio Snapshot workflow also supports broader sharing or Marketplace use. Review all dependencies before distributing the Snapshot.

---

title_en: Create and Use Text and Email Snippets in HighLevel
source_md:
Conversations • Snippets • Reusable Messaging

Create and Use Text and Email Snippets in HighLevel

HighLevel Snippets let you save reusable message content so you can respond faster without rewriting common messages. You can create separate Text and Email Snippets, personalize them with dynamic content, organize them into folders, and quickly insert saved content when communicating with contacts. Snippets help teams maintain consistent messaging while reducing repetitive work. This guide explains how to create, organize, manage, and use Snippets across supported HighLevel experiences.

What You'll Learn

Learn the difference between Text and Email Snippets, how to create and organize reusable content in the current HiRise Snippets interface, how to use Snippets in Conversations, how reusable SMS content works in workflows, and how attachments behave in different messaging experiences.

Important

The current **HiRise Snippets** experience is automatically enabled for locations and does not require a Labs or beta setting. The classic Snippets list layout has been retired. Users accessing Snippets through Conversations need **Conversations → View & manage conversation** permission.

# What Are Snippets in HighLevel?

Snippets are reusable templates for text or email messages. Instead of repeatedly typing the same response, your team can save frequently used content once and insert it whenever the same or similar message is needed.

HighLevel supports separate **Text Snippets** and **Email Snippets**. Snippets can also use supported personalization tools such as Custom Values and Trigger Links so reusable messages can still include information that is specific to the contact or use case.

Common uses for Snippets include:

- Appointment reminders and follow-ups
- Answers to frequently asked questions
- Customer support responses
- Promotional messaging
- Business hours and contact information
- Standard instructions or next steps
- Frequently reused email content

## Key Benefits of Snippets

Snippets make recurring communication faster while giving teams a centralized library of reusable messaging that can be reviewed, organized, and updated as business needs change.

- **Save Time:** Reuse frequently sent content instead of rewriting or repeatedly copying the same message.
- **Improve Consistency:** Give team members access to approved messaging for common situations.
- **Personalize Messages:** Use supported Custom Values to dynamically insert contact or account information.
- **Stay Organized:** Use folders, search, filters, and management controls to maintain larger Snippet libraries.
- **Reduce Repetitive Work:** Quickly insert prepared content into supported messaging experiences.
- **Keep Content Current:** Update reusable messaging from the Snippets workspace when business information or messaging changes.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Understanding where Snippets are stored, which permission controls access, and how different messaging channels treat reusable content helps prevent confusion when creating or sending Snippets.

Before you begin:

- Snippets are managed within the relevant **Sub-Account**.
- The current HiRise Snippets experience is automatically available; no Labs setting is required.
- Users accessing Snippets through Conversations need **Conversations → View & manage conversation** permission.
- Choose the appropriate **Text Snippet** or **Email Snippet** type based on the content you want to reuse.

Keep these distinctions in mind:

- **Text vs. Email:** Text Snippets and Email Snippets are separate reusable content types.
- **Attachments:** Attachment behavior differs between email templates, campaigns, and workflows.
- **Workflows:** Reusable content options depend on the workflow messaging action being configured.
- **RCS Snippets:** RCS uses separate formats and rich-message requirements.
- **WhatsApp Templates:** WhatsApp Templates are different from regular Snippets and have separate approval and usage requirements.

### Give a User Access to Snippets

Snippets inside Conversations depend on the user's Conversations permission, so review their role when the Snippets tab or composer option is not available.

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, click **Settings**.
2. Select **My Staff**.
3. Select the team member you want to update.
4. Open **Roles & Permissions**.
5. Locate **Conversations**.
6. Enable **View & manage conversation**.
7. Click **Save**.

## How To Create a Snippet

Creating a Snippet gives your team reusable content that can be searched, organized, and inserted whenever the same type of communication is needed.

### Step 1: Open the Snippets Dashboard

The current HiRise Snippets dashboard is located inside Conversations and provides access to your saved Snippets, folders, search, filters, and creation controls.

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, click **Conversations**.
2. Select **Snippets** at the top of the Conversations page.

### Step 2: Choose the Snippet Type

Text and Email Snippets are created separately so reusable content can be structured for the communication channel where it will be used.

1. Click **+ New Snippet**.
2. Select **Add Text Snippet** or **Add Email Snippet**.

![HiRise Snippets dashboard showing New Folder and New Snippet with Add Text Snippet and Add Email Snippet options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056243868/original/sK2i8lnlVoluWHqwbM9WF7TbQVsjM5sfhQ.png?1760702857=)

### Step 3: Build and Personalize the Snippet

A clear name, reusable message content, and supported dynamic values make the Snippet easier for other team members to understand and safely reuse.

1. Enter a descriptive name for the Snippet.
2. Add the message content.
3. Add supported **Custom Values** when information should populate dynamically.
4. Add a **Trigger Link** when the message requires a supported trackable link.
5. Review the available preview.
6. Use the available test option when appropriate.
7. Click **Save**.

**Naming Tip:** Use names that explain the purpose of the Snippet, such as *Appointment Reminder*, *FAQ - Business Hours*, *New Lead Introduction*, or *Support - Password Reset Instructions*.

**SMS Cost Awareness:** For SMS-oriented content, review the displayed character count, segment count, and estimated cost information before sending.

### Alternate Snippets Access

Snippets can also be accessed from **Sub-Account View → Marketing → Snippets**. The Conversations Snippets page uses the current HiRise layout and provides the most direct access to folders, search, filters, and management controls.

## How To Organize and Manage Snippets

Keeping your Snippet library organized helps team members locate approved content quickly and reduces the chance that outdated or duplicate messaging is reused.

From **Conversations → Snippets**, you can:

- Use **Search** to locate Snippets by name or keyword.
- Filter Snippets by supported type.
- Click **New Folder** to create folders.
- Move Snippets into folders.
- Edit existing Snippets.
- Duplicate a Snippet to create a variation.
- Delete Snippets that are no longer needed.
- Use the current page URL to preserve supported search and pagination preferences when sharing the view with another user in the same sub-account.

### Manage an Individual Snippet

The three-dot action menu gives you quick access to the most common Snippet management tasks without leaving the main Snippets list.

1. Go to **Conversations → Snippets**.
2. Locate the Snippet you want to manage.
3. Click the **three-dot menu (⋮)**.
4. Select the appropriate option:
   - **Move to Folder**
   - **Edit Snippet**
   - **Duplicate Snippet**
   - **Delete Snippet**

**Organization Tip:** Folders are useful for grouping Snippets by purpose, such as Sales, Support, Appointments, Billing, or FAQs.

## How To Use Snippets in Conversations

Using Snippets in Conversations lets team members quickly populate prepared messaging while still giving them an opportunity to review and edit the content before it is sent to the contact.

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, click **Conversations**.
2. Open the conversation with the contact you want to message.
3. Select the appropriate messaging channel.
4. Click the **Snippets** icon in the message composer.
5. Browse the available folders or search for the Snippet you want.
6. Select the Snippet.

![Conversation composer showing the Snippets picker for selecting reusable message content](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081372383/original/-u4VGvyjoGhCqJQXeRqtHysHub-KsrCjYg.png?1789854576)

7. Confirm that the Snippet content populates the message composer.
8. Review the message and make any necessary changes.
9. Confirm that supported dynamic values display as expected.
10. Send the message.

**Before Sending:** Selecting a Snippet does not lock the populated message. You can review and edit the inserted content before sending it to the contact.

## Using Snippets in Workflows

Reusable messaging can also help keep automated communication consistent. The available template controls depend on the workflow messaging action you are configuring.

### Use Reusable Content in a Send SMS Action

The Send SMS workflow action includes a Templates selector that can populate the SMS message with saved reusable content, helping standardize automated messages without retyping the same copy.

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, click **Automation**.
2. Select **Workflows**.
3. Open an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
4. Add or open a **Send SMS** action.
5. Locate **Templates** in the Send SMS configuration.
6. Select the saved reusable message you want to use.

![Workflow Send SMS action demonstrating selection of reusable message content from Templates](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054024535/original/CrC7ZfU2-KCpi3hNdfuPUmKu_olJGbSDQA.gif?1758186871)

7. Review the content that populates the message field.
8. Add or update supported Custom Values when needed.
9. Use the test SMS option to verify the message.
10. Save the workflow action.
11. Test the workflow before publishing it.

**Send Email Workflows:** The Send Email action also supports reusable email templates, but workflow email templates have separate editing, copy, and synchronization behavior. Use the dedicated workflow email template controls when configuring automated email content.

## How Attachments Work with Snippets

Attachment behavior changes depending on where Snippet content is used. Reviewing these differences helps ensure recipients receive the intended files instead of only the reusable message content.

| Where the Snippet Is Used | Attachment Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Email Templates** | Attachments associated with the Snippet are not automatically included when the Snippet is inserted into an email template. The supported message content is inserted. |
| **Campaign Emails** | Attachments associated with the Snippet are included when the Snippet is inserted into a campaign email. |
| **Workflows** | Attachments associated with the Snippet are not automatically added to workflow emails or SMS messages. Add any required file using the supported controls in the workflow action. |

**Before Sending:** Always review the final message and its attachments before sending a campaign or publishing an automated workflow.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the difference between a Text Snippet and an Email Snippet?

Text Snippets and Email Snippets are separate reusable content types designed for text-based and email communication. Choose the type that matches the content you plan to reuse.

Q: Where do I create and manage Snippets?

Go to **Sub-Account View → Conversations → Snippets**. Snippets can also be accessed from **Marketing → Snippets**.

Q: Do I need to enable the HiRise Snippets experience in Labs?

No. The HiRise Snippets page is automatically enabled for locations, and the classic Snippets layout has been retired.

Q: Can I organize Snippets into folders?

Yes. Click **New Folder** from the Snippets page, then move related Snippets into the appropriate folder.

Q: Can I search for or duplicate an existing Snippet?

Yes. Use the Search field to locate Snippets by name or keyword. To duplicate one, open its **three-dot menu (⋮)** and select **Duplicate Snippet**.

Q: Can Snippets include personalized information?

Yes. Snippets support Custom Values and other supported placeholders so reusable messages can include dynamic information.

Q: Is there a limit to how many Snippets I can create?

HighLevel currently documents no fixed limit on the number of Snippets you can create. Use folders, search, and filters to keep larger libraries organized.

Q: What permission does a user need to access Snippets in Conversations?

The user needs **Conversations → View & manage conversation** permission.

Q: Are WhatsApp Templates the same as regular Snippets?

No. Regular Snippets provide reusable content in supported conversations, while WhatsApp Templates have separate approval and usage requirements for WhatsApp messaging.

Q: Are RCS Snippets the same as Text Snippets?

No. RCS Snippets support RCS-specific message formats, media, actions, and fallback messaging. They use a separate creation and sending process.

title_en: LC Email Sending Limits, Ramp-Up, and Trial Agency Rules
source_md:
Email · What's New

LC Email — Sub-account Rampup: Smart Sending Graduation & Shared Domain Reputation Protection

Sub-accounts on a shared sending domain now see exactly where they stand — daily limit, today's usage, current stage, and a complete history of every stage change — directly on the Email Services page.

Availability

Available for new agencies created on or after **27 April 2026** on GHL Shared or Agency Shared domains. Existing agencies are unaffected.

What's covered

[The new Sending Limit panel](#section-1)

[Stage and status badge](#section-2)

[Contextual alerts and recommendations](#section-3)

[Stage History timeline](#section-4)

[Dedicated Domain nudge](#section-5)

[For agencies: the Update Limit control is now automatic](#section-6)

[Trial agency view: a flat 100/day cap](#section-7)

[Quick FAQ](#section-faq)

Watch the Walkthrough

[동영상](https://watchclueso.com/embed/tv4ey2oqb1v1dbjc)

Until now, sub-accounts on a shared domain had a daily sending limit but no real visibility into it — no usage counter, no context for why the limit was set the way it was, and no way to see how it would change over time. That has changed. The Email Services page now shows live limit data, the current sending stage, plain-language alerts when something needs attention, and a timeline of every stage change.

This article is a tour of what's new on the screen.

Sub-account user

Sections explain what end users will see and what the new states mean for day-to-day sending.

Agency admin

Sections explain what's changed in agency Advanced Settings and the support portal.

## The New Sending Limit Panel

Sub-account user

On any sub-account using a GHL Shared or Agency Shared domain, the Email Services page now shows a dedicated **Sending Limit** panel at the top. It surfaces three numbers side by side, with no extra clicks required.

- **Daily Limit** — the maximum emails this sub-account can send today, based on its current stage.
- **Sent Today** — a live counter of campaign and bulk emails sent so far.
- **Remaining** — the difference between the two, updated in real time.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070232730/original/dQIC_Gu-gXFNOiU68eSWtq7awVBgazdj_w.png?1777474036)

Healthy state: Sending Limit panel with live usage, current stage, and "Sending is healthy" status.

When the daily ceiling is hit, the panel switches to a red **Daily limit reached** state with a clear "Resets at midnight UTC" note, and the top of the page surfaces a blocking banner so it cannot be missed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070232829/original/wEZJ9yIs0dsSpeiZtKQDndYZDeZZaZPe1w.png?1777474082)

Daily limit reached: the page now blocks campaign sends and tells users exactly when the limit resets.

Note for users

1-to-1 emails, payment confirmations, calendar invites, and system notifications are *not* counted against the daily limit and continue to deliver normally even when the limit is reached.

## Stage and Status Badge

Sub-account user

Every shared-domain sub-account is on a stage from 1 (starting) to 8 (maximum). The panel shows the current stage as a badge alongside the daily limit, so users always know which tier they're on. A small **"Why do we use stages?"** tooltip next to the badge explains, in plain language, how the system protects shared-domain reputation.

The eight stages and their daily limits are:

| Stage | Daily limit |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — Starting | 1,000 |
| 2 | 2,500 |
| 3 | 5,000 |
| 4 | 6,500 |
| 5 | 8,000 |
| 6 | 10,000 |
| 7 | 14,000 |
| 8 | 15,000 |
| 9 - Maximum | 25,000 |

  

**Note:******New Stage 9 at 25,000/day (shared domain and agency owned)****  
**Before:** The shared domain ramp topped out at 15,000/day with no next step. Senders who outgrew this had only one option — upgrade to a dedicated domain.  
  
**After:** A new Stage 9 at 25,000/day gives high-volume senders room to grow before needing a dedicated domain.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070232961/original/T39g3ZbuHAWwM6yww-Wu2zdZjF8mzAYJ5Q.png?1777474179)

New account view: "Warming up" state at Stage 1 with an explanation of how the stage will grow.

Brand-new sub-accounts open at Stage 1 with the Warming up status. As sending performance stays healthy, the badge automatically rolls forward through the stages

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233081/original/nJueVp5InZt-b46JpQr0qRaXKoSdUispLQ.png?1777474247)

Stage 8 — Maximum: 15,000/day with a CTA to create a dedicated domain for unlimited sending.

## Contextual Alerts and Recommendations

Sub-account user

The page now adapts to the sub-account's actual sending health. Instead of one generic screen, it renders a different banner and recommendation block for each state. Every alert is paired with concrete, step-by-step actions the user can take to recover.

State A

Bounce downgrade

A red **High bounce rate detected** banner appears when the sub-account's hard bounce rate goes above the threshold. The recommendations differ depending on whether email validation is already enabled, so the guidance is always relevant.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233166/original/JBPqeeRgEJXOp1LURrvI2GkSw-hNfpUkVA.png?1777474306)

With email validation enabled.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233209/original/83bxI4d-NAPcYGVk0lgO4Pg2bZ7bBGKL4A.png?1777474337)

Without email validation enabled.

State B

Delivery downgrade

A "Delivery rate dropped below 95%" banner appears with recommendations to pause campaigns to unengaged contacts and tighten audience targeting.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233224/original/ajp166pgsla1RXsuaLZMbchSOyUmStBjbg.png?1777474365)

Delivery rate has slipped: actionable steps to pause low-engagement campaigns and reduce volume.

State C

Spam complaint downgrade

When spam complaints exceed the threshold, recommendations focus on opt-in quality, list hygiene, and unsubscribe visibility.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233267/original/Accv3nX7ApVu4QoQD9kLOkhB7E9yY1JF5A.png?1777474403)

Spam complaints crossed the threshold: guidance focuses on opt-in quality, list hygiene, and unsubscribe visibility.

State D — Stage 1 Flagged

If a sub-account at Stage 1 also has critical health issues, the page elevates to an **Account flagged** state. The warning explains exactly which contacts to suppress and reassures the user that transactional and 1-to-1 emails will continue to deliver.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233306/original/NVc84aWw-yDWswQJWegLod3rU_Suk5Bzlg.png?1777474436)

Stage 1 flagged: targeted recovery steps plus a reminder that transactional emails are unaffected.

State E — Suspended

Usage tiles read "unavailable" and the page makes it clear sending is fully halted pending review.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233383/original/LLoS_7VqTi_rK0IQGeCNfSSWKCyrLSdjUg.png?1777474469)

Suspended: usage tiles read "unavailable" and the page makes it clear sending is fully halted pending review.

What changed under the hood

AUP enforcement emails now use clearer, state-specific subject lines so it's immediately obvious whether an account is on a first-strike 12-hour block, a second-strike 24-hour block, or a permanent lock awaiting manual review.

## Stage History Timeline

Sub-account user

Agency admin

The Email Services page now includes an expandable **Stage History** section that lists every upgrade and downgrade with the date and the reason. This is the first time both end users and agencies have an in-product audit trail of how a sub-account's sending capacity has evolved.

- **Upgrade entries** are tagged "Stage improved" and include the new daily limit.
- **Downgrade entries** are tagged "Stage declined" and surface the trigger — bounce spike, sustained delivery issue, or spam spike.
- Brand-new accounts see a friendly empty state until enough sending activity is recorded.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233488/original/MkjYtyuzZQ30uDiD0Bj0pWGvksw7-I89-w.png?1777474545)

Stage History: each transition shown chronologically with the reason and the resulting limit.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233565/original/zhN_mf7YprnYluns5VEK0HEet9tsksFeRg.png?1777474608)

Empty state: shown for new accounts that haven't yet been evaluated.

## Dedicated Domain Nudge

Sub-account user

A persistent, dismissible banner now sits on the Email Services page for every shared-domain sub-account, encouraging an upgrade to a dedicated domain for higher throughput and a sender reputation tied to the user's own domain. The banner automatically disappears once the account reaches Stage 8 — at which point a similar nudge appears in the Maximum Stage card instead.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233860/original/ubP5pj8eE3PMhB_Bx74u4b3s4W3OFJHW-A.png?1777474789)

Shared-domain banner: "You're using a shared domain" with an "Add a dedicated domain" CTA.

## For agencies: The Update Limit control is now automatic

Agency admin

For new agencies (created on or after 27 April 2026), the manual **Update Limit** control on the agency Advanced Settings screen has been replaced with an informational banner that reads *"Limits are automatic now"* and links directly through to the sub-account's Email Services page.

- The Update Limit panel and footer button are hidden entirely from Agency Advanced Settings.
- Existing agencies are completely unaffected and keep the manual control.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070233979/original/RcCzwHysXl5qcxalYoD4DvpPQt3BhpyJtA.png?1777474870)

Why this changed

Shared-domain reputation is shared across every sub-account on it. Manual overrides on a single account could pull the reputation down for everyone else. Stage-based progression replaces overrides with an automatic, transparent path to higher limits — earned through clean sending behavior.

## Trial Agency View: A flat 500/day cap

Agency admin

Sub-account user

Trial agency sub-accounts can send email campaigns, subject to the applicable 500 emails/day trial limit.  
  
Sub-accounts under a trial agency don't enter the rampup system at all. They run on a dedicated trial view with a 500 emails/day cap, no Update Limit control, and a streamlined panel that shows only the domain card and the trial limit.  
  
Trial agency sub-accounts can send email campaigns, subject to the applicable 500 emails/day trial limit.  
  
The moment the parent agency converts to a paid plan, the trial UI is replaced with the full Sending Limit panel and Stage History, and the rampup engine activates automatically from Stage 1.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070234256/original/8BXH4eAo8ziGMG-VdVE3azepOcJ9NyOuwg.png?1777475007)  
  
  
**Note:******Trial sub-account cap: 100 → 500/day****  
  
**Before:** Every sub-account under a trial agency was silently capped at 100 emails/day — an emergency measure set in April to stop a spam attack. The actual fix (location creation cap) was already live, but the 100/day cap stayed on. Sub-accounts had no idea why they were hitting limits.  
  
**After:**Trial sub-accounts can now send up to 500/day. 99% of legitimate trial users never exceed this naturally.  

## Quick FAQ

Q: Will my existing sub-accounts change?

No. All agencies created before 27 April 2026 are completely unaffected  same limits, same controls, same UI. A migration plan for existing agencies will be communicated separately by end of Q2 2026.

Q: Where do I see my current stage?

Open **Email Services** from the sub-account's left navigation. The Sending Limit panel shows the current stage badge alongside Daily Limit, Sent Today, and Remaining. Expand **Stage History** on the same page for the full timeline.

Q: Can I request a manual limit increase?

For new agencies on shared domains, no — limits are governed entirely by the rampup engine. The fastest path to a higher daily limit is consistent, healthy sending, which will move the sub-account up the stages automatically. Sub-accounts that need a higher limit sooner should add a dedicated domain.

Q: What happens if my limit is reached?

Campaign and bulk emails sent after the daily ceiling will fail  they are not queued or retried. 1-to-1 emails, payment confirmations, calendar invites, and system notifications continue to deliver as normal. The limit resets at 00:00 UTC.

Q: Why did my account move down a stage?

The Stage History entry for the downgrade includes the trigger  bounce spike, sustained delivery issue, or spam spike — alongside the date. The banner on the page will also show targeted recommendations for that specific issue.

title_en: Introduction to Project Management
source_md:
Project Management brings tasks and projects directly into your CRM, so the work your team is doing sits alongside the contacts and opportunities it relates to. This introduction explains what Project Management is, how work is organised, and what each part of it does, providing a foundation before you explore individual features in depth.

```
Note: Project Management is now available to agencies on the $497 plan. To enable it, navigate to Agency or Sub-account Settings → Labs and toggle on Project Management to access the new experience.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Project Management?](#What-is-Project-Management?)

- [How to provide feedback](#How-to-provide-feedback)

---

## What is Project Management?

Project Management is a workspace inside your sub-account for planning and tracking work. Instead of keeping a separate tool for your team's tasks and a CRM for your customers, you create tasks in the same platform your customer records live in.

A task is a single unit of work with a status, an owner, dates, and a priority. Tasks live inside Lists, Lists are organised into Spaces, and any task can be broken down into subtasks. Tasks can also be linked to CRM records, so the work connected to a customer is visible in context.

For example, rather than tracking an onboarding checklist in a spreadsheet and manually copying updates into the CRM, you can:

1. Create an onboarding List with a task for each step.
2. Assign each task to the team member responsible and give it a due date.
3. Move tasks across the board as each step is completed.

---

## Where to find Project Management

Project Management is available through the tasks tab in the Contacts area of your sub-account. Open "Contacts" in the left navigation menu, then select the "Tasks" tab in the row of tabs at the top of the page. 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083531060/original/XIDaR5pAZTY9C9gttHkeEG7vMv-4vbdxuA.png?1792162233)

```
Individual tasks have their own address. When you open a task, the page address gains a task identifier, which means you can copy the address from your browser and share a link that opens directly on that task.
```

---

## Key benefits of using Project Management

1. One system of record: Keep customer data and the work being done for that customer in the same platform, with no copying between tools.
2. Clear ownership: Every task has an assignee, dates, and a priority, so nothing sits unclaimed.
3. Visibility at a glance: Switch between Kanban and List view to see either workflow stage or a detailed breakdown of the same tasks.
4. Structure that scales: Spaces, Folders, Lists, tasks, and subtasks let a short checklist and a large multi-team project live in the same system.
5. Fields that fit your process: Add custom fields to a Space so tasks capture the information your team actually needs.
6. Controlled access: A Space can be made private and shared with named members, so sensitive work is only visible to the people who need it.

---

## Use cases for Project Management

1. Client onboarding: Run a repeatable onboarding checklist per customer, with each step assigned and dated.
2. Campaign delivery: Track creative, copy, and launch tasks for a marketing campaign on a single board.
3. Internal operations: Manage recruiting, finance, or admin work in a private Space, separate from client-facing work.
4. Service delivery: Break a delivered engagement into subtasks so a large piece of work can be tracked stage by stage.
5. Sales follow-up: Turn commitments made during a deal into dated tasks so follow-up does not depend on memory.

---

## How work is organized

Project Management uses a nested structure, shown as an expandable tree in the panel on the left of the page.

### Spaces

A Space is the outermost container, usually representing a team, a department, or a major line of work - for example Marketing, Delivery, or Internal Ops. Each Space is shown with a color dot and can be expanded to reveal what is inside. A Space holds its own set of task statuses, its own custom fields, and its own member list, and it can be made private.

### Folders

A Folder is an optional grouping layer inside a Space, used when a Space has enough Lists that they need sorting. A Folder holds Lists and can be expanded like a Space.

### Lists

A List holds the tasks themselves and is typically a project, a client, or an ongoing work stream - for example Q3 website refresh or Acme Corp onboarding. A List can sit directly inside a Space, or inside a Folder within that Space. Lists do not expand in the tree, because tasks are shown in the main area of the page rather than in the tree.

### Tasks and subtasks

A task is the unit of work inside a List. A subtask is a task nested under a parent task, used to break a larger piece of work into steps.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439337/original/6WHzXFKKAis7p1E1mVgrdOCYu3ZVWQ4dhA.png?1786707263)

## What a Task contains

Opening a task slides a panel in from the right. The top of the panel shows a breadcrumb telling you where the task lives, in the form Space / List. The panel contains:

1. Task name: Editable directly in the panel.
2. Description: A rich text editor for the detail of the work, with formatting controls and undo and redo.
3. Status: The stage the task is at. The available statuses come from the Space the task belongs to.
4. Assignee: The single person responsible for the task.
5. Dates: A single date or a date range, shown with the timezone it is being displayed in.
6. Priority: Low, Normal, High, or Urgent.
7. All fields: The custom fields configured for the Space, with a count of how many exist.
8. Associated objects: CRM records linked to the task, with a count.
9. Subtasks: Tasks nested under this one, with a count and a button to add another.
10. Comments: A composer at the foot of the panel for discussion on the task.

---

## Views: Kanban and list

The same tasks can be displayed in two layouts. Changing the view does not change the tasks, only how they are arranged, so you can switch freely.

Examples of what each view suits:

**1. Kanban view**- seeing where work is sitting and what is stuck.

**2. List view** - scanning many tasks at once and comparing their details.

In Kanban view, tasks appear as cards in columns, with each column representing a status. Each column header shows the status name and how many tasks it holds, and each column has an Add Task control at the foot. Cards show the task name, its date or date range, and a subtask count if it has any.

In List view, tasks appear as rows rather than cards.

Switch between them using the "View" control in the toolbar above the board.

Kanban view 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083530771/original/2Y3NYH6LLqjryIvBpeaGeZOSWxp6LpbmDg.png?1792162103)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439357/original/PaGPTZE0p-ilQp92r_CLZ0SmrsSaLiE_BQ.png?1786707264)

List view 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439352/original/H2PzZohW8yIcXE-oip3ya8K2z0Colei5Jw.png?1786707264)

```
For a full walkthrough of both layouts, including grouping and filtering, see the article "Board (Kanban) and list views"
```

---

## Steps for getting started

Open Tasks

- Go to "Contacts" in the left navigation menu of your sub-account, then select the "Tasks" tab.

Contacts area with the Tasks tab selected

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439351/original/qa4lg22qN2EGkUV4uDksHMje_0h2AEcbLg.png?1786707264)

Create a Space

- Create a Space for the team or area of work you are setting up, and give it a name a new team member would recognize, such as Marketing or Client Delivery. You can also give it a color so it is easy to pick out in the tree.

Creating a new Space

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439335/original/-TdZ1eockoGia1yjnB65a5zmCtktqw9A8A.png?1786707263)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439342/original/8buvlSot95YbIjXW_Isog_IXsLODJJvxaw.png?1786707263)

**Create a List inside the Space**

- Hover over your new Space in the left panel, open its options menu, and choose "Create list". This is where your tasks will live. If you expect a lot of Lists, use "Create folder" first and put the Lists inside it.

**Review your task statuses**

- Open the Space options menu and select **Status options**. Each Space organizes task statuses into four groups: **Not started**, **Active**, **Done**, and **Closed**. You can create custom statuses in Not started, Active, and Done. Closed is a system-defined group that does not support custom statuses.
- Review these before adding tasks, because they become the columns on your Kanban board.

**Create your first task**

- Click "Add task" in the toolbar, or "+ Add Task" at the foot of the status column you want the task to start in. Give it a clear name, then set an assignee, a date, and a priority.

The inline task composer with name, assignee, date, and priority

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078830013/original/1AAJKnOhc0P-bwWMmlj9NqDZQ25TkuW5WQ.gif?1787154888)

Add the detail

- Open the task to add a description, fill in any custom fields your Space uses, and link the CRM records the work relates to.

Break the work down with subtasks

- If a task has multiple steps, open it and use the Add Task control in the Subtasks section. This keeps the parent task as the headline and the detail underneath.

Start working the board

- Drag cards between status columns as work progresses, and use Group by and the filter controls in the toolbar to narrow down what you are looking at.

Dragging a task card between two status columns

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439343/original/uP2chDzpAh9gwxIis82donqa0VdYaMCGjg.png?1786707264)

Control who can see the Space

- Once your structure is working, open the Space options menu and choose "Settings" to make the Space private and choose who it is shared with.

Space settings panel with the privacy option

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078439344/original/YumoLnei04jYncoD9fe6m6dhVDTtW3sKYw.png?1786707264)

---

Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Where do I find Project Management?**

Under Contacts in the left navigation menu, on the Tasks tab.

**Q: What is the difference between a space, a folder and a list?**

A Space is the outer container, usually a team or department, and it holds statuses, custom fields, and members. A Folder is an optional grouping layer inside a Space. A List holds the actual tasks and usually represents one project or client. A List can sit directly in a Space or inside a Folder.

**Q: What is the difference between a task and a subtask?**

A task is a unit of work in a List. A subtask is a step nested under a parent task, managed from the Subtasks section of the parent.

**Q: Can I hide a project from the rest of my team?**

Yes. A Space can be marked as private and shared with named members.

**Q: Can I link a task to a contact or an opportunity?**

Yes. Each task has an Associated objects section for linking CRM records.

**Q: Can I share a link to a specific task?**

Yes. Open the task and copy the address from your browser. It includes a task identifier, so the link opens on that task.

**Q: What happens to the tasks in a list if I delete the list ?**

On deleting the list, tasks under the list are deleted. Deleted items can be restored within 2 months via respective audit logs.

---

## Next up

## [Learn to organize work with Spaces, Folders and Lists](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008443-organize-work-with-spaces-folders-and-lists)

---

## How to provide feedback

## Your feedback is critical to improving Project Management before General release. Here's how to share it:

- Post your feedback/suggestions/ideas on our [Canny board](https://highlevel.canny.io/tasks)
- Schedule a feedback call: Book a time that works for you using [scheduling link](https://speakwith.us/abhilasha)

title_en: How to Set Up and Use Service Booking in the Client Portal
source_md:
Clients can now book services directly from the new HighLevel Client Portal, alongside their meeting appointments. Businesses choose which Services booking pages appear, so clients can find and book services without separate booking links. Client information is automatically filled in during booking, and eligible appointments can be managed from the same Appointments area. This guide covers configuration, the client booking experience, and appointment management.

---

**Table of Contents**

- [What is Service Booking in the Client Portal?](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#what-is-service-booking-in-the-client-portal)
- [Key Benefits of Service Booking in the Client Portal](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#key-benefits-of-service-booking-in-the-client-portal)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#prerequisites-and-limitations)
- [How To Setup Service Booking in the Client Portal](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#how-to-setup-service-booking-in-the-client-portal)
- [How Clients Book Services](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#how-clients-book-services)
- [View and Manage Service Appointments](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#view-and-manage-service-appointments)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#frequently-asked-questions)
- [Related Articles](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad57b44-1838-8324-b14c-3c369841394b#related-articles)

---

# **What is Service Booking in the Client Portal?**

Service Booking allows clients to discover, book, and manage services directly from the **Appointments** area of the HighLevel Client Portal.

Previously, the Client Portal appointment-booking experience focused on meeting calendars. With Service Booking, clients can also access Services booking pages that a business has enabled for the Client Portal.

When a client selects **Book Appointment**, available calendars and Services booking pages appear in one booking catalog.

Clients can choose a service, select an available date and time, and submit their booking without leaving the Client Portal. Depending on the booking-page configuration, they can book one or multiple services.

Businesses retain control over which Services booking pages appear and whether the Appointments feature is available in the Client Portal.

---

## **Key Benefits of Service Booking in the Client Portal**

Service Booking reduces the effort required to schedule services while keeping booking availability and portal access under business control.

- **Unified Booking Experience:** Clients can find meeting calendars and Services booking pages together under Appointments instead of using separate booking links.

- **Faster Booking:** Available client information is automatically filled in during booking, reducing repeated data entry.

- **Multiple Service Selection:** Clients can book one or multiple services in a booking session when the relevant Services settings allow it.

- **Appointment Self-Service:** Clients can reschedule or cancel eligible service appointments directly from the Client Portal.

- **Centralized Appointment Management:** Upcoming and Past views make it easier for clients to review scheduled and previous appointments.

- **Flexible Booking Visibility:** Businesses choose which Services booking pages appear in the portal rather than automatically exposing every booking page.

- **Controlled Portal Access:** App Permissions determines whether clients can access the Appointments feature.

---

## **How To Setup Service Booking in the Client Portal**

Service Booking uses two configuration controls. First, make individual Services booking pages available to clients. Then enable Appointments in Client Portal App Permissions so clients can access those pages.

### 

### **Step 1: Enable a Services Booking Page in the Client Portal**

Each booking page must be explicitly enabled before clients can discover it through the Client Portal. This lets businesses choose which services are available through this booking channel.

1. From the HighLevel **Sub-Account view**, select **Calendars** from the left navigation menu.
2. Select **Services**, then open **Booking Pages**.
3. Locate the Services booking page you want to make available and open its editor.
4. In the **Edit booking page** screen, select **Client Portal** from the left-side settings menu.
5. Under **Show in client portal**, turn on **Allow booking from client portal**.
6. Review the **Booking page name**. This name appears as the title of the booking page's tile in the Client Portal.
7. Review the **Short description**. This description appears beneath the booking page name in the Client Portal.
8. Click **Save changes**.
9. Repeat these steps for each additional Services booking page you want to display.

### 

### 

### **Step 2: Enable Appointments in Client Portal App Permissions**

The Appointments permission controls whether clients can access appointment booking and management from the Client Portal. Enable this permission in the same sub-account as the Services booking pages.

1. From the HighLevel **Sub-Account view**, select **Memberships** from the left navigation menu.
2. Select **Client Portal**.
3. Open **Settings**.
4. Select **App Permissions**.
5. Locate **Appointments** in the list of available applications.
6. Turn on **Appointments**.
7. Click **Save** to apply the setting.

**Result:** Clients using the new Client Portal UI can access Appointments and discover Services booking pages that have Client Portal booking enabled.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083623535/original/eRkD5J7mN4tF9FMDJfTJU2wcEunBCrFbkA.gif?1792397944)

---

## **How Clients Book Services**

Clients can book services through the same Appointments area used for meeting calendars. The booking catalog provides access to enabled Services booking pages, while each page determines which services are available to select.

### 

### **Step 1: Open the Booking Catalog**

Clients begin from the Client Portal rather than using an individual service booking link.

1. Sign in to the new **Client Portal**.
2. Select **Appointments** from the left navigation menu.
3. Click **Book Appointment** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the booking catalog, select **Services** to view Services booking pages. Clients can also find Services booking pages in the **All** view.
5. Find the desired booking page.
6. Click **View** on that booking page's card.

### **Step 2: Select and Review Services**

After opening a booking page, clients can choose the services they want. The available options depend on the business's service setup.

1. Select the desired service from the booking page.
2. On **Review your booking**, check the selected service, duration, and price.
3. If additional service selection is available, click **Add another service** to include another service.
4. Review the **Booking details** summary.
5. Click **Next**.

### **Step 3: Select a Date and Time**

The booking calendar presents dates and times available for the selected service. Clients use these options to choose when their appointment should take place.

1. On **Select Date & Time**, review the displayed calendar.
2. Use the month navigation arrows if you need another month.
3. Select an available date.
4. Choose a time from the available time slots.
5. Click **Select** to confirm the chosen time slot.
6. Review the date and time in the **Booking details** summary.

### **Step 4: Complete the Booking**

The remaining booking steps depend on the configured Services booking page. Available client information is automatically filled in during the booking process.

1. Review the booking information and any required form or payment details presented by the booking page.
2. Complete the required information.
3. Submit the booking using the page's final booking action.
4. Review the booking confirmation or appointment-request acknowledgment.

The confirmation screen can display the selected service, appointment date, time, duration, location, staff information, and amount.

```
Important: The example screenshot displays an appointment-request acknowledgment. Whether a booking requires manual confirmation depends on the configured Services settings.
```

---

## **View and Manage Service Appointments**

Client Portal Appointments brings meeting and service bookings together so clients can review their schedules without switching booking platforms.

### 

### **View Upcoming and Past Appointments**

The Appointments page provides a calendar and appointment list for finding bookings by date or status.

1. Sign in to the **Client Portal**.
2. Select **Appointments** from the left navigation menu.
3. Use the appointment calendar to locate a booking.
4. Select **Upcoming** to review upcoming appointments.
5. Select **Past** to review previous appointments.
6. Click **More details** on an appointment card to review available information.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083624388/original/CCGjeyYCbEblDg9deypC0PXch2f2VY26JQ.png?1792398367)

### 

### **Reschedule or Cancel an Eligible Service Appointment**

When service-booking policies permit changes, clients can manage their appointments from the Client Portal.

1. In the Client Portal, select **Appointments**.
2. Open **Upcoming**.
3. Locate the service appointment you want to manage.
4. Click **More details**.
5. If the appointment is eligible, use the available rescheduling or cancellation action.

Whether a client can complete an action depends on the cancellation and rescheduling rules configured for the service booking.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can clients book more than one service in the same booking?**

Yes. Clients can select multiple services when the Services configuration allows it. The **Allow Multiple Service Selection** setting in Services Global Settings controls this capability.

**Q: Why might a booking display an appointment-request message rather than an immediate confirmation?**

Services Global Settings includes **Auto Confirm New Appointments**. When this setting is disabled, new bookings remain unconfirmed until they are reviewed. The displayed acknowledgment also depends on the configured confirmation-page experience.

**Q: Why can't a client cancel or reschedule a service appointment?**

The business's service-booking settings control cancellation and rescheduling eligibility. These settings include whether the action is allowed and when its permitted period expires.

**Q: Are Services booking pages the same as Calendar Service Menus?**

No. This feature uses Services booking pages. The older Calendar Service Menus feature is a separate booking experience built around service calendars.

**Q: Can different Services booking pages have different Client Portal visibility settings?**

Yes. The **Allow booking from client portal** setting is configured for each booking page individually. This allows businesses to make selected booking pages available without enabling all of them.

**Q: Does disabling Appointments in Client Portal App Permissions delete existing appointments?**

No. Disabling the Appointments application removes access to that application from the Client Portal. It does not delete the underlying appointment records maintained in HighLevel.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [App Permissions in Client Portal: Enabling/Disabling Child Apps and Authentication](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002136-app-permissions-in-client-portal-enabling-disabling-a-child-app)
