title_en: Use the Companies side panel
source_md:
The redesigned side panel turns a Company into an account workspace you can act from. It brings the Company's fields, associated contacts and deals, appointments, tasks, notes, and conversations into one place, and lets you start a conversation, book or link an appointment, and manage linked records without leaving the panel. The Companies list stays open in the background.

```
Note

This feature is available only through a private beta and applies only to locations where it has been enabled.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Use a Company as an account hub](#Use-a-Company-as-an-account-hub)
- [Open a Company](#Open-a-Company)
- [Review Company details](#Review-Company-details)
- [Switch between tabs](#Switch-between-tabs)
- [Work with Conversations](#Work-with-Conversations)
- [Work with Appointments](#Work-with-Appointments)
- [Book a meeting](#Book-a-meeting)
- [Link an existing appointment](#Link-an-existing-appointment)
- [Record actions](#Record-actions)
- [Frequently asked questions](#Frequently-asked-questions)
- [Editorial checks before publication](#Editorial-checks-before-publication)

---

# **Use a Company as an account hub**

Because each tab lets you take action as well as review, the Company becomes the place your team manages the account from.

- **Account context:** Review the Company's contacts, opportunities, and other associated records in one view before a call or meeting.
- **Follow-up:** Start a conversation with a contact at the Company from Conversations, with the Company already linked.
- **Meetings:** Book a meeting from Appointments with the Company preselected, or link a booking that already exists.

---

## **Open a Company**

- Go to **Contacts → Companies**, then click a Company name.

The Company opens in the side panel. Use the arrows at the top to move to the previous or next Company in the current list. Use **Close** to return to the list.

---

## **Review Company details**

The **Details** tab shows the Company's name, associations, and fields.

- **Associations:** Review linked records grouped by relationship. Use the add control beside a relationship to open its association selector, or **View all** when shown to see more associations.
- **Search fields and folders:** Find a field or folder without scrolling through the full record.
- **Hide empty fields:** Focus on fields that have values.
- **Folders and counts:** Expand folders to find their fields and see the field count.
- **Edit fields:** Click a field value to open its editor.

**Step 1:** Go to Contacts > Companies and click a Company name.

![Step 1: Go to Contacts > Companies and click a Company name.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159009/original/pqrDwriMwCKd8QGEbWrSaqxe8Xtjy3q4bw.png?1792995605)

**Step 2:** Review associations and fields in Details. Use field search and Hide empty fields to narrow the view.

![Step 2: Review associations and fields in Details. Use field search and Hide empty fields to narrow the view.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159006/original/LSUnWhBlGNTcRjzbEj3VoBYQokVn0O6VPQ.png?1792995605)

**Step 3:** Use the icons on the right to switch tabs, such as Associations.

![Step 3: Use the icons on the right to switch tabs, such as Associations.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159007/original/MkEYCbHcHCbVTovJzidCXYdXkGFu09ONUA.png?1792995605)

**Step 4:** Open the three-dot menu to copy the record ID, view audit logs, or delete the record.

![Step 4: Open the three-dot menu to copy the record ID, view audit logs, or delete the record.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159004/original/NVvXWDvaaUHqJW13cLtgtRf8T4IzXYJgoQ.png?1792995605)

**Step 5:** Use the arrows at the top to move to the previous or next record.

![Step 5: Use the arrows at the top to move to the previous or next record.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159008/original/hHehp9IBD1yDdRJcOYUnE-giWsrc0tV5kA.png?1792995605)

---

## **Switch between tabs**

Use the icons on the right edge of the panel:

| **Tab** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- |
| Details | Review the record's fields and associations |
| Appointments | Review appointments linked to the record, book an appointment, or link an existing one |
| Associations | Open the record's associations section |
| Tasks | Open the record's tasks section |
| Notes | Open the record's notes section |
| Conversations | Review or create conversations associated with the record |

---

## **Work with Conversations**

1. Open the Company and select **Conversations**.
2. Review the conversation feed. If there are no linked conversations, the panel shows an empty state.
3. Click **Create a conversation** or **Create new conversation**.
4. Select a **Contact**. The current Company is already marked **Linked**.
5. Click **Create conversation** to continue.

The Contact is the person involved in the conversation. The linked Company gives the conversation its account context.

**Step 6:** In Conversations, click Create a conversation. The Company is already Linked. Select a Contact and continue.

![Step 6: In Conversations, click Create a conversation. The Company is already Linked. Select a Contact and continue.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159003/original/tZpZmqyVuPAeCnGAK9kT3OxE6GQIDrfPUg.png?1792995605)

---

## **Work with Appointments**

1. Open the Company and select **Appointments**.
2. Switch between **Upcoming** and **Past**.
3. Use **Search by Calendar Name** to find appointments.
4. Click **Add** to choose **Meetings**, **Services**, or **Link existing appointment**.

**Step 7:** In Appointments, click Add, then choose Meetings, Services, or Link existing appointment.

![Step 7: In Appointments, click Add, then choose Meetings, Services, or Link existing appointment.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159002/original/Kh4gtscwaNom_vN8M2dmTosv6yzE56cW5Q.png?1792995605)

---

### **Book a meeting**

1. Select **Add → Meetings**.
2. Choose the calendar, appointment details, date, time, and Contact.
3. Review **Associated objects**. The current Company is preselected.
4. Review the remaining booking details, then select **Book appointment**.

**Step 8:** When booking a meeting, open Associated objects to confirm the current Company is preselected.

![Step 8: When booking a meeting, open Associated objects to confirm the current Company is preselected.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159010/original/kymCDdOkTVUPwVjP3sPKwXbxwTG4uDaE8A.png?1792995605)

---

### **Link an existing appointment**

1. Select **Add → Link existing appointment**.
2. Search for an appointment in the current location.
3. Select **Link** beside the appointment you want associated with this Company.

**Step 9:** To use a booking that already exists, choose Link existing appointment, search, and click Link.

![Step 9: To use a booking that already exists, choose Link existing appointment, search, and click Link.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084159005/original/IpucPfQVJVGZJCR9DPwpU2SeAPV0WxCSgw.png?1792995605)

---

## **Record actions**

Open the three-dot menu at the top of the panel to access **Copy record ID**, **View audit logs**, or **Delete**.

---

## **Frequently asked questions**

**Q: Why is the Conversations tab empty?**

The selected Company has no conversations in its feed. You can start one from **Create a conversation** and choose a Contact.

**Q: Can I link an appointment that already exists?**

Yes. Open **Appointments → Add → Link existing appointment**, search, and select **Link** beside the appointment.

**Q: Why do I need to choose a Contact?**

Conversation creation requires a Contact. The current Company is linked separately to provide account context. The meeting booking form also requires a Contact.

**Q: Does this panel include Opportunity pipeline controls or a Payments tab?**

The Companies panel has six tabs: Details, Appointments, Associations, Tasks, Notes, and Conversations. Opportunity-specific pipeline controls and a Payments tab are not present in this panel.

##

title_en: Understanding LinkedIn statistics in Ad Manager
source_md:
HighLevel Ad Manager provides an integrated dashboard for tracking your **LinkedIn ad performance** alongside Meta and Google campaigns. With LinkedIn Statistics, you can monitor results at every level, from overall campaign groups to individual ads.

This guide explains **where to find LinkedIn statistics**, the **metrics available** and how to **interpret results** for Lead Generation and Website Traffic campaigns.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Where to find LinkedIn Statistics](#Where-to-find-LinkedIn-Statistics)
- [Statistics Hierarchy](#Statistics-Hierarchy)
- [Metrics Overview](#Metrics-Overview)
  - [Performance Analytics (Trends Over Time)](#Performance-Analytics-(Trends-Over-Time))
  - [Detailed Metrics Tables](#Detailed-Metrics-Tables)
- [Metrics by Objective](#Metrics-by-Objective)
  - [Lead Generation Campaigns](#Lead-Generation-Campaigns)
  - [Website Traffic Campaigns](#Website-Traffic-Campaigns)
- [How to Interpret the Data](#How-to-Interpret-the-Data)
- [Best Practices](#Best-Practices)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

## **Where to find LinkedIn Statistics**

1. Navigate to **Marketing > Ad Manager > Statistics tab**on top left.
2. From the platform dropdown, select **LinkedIn**.
3. Choose a **date range** for the performance window you want to analyze.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054820034/original/3p2xULZEygChrsWES2ONPjLD6XoHiD0I_w.png?1759148965)

---

## **Statistics Hierarchy**

HighLevel organizes LinkedIn advertising data into the following hierarchy:

- **Campaign Group** – Top-level container for related campaigns.
- **Campaign** – Contains targeting, audience, and campaign-level settings.
- **Ad** – Individual creative shown to the audience.

You can drill down through:

**Campaign Group > Campaign > Ad**

> **Note:** LinkedIn has updated its Campaign Manager terminology. In LinkedIn Campaign Manager, what HighLevel refers to as a **Campaign Group** may appear as a **Campaign**, while a HighLevel **Campaign** may correspond to a LinkedIn **Ad Set**. The underlying campaign structure remains the same.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054820181/original/Gvx5KZKVvtSBgkDrAeK0TtUyOSt6eRhiig.png?1759149014)

---

## **Metrics Overview**

The Statistics dashboard can display performance metrics across your LinkedIn campaigns, including:

- **Impressions** – Number of times your ad was displayed.
- **Clicks** – Total chargeable clicks based on the campaign objective.
- **Conversions** – Desired actions attributed to an ad after a click or impression when conversion tracking is configured.
- **Spend** – Total amount spent on the campaign.
- **Average CPC** – Average amount spent per click.
- **Average CPM** – Average amount spent per 1,000 impressions.
- **Cost per Conversion** – Average amount spent for each attributed conversion.
- **Leads** – Number of leads collected through LinkedIn Lead Gen campaigns.
- **Cost per Lead (CPL)** – Average amount spent per lead.

---

### **Performance Analytics (Trends Over Time)**

Graphs help you identify performance trends over the selected date range:

- **Impressions graph** – Shows how often your ads were displayed over time.
- **Clicks graph** – Shows changes in chargeable ad clicks.
- **Conversions graph** – Shows attributed conversion activity when conversion tracking is available.

---

### **Detailed Metrics Tables**

Each level (Group, Campaign, Ad) includes a detailed table with columns:

- **Status** : Active, Paused, In Review.
- **Spend** : Total amount spent.
- **Impressions** : Number of ad views.
- **Clicks** : Number of ad clicks.
- **CTR (Click-through Rate)** : Clicks ÷ Impressions (%).
- **CPC (Cost per Click)** : Spend ÷ Clicks.
- **C****PM (Cost per 1000 impressions)** : Spend ÷ Impressions × 1000.
- **Leads** (Lead Gen campaigns only).
- **CPL (Cost per Lead)** : Spend ÷ Leads.
- **Conversions** (Website Traffic campaigns only).
- **Cost per Conversion** : Spend ÷ Conversions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054820839/original/_2sT34q36435d1eF6nhpLsRtNfkE0ofP1A.png?1759149314)

---

## **Metrics by Objective**

### **Lead Generation Campaigns**

Lead Generation campaigns focus on measuring LinkedIn Lead Gen Form performance.

Common metrics include:

- **Leads** – Number of completed lead form submissions.
- **Cost per Lead (CPL)** – Average amount spent for each lead collected.
- **Lead Form Opens** – Number of times users opened the Lead Gen Form, when available.
- **Lead Form Completion Rate** – Percentage of opened forms that were submitted, when available.
- **Other performance metrics** – Spend, Impressions, Clicks, CTR, CPC, and CPM.

---

### **Website Traffic Campaigns**

Website Traffic campaigns are designed to drive users to an external website or landing page.

Key performance indicators can include:

- **Clicks** – Chargeable clicks generated by the campaign.
- **CTR** – Percentage of impressions that resulted in a chargeable click.
- **CPC** – Average amount spent per click.
- **Impressions** – Number of times the ads were displayed.
- **CPM** – Average cost per 1,000 impressions.
- **Spend** – Total campaign spend.

If LinkedIn conversion tracking is configured, conversion-related metrics may also be available for website actions attributed to the campaign.

---

## **How to Interpret the Data**

- **Impressions and Clicks** – Compare visibility with the number of users interacting with your ads.
- **CTR** – Helps indicate how effectively the ad creative and targeting are generating clicks.
- **CPC and CPM** – Help evaluate advertising cost efficiency across campaigns.
- **Leads and CPL** – Measure lead-generation volume and acquisition efficiency.
- **Conversions and Cost per Conversion** – Evaluate attributed website actions when conversion tracking is configured.
- **Spend** – Monitor how much of the campaign budget has been used during the selected period.

---

## **Best Practices**

- Always check **Status** : Ads in “In Review” will not deliver until LinkedIn approves.
- Use **drilldowns** to compare campaigns within the same group or ads within a campaign.
- Customize your view : Use the **Columns** button to add/remove metrics based on what matters most.
- Export reports : Click **Export** to generate spreadsheets for deeper client reporting.
- Monitor **spend pacing** : Ensure budgets are aligned with campaign goals.
- Compare objectives : CPL for Lead Gen vs. Cost per Conversion for Traffic campaigns.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q. Why are my LinkedIn statistics not showing any data?**

Statistics may not appear if the campaign has not started delivering, the selected date range does not contain campaign activity, or no reportable activity has occurred yet. Verify the selected date range and campaign status before reviewing the statistics.

**Q. What is the difference between impressions and clicks?**

Impressions measure how many times your ad was displayed, while Clicks represent chargeable clicks based on the campaign objective. A single user may generate multiple impressions.

**Q. Why don't I see conversion metrics for my LinkedIn campaign?**

Conversion metrics depend on conversion tracking being properly configured and the campaign generating attributable conversion activity. If conversion tracking is not configured or no conversions have been attributed during the selected period, conversion data may not be available.

**Q. What is the difference between CPC, CPM, and CPL?**

- CPC (Cost per Click) measures the average amount spent for each click.
- CPM (Cost per 1,000 Impressions) measures the average cost of 1,000 ad impressions.
- CPL (Cost per Lead) measures the average amount spent for each lead generated.

The metrics you prioritize should depend on the objective of your campaign.

**Q. Why does the campaign terminology in HighLevel differ from LinkedIn Campaign Manager?**

HighLevel currently organizes LinkedIn advertising data using Campaign Group > Campaign > Ad. LinkedIn has updated its Campaign Manager terminology so that a Campaign Group may appear as a Campaign, while what HighLevel calls a Campaign may appear as an Ad Set in LinkedIn. The underlying hierarchy remains comparable even though the terminology differs.

title_en: Error 30034: Linking a Phone Number to an Approved A2P Campaign
source_md:
After your A2P brand and campaign are approved, each applicable phone number must be associated with the approved campaign before it can use the registered messaging route. Linking the number helps ensure compliant SMS and MMS delivery through a 10-digit local number. This process is also useful when you purchase an additional number or encounter SMS error **30034**. 

```
Important: You must have successfully completed the A2P Brand and Campaign submission process before linking a number to a campaign. For more details on how to submit a campaign, see What is A2P 10DLC
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is A2P Campaign Linking?](#What-Is-A2P-Campaign-Linking?)
- [Requirements Before Linking a Phone Number](#Requirements-Before-Linking-a-Phone-Number)
- [How to Link a Phone Number to an Approved A2P Campaign](#How-to-Link-a-Phone-Number-to-an-Approved-A2P-Campaign)
- [Troubleshooting Error 30034](#Troubleshooting-Error-30034)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is Linking Phone Number to A2P Campaign?**

A2P campaign linking associates a specific phone number with an approved A2P 10DLC campaign. This connection tells carriers which registered business and messaging use case apply to messages sent from that number.

A phone number may be available in HighLevel without being linked to your approved campaign. When the association is complete, the number displays an **A2P Verified** label on the Phone Numbers page as shown in the screenshot below.

A2P 10DLC registration applies to business messaging through applicable US 10-digit local numbers. Toll-free phone numbers do not use A2P campaign linking and follow a separate verification process.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077278498/original/TwrMJuVV-lSRnRCDEm9UOZ47RHbAC4a7ZQ.png?1785434394)

---

## **Requirements Before Linking a Phone Number**

Campaign linking is available after the required registration steps have been completed. Confirming these prerequisites prevents you from attempting to link a number to a campaign that is not ready or not eligible for the number setup.

Before continuing, verify that:

- Your A2P brand has been approved.
- Your A2P campaign has been approved.
- The phone number is an applicable 10-digit local number.

Need help registering your A2P brand or campaign? See [What is A2P 10 DLC: Brand and Campaign Registration](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002380)

```
Important: Sole Proprietor brands are limited to 1 campaign and 1 phone number per campaign. If a Sole Proprietor sub-account has two or more local numbers, SMS error 30034 may occur even when one number was previously approved. Check the registration type in Settings > Phone System > Trust Center before linking additional local numbers.
```

---

## **How to Link a Phone Number to an Approved A2P Campaign**

Properly linking the number completes the association between the sending number and its approved campaign. Repeat these steps for each additional applicable number that needs to use the campaign.

1. Go to **Settings > Phone System > Phone Numbers**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077278718/original/OKpUHwnT99VG2E3Tcn5iguO7NHMxz1e5ig.png?1785434552)
2. Locate the phone number that you would like to link to an A2P campaign and select the **three-dot menu** on the right side of that number.  
     
   If this number is not yet added to an A2P campaign, it will not have the green**A2P Verified** badge.  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077278839/original/9hWo3EXucMiJmdxZUTeqdUcR9A-4-SQFHg.png?1785434689)**
3. Click on **Select A2P campaign to Link**.  
     
   If this option is not available, check that your A2P Brand and Campaign have been approved. If they have not been approved, this option will not show.  
     

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077275509/original/wY1rSPbGXUJzsKys4Sz7PWchZKCm6BRaWA.png?1785431513)
4. Select the campaign that should be associated with the number.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077278792/original/0TgMmp0Eiy34hQ84mwnFxzinlljjAgUSnQ.png?1785434629)
5. Return to the Phone Numbers list and confirm that the green **A2P Verified** label appears beneath the number.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077278820/original/8TFxBCaFoc9c2JajByNnL7c8BZEPKiBjVg.png?1785434663)

---

## **Troubleshooting Error 30034**

Error **30034** can occur when the sending number is not linked to a valid, approved A2P campaign. It can also occur when a **Sole Proprietor** registration has more than one local number, because Sole Proprietor registrations only support one local number per campaign.

Before escalating or re-registering the campaign, check the following:

- Go to **Settings > Phone System > Phone Numbers**and locate the sending number. Confirm whether the number displays the green **A2P Verified** label. If the label is missing, use the steps above to link the number to the correct approved A2P campaign.
- Go to **Settings > Phone System > Trust Center > Brands and Campaigns**. Confirm whether the account is registered as **Standard** or **Sole Proprietor**. If the account is **Sole Proprietor**, confirm that only one local number is being used. If there is more than one local number in a Sole Proprietor account, reduce the setup to one local number or review whether the business should complete Standard registration instead.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does campaign approval automatically link every phone number?**  
No. Check each applicable number on the Phone Numbers page. A linked number displays the green **A2P Verified** label.

**Q: Can I link an additional phone number after my campaign is approved?**  
Yes, when the registration type supports additional local numbers. Sole Proprietor registrations are limited to 1 campaign and 1 phone number per campaign.

**Q: How can I tell whether a number is already linked?**  
Look for the green **A2P Verified** label beneath the number in **Settings > Phone System > Phone Numbers**.

**Q: How can I tell whether the account uses Standard or Sole Proprietor A2P registration?**  
Open **Settings > Phone System > Trust Center > Brands and Campaigns** and review the registered brand type.

**Q: Why is the approved phone number also getting error 30034?**  
Error 30034 can occur when the sending number is not linked to a valid approved A2P campaign. First, check whether the number displays **A2P Verified** in **Settings > Phone System > Phone Numbers** and link it to the correct campaign if needed. If the account uses Sole Proprietor registration, error 30034 can also occur when the account has multiple local numbers, because Sole Proprietor registrations only support one local number per campaign.

**Q: Why does my number not display A2P Verified after purchase?**  
The number may not yet be associated with an approved campaign. Use the three-dot menu to check whether a campaign can be selected. Before linking, confirm whether the account uses Standard or Sole Proprietor registration.

**Q: Can a toll-free number be linked to an A2P campaign?**  
No. Toll-free numbers use a separate verification process and do not use A2P 10DLC campaign linking.

**Q: Why don't I see the "Select A2P campaign to Link" option?**

The option will not appear if your A2P Brand and Campaign have not been approved. You must successfully complete the A2P registration and approval process before you can link a phone number to a campaign.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [What is A2P 10 DLC: Brand and Campaign Registration](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002380)
- [A2P Campaign Registration: Step by Step Guide and FAQs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004539)
- [Registering Your A2P Brand](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008140)
- [LC Phone System - Error Code and Warning Dictionary](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005526)

title_en: Notion Integration with HighLevel
source_md:
Effortlessly push and pull data between HighLevel and Notion—no Zapier or webhooks required. This guide shows you how the new native Notion Integration unlocks automated page creation, database updates, comments, and more, all from inside Workflows.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Notion Integration with HighLevel?](#What-is-Notion-Integration-with-HighLevel?)
- [Key Benefits of Notion Integration](#Key-Benefits-of-Notion-Integration)
- [Triggers: Triggers (Notion → HighLevel)](#Triggers%3A-Triggers-(Notion-%E2%86%92-HighLevel))
- [Actions (HighLevel → Notion)](#Actions-(HighLevel-%E2%86%92-Notion))
- [Getting Started with Notion](#Getting-Started-with-Notion)
- [How Notion Triggers Work](#How-Notion-Triggers-Work)
- [Use Case 1: Create Notion Docs from Form Submissions](#Use-Case-1%3A-Create-Notion-Docs-from-Form-Submissions)
- [Use Case 2: Sync Appointment Outcomes to Notion Logs](#Use-Case-2%3A-Sync-Appointment-Outcomes-to-Notion-Logs)
- [Use Case 3: Auto-Generate Proposal Pages](#Use-Case-3%3A-Auto-Generate-Proposal-Pages)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

## **What is Notion Integration with HighLevel?**

The Notion integration in HighLevel enables seamless automation between your CRM workflows and Notion’s powerful workspace platform. Whether you’re managing internal documentation, client portals, or dynamic project wikis, this integration allows you to trigger workflows or automate Notion actions — reducing manual effort and enhancing visibility across your tools.

**Why It Matters:**

With this integration, agencies, marketers, and small businesses can:

- Automatically sync customer data into Notion databases
- Create tasks, notes, or updates based on CRM events
- Build live, CRM-powered knowledge bases and content repositories

---

## **Key Benefits of Notion Integration**

- Replace Zapier/n8n stacks with one native connection, cutting subscription costs.
- Sync onboarding forms, appointment results, or pipeline changes directly into structured Notion databases.
- Auto-generate project wikis, proposals, or SOP pages the moment deals advance.
- Two-way communication: trigger workflows from Notion edits or drive Notion updates from HighLevel actions.
- Five-minute polling keeps Notion-originated triggers responsive without overloading your workspace.

---

## **Triggers: Triggers (Notion → HighLevel)**

These are events in Notion that can initiate workflows in HighLevel:

| **Trigger Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| New Database Item | Fires when a new item is added to a Notion database |
| Updated Database Item | Fires when an existing item is modified |
| Updated Page | Fires when a Notion page is updated |

```
Note: All triggers rely on polling. HighLevel checks Notion every ~5 minutes for changes and processes new data accordingly.
```

---

## **Actions (HighLevel → Notion)**

These are actions HighLevel can execute in Notion through workflows:

| **Action Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Archive Database Item | Archives a selected database item in Notion |
| Create Database Item | Adds a new item to a chosen database |
| Add Content to Page | Appends content to an existing Notion page |
| Update Database Item | Updates the fields of an existing database item |
| Retrieve a Page | Fetches a Notion page and its metadata |
| Retrieve Block Children | Retrieves child blocks under a Notion block (e.g., text, to-do, toggle) |
| Find Database Item | Locates a specific database item using filters |
| Get Page and Children | Retrieves a page along with all nested blocks |
| Find or Create Database Item | Finds an item or creates it if it doesn’t exist |
| Add Comment | Posts a comment on a Notion page |
| Create Page | Creates a new Notion page |
| Restore Database Item | Reactivates a previously archived item |
| Retrieve Database | Fetches metadata and schema for a database |
| Get Page Comments | Retrieves all comments from a Notion page |
| Find Page (By Title) | Searches for a page using its title |
| Find or Create Comment | Finds or creates a comment based on the uniqueness criteria |

---

## **Getting Started with Notion**

1. **Search in Workflows:** Open your HighLevel workflow builder and search for any Notion actions or triggers you’d like to add.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056474481/original/YJWATrZ5sI3mPaZLjA9b3DsESVv1tGdmpQ.png?1761050196)

2.**Connect Your Account:** If your Notion account is already connected, you’ll see configuration options immediately. If not, click Connect Now and complete the Notion authorization flow (via OAuth).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056474590/original/niyMn41_njkwYAqu7XvEvk1NJXXziGoCiw.png?1761050242)

3. **Alternative Method:** Navigate to Settings → Integrations. Find Notion and connect your workspace.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056474751/original/BwPIiu2jNYvGNg_Z4h0BwdDROD19-AXLJQ.png?1761050296)

```
Once connected, you can create, update, and sync pages or database items directly from your workflows.
```

---

## **How Notion Triggers Work**

Notion triggers are powered by polling. Every 5 minutes, HighLevel sends a request to Notion to check for any changes. If it detects a qualifying event (e.g., new database item or an updated page), it triggers your workflow.

**Setup Instructions:**

1. Choose a trigger (e.g., New Database Item).
2. Name your trigger and click **Test Trigger**.
3. HighLevel will retrieve metadata from Notion to enable dynamic field mapping in downstream actions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155050793646/original/ESjlqD-tOXkp8e52BwYogRao7GcA1l5DBQ.png?1754048482)

---

## **Use Case 1: Create Notion Docs from Form Submissions**

**Goal:** Capture form submissions in Notion for project tracking or onboarding.

**Workflow Setup:**

- **Trigger:** Form Submitted
- **Filter:** Form Name = “Onboarding Form”
- **Actions:**

  - Create Database Item (Notion)
  - Add Comment (Notion)

**Example:**A client submits the onboarding form → A new entry is created in the “Client Onboarding DB” in Notion → A welcome message is added as a comment.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155050793594/original/THKmE-hrxiDflYuACRcvQhgGsHYyD81p4w.png?1754048433)

---

## **Use Case 2: Sync Appointment Outcomes to Notion Logs**

**Goal:** Maintain an auditable meeting log in Notion.

**Workflow Setup:**

- **Trigger:** Appointment Status Changed
- **Filter:** Calendar = “Consultations”
- **Actions:**

  - Update Database Item (Notion)
  - Add Content to Page (Notion)

**Example:**A lead misses their consultation → The relevant database item is updated → Follow-up notes are appended to the page.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155050793681/original/exMQB5rrG9UO5KoNDNEeQQJOcQnzbMCe4A.png?1754048511)

---

## **Use Case 3: Auto-Generate Proposal Pages**

**Goal:** Create personalized proposal pages when an opportunity advances.

**Workflow Setup:**

- **Trigger:** Pipeline Stage Changed
- **Filter:** Status = “won”
- **Actions:**

  - Create Page (Notion)
  - Add Content to Page
  - Add Comment

**Example:**A deal moves to the “Proposal” stage → A Notion page titled “Proposal for {{contact.name}}” is created with summary content and team mentions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155050793722/original/pcgqbIB1mwtgJbJ-mymiJQEtWd_yIuaEYw.png?1754048551)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need a paid Notion plan to use this integration?**  
No, the integration works with Notion’s free plans. However, some features like teamspaces or analytics may require a paid subscription.

**Q: Are there limits on the number of workflows with Notion?**  
Workflow limits are based on your HighLevel plan. The integration also respects Notion’s official API rate limits.

**Q: How often does HighLevel check Notion for trigger updates?**

Every five minutes.

**Q: Will existing webhooks break after switching to the native integration?**

No. You can run webhooks and the native integration side by side while you migrate.

title_en: Router Action
source_md:
## Table of Contents

1. Overview
2. Key Benefits
3. Action Name
4. Action Description
5. Action Details
6. How to Configure
7. Behaviour and Logic
8. Testing the Router
9. Use Case
10. FAQs

## Overview

The Router action sends a contact down every branch whose conditions match. The branches run one after another, from left to right. Use it when one contact can qualify for more than one path, such as a form lead who picks several services at once.

Router belongs to the same family as If/Else. The difference is how many branches run. If/Else sends the contact into the first branch that matches and ignores the other branches, even when the contact matches them too. Router checks every branch and runs each one that matches.

## Key Benefits

- **Every match runs:**a contact who matches three branches goes into all three, not only the first one.
- **Predictable order:**branches run from left to right, and you can drag them into the order you need.
- **Three branch types:**use Custom rules, Always run or Fallback to decide when each branch runs.
- **Familiar conditions:**build each rule with fields, operators, conditions and rule groups.
- **Fewer duplicate workflows:**one Router replaces extra branches or workflows that you built to catch a second or third match.
- **Clear test results:**the test output shows which branch conditions passed and why.

## Action Name

Router

## Action Description

Send the contact down every branch whose conditions match. Branches run one after another, left to right.

## Action Details

| Field | Description | Mandatory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Action Name** | The name shown on the workflow canvas. Defaults to “Router”. | Yes |
| **Branches** | The list of branches in this Router, in run order. Use Add branch to add a branch, the drag handle to change the order, and the delete icon to remove a branch. | Yes |
| **Branch Name** | The name of the branch, for example “Branch 1”. It shows on the canvas above the branch. | Yes |
| **Branch Type** | Custom rules: runs only when the conditions below match. Always run: runs for every contact, with no conditions. Fallback: runs only when no other path matched. | Yes |
| **Only Continue If** | Shown for Custom rules. The conditions the contact must match. Select a field, select an operator and enter a value. Use Add condition and Add rule group for more conditions. | Yes, for Custom rules |

## How to Configure

The steps below follow the most common journey: a trigger brings in a contact, and the Router sends that contact into each branch it matches.

### Step 1: Add the Router action

In the workflow builder, click the + icon where the Router should go. In the Actions panel, search for Router and select it. The Router appears on the canvas with its branches below it.

### Step 2: Open a branch

In the Router panel, the Branches list shows every branch. Click a branch to open its settings. Enter a Branch Name. Click Back to branches to return to the list.

### Step 3: Choose the Branch Type

Open the Branch Type dropdown and select one option:

- **Custom rules:**the branch runs only when the conditions below match.
- **Always run:**the branch runs for every contact, with no conditions.
- **Fallback:**the branch runs only when no other path matched.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084503340/original/DAFc2bwWdBxiiTjCvoZ6pqAPREp5GygFhA.gif?1793276740)

*Selecting the Router action, choosing the Branch Type and setting a condition.*

### Step 4: Set the conditions

For Custom rules, build the rule under Only Continue If. Select a field, for example a contact field or a custom field. Select an operator, such as is, is not, contains, does not contain, is any of (comma separated), is none of (comma separated) or is not empty. Enter the value. Click Add condition or Add rule group to add more conditions. Save the branch.

### Step 5: Add more branches

Click + Add branch on the canvas, or Add branch in the Branches list. Set the Branch Name, the Branch Type and the conditions for each new branch. Add as many branches as your use case needs.

### Step 6: Set the run order

Branches run from left to right. To make a branch run first, drag it by its handle to the top of the Branches list. The canvas updates to show the new order.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084503413/original/nSjfIsnZFa2xa8bVj3bWuyQ0nDL6cNhrSA.gif?1793276782)

*Dragging Branch 2 above Branch 1. Branch 2 now runs first.*

### Step 7: Save and add the next steps

Click Save action. Then click the + icon under each branch and add the actions that branch should run, such as a note, an internal notification, a tag or a task.

## Behaviour and Logic

| Rule | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Which branches run** | Every branch whose conditions match runs. A contact who matches three branches goes into all three. |
| **Run order** | Matching branches run one after another, from left to right. The order in the Branches list is the run order. |
| **Custom rules** | The branch runs only when the contact matches its conditions. |
| **Always run** | The branch runs for every contact, with no conditions. |
| **Fallback** | The branch runs only when no other path matched. |
| **Compared with If/Else** | If/Else runs only the first branch that matches. Router runs every branch that matches. |

## Testing the Router

Use Test workflow to check the Router on a real event before you publish.

- **Input:**open the Router step and the Test tab. The Input lists each branch condition and its rule, for example Branch 1 · condition 1.
- **Run the test:**select a real event, such as a recent Form Submitted event, and run the test for the Router action.
- **Output:**the Action tested banner confirms the run. The Output lists each branch condition with Passed and the reason, including the actual value the contact had. For example: Passed, includes HVAC (actual: HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084503480/original/A6BOrMg7qZH2lFQbSKXux4MGFyU02OKXIA.gif?1793276814)

*The test output shows Branch 1, Branch 2 and Branch 3 passed, each with its reason.*

## Use Case

Scenario: a home services business asks one question on its form: “What service do you need?” The lead can select more than one option: HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical or Carpentry. Each service has its own team and its own follow up steps.

- **Trigger:**Form Submitted, for the home services form.
- **Action:**Router with four branches.
- **Branch 1:**Custom rules. The service includes HVAC.
- **Branch 2:**Custom rules. The service includes Plumbing.
- **Branch 3:**Custom rules. The service includes Electrical.
- **Branch 4:**Fallback, for leads that match no other branch.
- **Inside each branch:**the next steps for that team, such as a note, an internal notification, a tag or a task.
- **Result:**a lead who selects HVAC, Plumbing and Electrical goes into Branch 1, Branch 2 and Branch 3, in that order. With If/Else, only the HVAC branch would run.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084503431/original/k9bRvGGnjuw74jCjbslvU4gCWq-AV9RlxQ.gif?1793276797)

*The form question with multiple selections, and the Router branches for each service.*

## FAQs

**Q: What is the difference between Router and If/Else?**

If/Else sends the contact into the first branch that matches and ignores the rest. Router sends the contact into every branch that matches, one after another, from left to right.

**Q: In what order do the branches run?**

From left to right, in the order of the Branches list. Drag a branch to the top of the list to make it run first.

**Q: Do the matching branches run at the same time?**

No. They run one after another.

**Q: How do I make a branch run for every contact?**

Set its Branch Type to Always run. It runs for every contact, with no conditions.

**Q: How do I handle contacts that match no branch?**

Add a branch with the Branch Type set to Fallback. It runs only when no other path matched.

**Q: How can I check which branches a contact will go into?**

Test the Router with Test workflow on a real event. The Output lists each branch condition with Passed and the reason.

title_en: Getting Started with Coupons
source_md:
## [동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/JIvQuxqM3v8?&wmode=opaque)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Coupons?](#What-is-Coupons?)
- [How to Create a Coupon](#How%C2%A0to%C2%A0Create%C2%A0a%C2%A0Coupon)
- [How Coupons Work at Checkout](#How%C2%A0Coupons%C2%A0Work%C2%A0at%C2%A0Checkout)
- [Important Behaviors & Limitations](#Important%C2%A0Behaviors-&%C2%A0Limitations)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

# **What is Coupons?**

Coupons help you offer discounts on your products and increase conversions across your checkouts. You can create coupons that apply to one-time and recurring products and control how, where, and how often they can be used.

Coupons allow you to:

- Offer **percentage or fixed discounts**
- Apply discounts on **entire carts or specific products**
- Control usage through limits and restrictions
- Apply discounts on **subscriptions (with duration controls)**
- Track usage and redemption

Coupons can be used across:

- Events (Events can use existing coupons created under Payments → Coupons. Events also support event-specific coupons created from within an individual event)
- Funnels (Order Forms)
- Stores
- Websites
- Payment Links
- Calendars
- Services
- Gift Card Sell Page
- Business Facing - Create Subscription

```
Coupons are not supported on Estimates and Invoices. Certain types of coupon settings are not supported for subscription payments made with PayPal.
```

---

## **How to Create a Coupon**

### **Step 1: Navigate to Coupons**

Go to**Payments → Coupons → Create Coupon**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067095692/original/bXahrvIuWIAvgNTrKzos4JrrvBDe-9cLFw.png?1773739904)**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067274628/original/JkrjdFQtc4tIxL3Rnnt7W-X79xocw9fYFA.png?1773901987)**

### **Step 2: Enter Basic Details**

#### 

#### **Coupon Name**

- Internal reference for your coupon
- Example: `SUMMER SALE 2025`

#### 

#### **Coupon Code**

- The code customers will enter at checkout
- Must be:

  - Alphanumeric only
  - No spaces or special characters
  - Case-insensitive (automatically converted to uppercase)
- You can also click **Generate** to auto-create a code

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298017/original/jqwGXNit07EQDY8NMffBuG4sCCftLNnu9Q.png?1773919127)

### **Step 3: Select Coupon Type**

You can choose between two types:

#### **1. Percentage-Based Coupon**

- Applies a percentage discount on the total value
- Example:

  - Cart = $100
  - Coupon = 25%
  - Final = $75

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298055/original/kYtJhdCVYauIBfmA1zyuzVSrxUYWbC9ELw.png?1773919160)

#### **2. Fixed Amount Coupon**

- Applies a fixed discount regardless of order size
- Example:

  - Cart = $100
  - Coupon = $25
  - Final = $75

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298093/original/36kr_pbEV_6P6fcQaSZQLfPsh137mTXx1g.png?1773919196)

## 

### **Coupon Currency**

- Coupon currency is **automatically set** to your **sub-account currency**
- It **cannot be changed manually**

## 

### **Step 4: Set Validity (Optional)**

You can define when the coupon is usable:

- **Start Date & Time** → When the coupon becomes active
- **End Date & Time** → When the coupon expires

If no end date is set → coupon remains active indefinitely

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298143/original/-nlSVBYAQMFWsJRrktsurBBaUzE9ICniew.png?1773919223)

### **Step 5: Configure Usage Restrictions**

You can apply the following controls:

#### **1. Limit Total Redemptions**

- #### Restrict how many times the coupon can be used
- Example: Limit to 100 uses

#### **2. Limit to Selected Products**

- #### Restrict coupon usage to specific products
- Example:

  - Coupon works only for “Premium Plan”
  - Cannot be used on other products
- Coupons can also be restricted to certain prices and variants instead of all under a product.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067297860/original/rpJemNEmBQm5_GgtsWaZrEn5Ls87WvxjFg.png?1773918991)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067297906/original/-SC0iex1rPRmyAEGlC-mW7aHHqXxtprvpg.png?1773919028)

#### **3. Limit to One Use per Customer**

- #### Prevent a single customer from reusing the coupon

### **Step 6: Configure Subscription Behavior (If Applicable)**

For recurring products, you can control how long the discount applies:

#### **Apply to Future Payments**

You can choose:

- **Forever**  
  → Discount applies to every billing cycle
- **Multiple Months**  
  → Discount applies for a fixed duration

Example:

- Subscription = $100/month
- Coupon = 20% for 3 months
- Customer pays $80/month for first 3 months
- Then returns to $100/month

Note: This applies regardless of billing frequency

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298181/original/cucHH0eRoLNkVRF2swJ0Z7MZAXMhjwVhOQ.png?1773919266)

### **Step 7: Create the Coupon**

Click **Create**

Your coupon is now active (or scheduled based on your settings).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155067298370/original/ikZsXZqCY4m9GcSLvV78rakbyCYpiTjp0Q.png?1773919338)

---

## **How Coupons Work at Checkout**

- Coupon input field appears **only when a valid coupon exists**
- If no applicable coupon → field is hidden automatically
- Discounts are:

  - Shown in checkout summary
  - Applied across applicable products proportionally
  - Visible in order details
- Many checkouts (Funnels, Payment Links, etc.) have an option on the builder to enable or disable visibility and application of coupons during checkout

---

## **Important Behaviors & Limitations**

- Coupons apply to:

  - One-time products
  - Recurring products
- Coupons do **not apply to one-click upsells**(in case of Funnels)
- Coupons can reduce cart value to **$0**

  - Customer still needs to enter card details for verification, if builder level setting for this is checked. If builder doesn't have setting for managing $0 transactions, card details are always required.
- 100% discounts support via most providers except PayPal.
- Coupon codes are:

  - Case-insensitive
  - Unique
- Discounts are distributed proportionally across products

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I create a free product using coupons?**

Yes,use a 100% discount coupon

**Q: Can I edit or delete coupons later?**

Yes — you can edit, delete, or view usage history anytime

**Q: Can a coupon be applied to both one-time and subscription products in the same order?**

Yes. Coupons apply to both one-time and recurring products within the same order. For subscriptions, the coupon behavior will follow the configured duration (e.g., one-time, multiple months, or forever).

**Q: What happens if a coupon is applied to a product with multiple quantities?**

The discount is calculated based on the total value of that product (quantity × price). For example, if a product costs $20 and a customer buys 5 units with a 10% coupon, the discount applied will be $10 (10% of $100).

**Q: Can I change a coupon after it has already been used?**

You can edit certain coupon settings (like name, limits, or validity), but changes will only apply to future uses. Past orders where the coupon was already applied will remain unchanged.

**Q: Does the coupon apply on Set-up Fees?**

Yes. Coupon applies on set-up fees in case of subscription products.

**Q: Which coupon configurations are not supported with PayPal?**

The following configurations are not supported with PayPal:  
1. Subscription setting with defined number of months instead of 'Forever' does not work with PayPal. It would charge for the entire duration of the subscription rather than the defined months.

2. A coupon that changes the order value to $0 i.e. it's a 100% OFF coupon or an amount based coupon that makes the final order to be $0, doesn't work with PayPal if subscription products are part of the checkout.

title_en: Introducing the All-New GoKollab Discover
source_md:
GoKollab Discover gives knowledge creators a refreshed way to showcase courses and communities and connect with new audiences. The redesigned experience introduces curated discovery sections, smarter ranking, dedicated sales pages, unified creator profiles, and a modern responsive interface. This guide explains what GoKollab Discover is, how content is surfaced, and how creators can make Membership courses available in the GoKollab Marketplace.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is GoKollab Discover?](#what-is-gokollab-discover)
- [Key Benefits of GoKollab Discover](#key-benefits)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#prerequisites-limitations)
- [How To Setup GoKollab Discover](#setup-gokollab-discover)
- [How Discovery Works in GoKollab](#how-discovery-works)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

# **What is GoKollab Discover?**

GoKollab Discover is a redesigned discovery experience that helps people find courses, communities, and creators across GoKollab. It brings together curated content sections, ranking signals, dedicated sales pages, and creator profiles to make relevant offerings easier to explore.

Top, Popular, and Featured sections surface courses and communities category by category. GoKollab also uses engagement, growth, quality, and traction as signals when ranking creator offerings.

---

## **Key Benefits of GoKollab Discover**

GoKollab Discover gives creators more ways to present their work while helping potential learners find relevant courses and communities.

- **Increased visibility:** Top, Popular, and Featured sections provide additional opportunities for courses and communities to be discovered.
- **Smarter discovery:** GoKollab uses engagement, growth, quality, and traction as signals when ranking creator offerings.
- **Dedicated sales pages:** Courses and communities have dedicated landing pages that present the offering and support enrollment.
- **Unified creator profiles:** Visitors can explore a creator's offerings from one profile and learn more about their content.
- **Category-based discovery:** Courses and communities can be surfaced by category, helping visitors find content relevant to their interests.
- **Modern responsive experience:** The refreshed GoKollab interface provides a polished experience across supported screen sizes.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Understanding how GoKollab discovery works helps creators prepare their content while avoiding assumptions about ranking or placement.

**For Membership courses:**

- The course must exist in the applicable HighLevel sub-account.
- A course must be listed in the GoKollab Marketplace to make it publicly discoverable there.
- Clear course titles, descriptions, and About content help GoKollab assign an appropriate category through Smart Categorization.

**Keep these current limitations in mind:**

- GoKollab does not document the weighting or calculation behind its Discover ranking system.
- The confirmed ranking signals are engagement, growth, quality, and traction.
- The release does not document a way to manually place an offering in the Top, Popular, or Featured sections.
- Rankings are described as receiving regular updates, but a specific update schedule is not provided.

---

## **How To Setup GoKollab Discover**

For Membership courses, HighLevel's documented marketplace workflow lets creators publish eligible courses to the GoKollab Marketplace for public discovery.

### **List a Membership Course in the GoKollab Marketplace**

Follow the complete path from your HighLevel sub-account to publish a Membership course in GoKollab.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082800177/original/ZbxaMD9F5Umf1s-ttpSeltaEaWnRdpnEEw.png?1791428395)

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, select **Membership** in the left menu.
2. Select **Gokollab Marketplace**.
3. Select the **Courses** tab.
4. Click **+ Add Course**.
5. Open the course dropdown and select the course you want to list.
6. Select the applicable **Pricing Model**.
7. Enter the pricing details required for the selected model.
8. Click **Add Course** to publish the course to the GoKollab Marketplace.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082778413/original/bsmhKjjCSH-rAEzMRVyRfBX0dwvQhsm2ZA.png?1791389907)

After a course is listed, you can return to **Membership → Gokollab Marketplace → Courses** to manage whether it remains listed in the marketplace.

### **Optimize Content for Smart Categorization**

GoKollab uses Smart Categorization to automatically assign courses and communities to relevant categories. Clear product information helps the system understand where an offering belongs.

To support accurate categorization:

- Use a specific title that clearly describes the topic.
- Write a focused description that explains the purpose and audience.
- Keep the **About** content relevant to the course or community.
- Update this information when the focus of the offering changes.

---

## **How Discovery Works in GoKollab**

GoKollab combines curated sections, ranking signals, categories, sales pages, and creator information to help visitors evaluate relevant courses and communities.

### **Top, Popular, and Featured Sections**

Top, Popular, and Featured sections provide curated ways to explore GoKollab content. Courses and communities can be surfaced category by category, helping visitors find relevant offerings faster.

The release does not document a manual placement process for these sections. Placement is connected to GoKollab's discovery and ranking experience.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082800189/original/CvkkCWihbyspp0U8QS0cGZYM-Fneje8g3Q.png?1791428437)

### **Smart Ranking**

GoKollab's ranking system uses engagement, growth, quality, and traction as signals to determine how creator offerings are surfaced.

Rankings receive regular updates so discovery can reflect changing performance across the platform. The exact calculation, weighting, and update frequency are not documented.

### **Sales Pages and Creator Profiles**

Dedicated sales pages help visitors understand a course or community before enrolling. Each offering can present its value through a focused landing-page experience.

Creator profiles bring a creator's portfolio together in one place. Visitors can explore available offerings, learn more about the creator, and continue into relevant content.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What determines ranking in GoKollab Discover?**

A: GoKollab identifies engagement, growth, quality, and traction as ranking signals. The exact formula and weighting are not documented.

**Q: How often are GoKollab Discover rankings updated?**

A: Rankings receive regular updates. A specific refresh schedule is not documented.

**Q: Can I manually place my course or community in the Top, Popular, or Featured sections?**

A: The release does not document a manual placement process for these sections.

**Q: Does GoKollab Discover support free and paid offerings?**

A: Yes. The GoKollab Discover release describes its sales-page and enrollment experience as supporting both free and paid offerings.

**Q: How do I make a Membership course discoverable through GoKollab?**

A: From the Sub-Account View, go to **Membership → Gokollab Marketplace → Courses**, click **+ Add Course**, select the course, configure its pricing, and click **Add Course**.

**Q: How are categories assigned to courses and communities?**

A: GoKollab uses Smart Categorization to analyze the title, description, and About content and automatically assign a relevant category.

---

### **Related Articles**

- **[Integration of Membership Courses with GoKollab](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005165)**
- **[How To Use Smart Categories on GoKollab](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005688)**
- **[Manage Your Communities and Courses with GoKollab Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005899)**
- **[How to integrate Stripe with GoKollab](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004681)**

title_en: Universal Elements in the HighLevel Page Builder
source_md:
Universal Elements in HighLevel’s Page Builder let you design an element once and reuse it across Funnels, Websites, Blogs, Webinars, and Store pages—while keeping every instance consistent. This guide explains what Universal Elements are, how they differ from other saved items, and the safest way to create, place, and update them. You’ll also learn publishing best practices, rollback options, and tips for organizing your library for scale.

---

# **What are Universal Elements?**

Universal Elements are single elements you save to the Saved Assets library so they remain *linked* wherever they’re used. When a linked Universal Element is updated and published, all placed instances reflect the change, helping teams maintain brand consistency and reduce repeated edits across pages and assets.

---

## **Key Benefits of Universal Elements**

Understanding the core benefits helps you decide when Universal Elements are the right tool versus other saved item types. Focus on speed, consistency, and maintainability across your account.

- **Brand consistency:** Keep typography, colors, and styles aligned everywhere without manual updates.
- **Faster builds:** Drag from the Saved Assets library instead of redesigning common elements.
- **Centralized updates:** Edit once and publish the affected pages so all instances reflect the change.
- **Organized library:** Thumbnails and search in Saved Assets make frequently used elements easy to find.
- **Team-friendly workflows:** Standardize key components so collaborators build with approved patterns.

---

## **Universal Elements vs. Element Templates vs. Universal Sections**

HighLevel offers multiple ways to save and reuse content. Choosing the right option prevents confusion and avoids accidental design drift. Use this comparison to pick the best fit for each scenario.

| Saved type | Scope | Syncing behavior | Typical uses | Where to find |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Universal Elements** | Single element | Linked reuse; updates appear on placed instances after publishing affected pages | Buttons, logos, icons, menus | Saved Assets → **Universal Elements** |
| **Element Templates** | Single element | Inserted as a starting point (copy); later edits do **not** sync to existing placements | One-off variants, quick starting patterns | Saved Assets → **Element Templates** |
| **Universal Sections** | Section (group of elements) | Linked reuse at section level; edits can sync across placed instances after publishing | Headers, footers, announcement bars | Saved Assets → **Sections** (Universal) |

```
Tip: Use Universal Elements for small, repeating items (e.g., buttons, badges). Use Universal Sections when you need a full, reusable layout block (e.g., header/footer).
```

---

## **How To Setup Universal Elements**

Saving correctly the first time prevents rework and ensures the element is stored as a *linked*Universal Element instead of a non-syncing template.

1. Open a page in the Page Builder (Funnel, Website, Blog, Webinar, or Store).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060208344/original/6gFjDPKXGd047GR-2ccJTY5x9wMgrfeMyg.png?1765279297)
2. Select the element you want to reuse (e.g., button, image, icon, headline, or menu) and save it as a **Universal Element** from either location:

   - The element’s orange toolbar → **Save** icon  
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060249962/original/IcrWNS_DjkYfFStNMGrj4blWU92FutX9gg.gif?1765298839)
   - **Layers** panel → **⋯** menu → **Save as Universal Element**  
       
     **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060250012/original/4ezdLDN7CvJ7FwrDV9fTdL3cEOzFH15Ppg.gif?1765298876)**
3. Give the item a clear, searchable name (e.g., `Button — Primary CTA`).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060209724/original/3IYT1URUkMZ7qIHPIdcZ9jjidGD1YjEB0w.png?1765279809)
4. Confirm the save. The item now appears in **Saved Assets → Universal Elements** with a thumbnail.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060320698/original/ltWTVk6J7W6wtXg42IkFcJxrRnhRLHqkaA.png?1765372871)

---

## **Placing & Editing Universal Elements**

Place Universal Elements from the Saved Assets library to ensure each instance stays linked. When you edit a Universal Element, you’ll publish changes to make them live on the affected pages.

AI Page Revisions are designed to respect linked Universal Elements and focus changes on the targeted content. When a revision runs, use the post-revision summary to verify whether a linked element was changed.

**Best practices**

- Confirm whether your target area includes a **linked Universal Element** before running a revision.
- If you need a page-only variant, duplicate the Universal Element locally (convert to a non-linked copy) before revising.
- If a revision updates a linked element, review the change summary and publish global changes deliberately after validation.

**Place a Universal Element**

- Open **Add Elements → Saved Assets → Universal Elements**.
- Use search or browse thumbnails, then drag the element onto the canvas.

**Edit a Universal Element**

- Select a placed Universal Element to adjust design or settings.
- Save your page changes.
- **Publish** the page so updates become visible to visitors.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060321656/original/sHDh0V9FTNioEFGmiFKDSzYw2_A-8W4FOw.gif?1765373452)

---

## **Managing Saved Universal Elements**

A tidy library speeds up builds and reduces mistakes. Use clear names, search effectively, and remove unused entries when appropriate.

- **Browse & search:** **Add Elements → Saved Assets → Universal Elements** provides thumbnails and keyword search.
- **Rename for clarity:** Use consistent prefixes (e.g., `Button —`, `Icon —`, `Nav —`).
- **Remove cautiously:** Deleting a saved item detaches it from the library for future use. Review pages that currently rely on it before removing.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155060321228/original/_LsnzQW608YEoqH32qpuyYNYXhZBbH9nRw.png?1765373116)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I have to publish for changes to be visible to visitors?**  
Yes. Saving keeps edits in the builder. Publishing the affected page(s) makes updates live.

**Q: Where do I find saved Universal Elements?**  
In the Page Builder, open **Add Elements → Saved Assets → Universal Elements** to browse thumbnails or search by name.

**Q: Can I rename or delete a Universal Element later?**  
You can rename items for clarity. Deleting removes the saved item from the library for future use; review pages that currently rely on it before removing.

**Q: What if I need a one‑off variation on a single page?**  
Consider placing an **Element Template** or creating a local copy so changes don’t affect other pages.

**Q: How can I revert a recent change if something looks wrong?**  
Use **Version History** on the affected page to restore a previous version, then republish.

---

## **Related Articles**
